body: Eli Machpod delivered a dose of realism to Hapoel Petah Tikva's fanbase this week, telling ONE's studio show that he does not expect the newly promoted club to match last season's remarkable run to the top-six playoff.
"I don't think Hapoel Petah Tikva will have a season like last year," Machpod, one of the club's most decorated former players, said in the aftermath of the derby against Maccabi Petah Tikva.

Hapoel won that match 1-0 at HaMoshava Stadium in the opening round of the Toto Cup, with Noam Cohen settling a scrappy occasion with a goal in the 89th minute. Machpod was unimpressed by the overall quality, dismissing it as a below-average contest.

His skepticism about the season ahead stems largely from the scale of turnover in the squad that Omer Peretz guided from the second tier to a top-six finish - the club's first appearance in the upper playoff in more than two decades.

Several contributors from that campaign have already left, and Machpod pointed to the club's financial reality as the reason further departures are likely. "There's no money, so there's nothing to do," he said. "If a suitable offer comes for players, they'll be sold."

That comment lands against a backdrop of reports that Hapoel Petah Tikva are pushing for a higher transfer offer for Zambian winger Chapyuka Songa, one of the more coveted names to emerge from last season's promotion push.

In their place, the club have brought in fresh faces at the back. Left-back Yazan Nassar, a summer signing from Hapoel Tel Aviv, and defender Avishai Cohen were both handed derby debuts, alongside winger Guy Badash.

Machpod's forecast for the coming campaign has Hapoel Petah Tikva locked in a battle for sixth place with Maccabi Netanya, rather than another surprise push toward the top of the table. He was harsher still on the cross-town rivals, predicting Maccabi Petah Tikva will instead be fighting to avoid relegation.

None of this reflects any lack of faith in Peretz himself. The 40-year-old, who has overseen the club's rise since arriving before last season, signed a contract extension through 2027/28 in the close season, with his salary reported to have risen by roughly a third.
For a club still adjusting to life back in the Israeli top flight, the message from one of its own icons is clear: last season's overachievement was the exception, not the new baseline.

title: Barcola turns down new PSG deal, opening the door for Liverpool
dek: The France winger has stopped contract talks with the reigning European champions after growing frustrated with his role under Luis Enrique, and Liverpool are being given priority if a fee can be agreed.

verificationSources.label: ONE
FootballTransfers

body: Bradley Barcola has told Paris Saint-Germain he will not sign a new contract at the club, according to ONE, ending months of stop-start negotiations and pushing the France winger a significant step closer to an exit this summer.

The 23-year-old still has two years to run on the deal he signed when he arrived from Lyon in September 2023 for around €45 million, with terms through 2028. But according to ONE and reporting out of France picked up by Fabrizio Romano, Barcola has effectively ceased extension talks despite PSG offering him improved terms.

At the heart of it is playing time in the games that matter most. Barcola was a regular contributor in Ligue 1 last season, but Luis Enrique consistently preferred Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the biggest European nights, including PSG's Champions League final win over Arsenal in Budapest in May, where Barcola started on the bench.

That victory made PSG back-to-back European champions, the first team to retain the trophy since Real Madrid, and left Enrique with one of the deepest and most decorated forward lines in world football. For Barcola, the reward for staying has been rotation rather than a guaranteed starting shirt, even after a season in which he made 49 appearances across all competitions, scoring 13 goals and adding six assists, per ONE's figures.

PSG have made clear they will not simply let him leave for nothing. ONE reports the club is holding out for a fee in excess of €100 million to sanction a sale, more than double what they paid Lyon three years ago. Other reports in England have floated an even higher valuation, in the region of €170 million, though no figure has been confirmed by either club, and it should be treated as a starting position rather than an agreed price.

Liverpool are described as the leading candidates, with Barcola said to have given the Anfield club priority if a deal with PSG can be struck. The Merseyside club have been searching for attacking reinforcements since Mohamed Salah's departure as a free agent at the end of last season after nine years at the club, and Arsenal have also been credited with interest in the France international.

Nothing here amounts to an agreed transfer. Barcola remains PSG property, the two Premier League clubs are said to be only monitoring or working on the situation, and the fee PSG want has not been tested by any concrete bid. What is now clear, on ONE's reporting and elsewhere, is that Barcola himself has decided his future lies away from the Parc des Princes.

body: Hapoel Haifa owner Yoav Katz has ruled out any sale of Yaad Gonen this summer, revealing that offers for the young midfielder landed on his desk within hours of the player inspiring a derby win over Maccabi Haifa.
"We received offers on Gonen last night, he is not for sale," Katz told ONE. "I think the right place for him is Hapoel Haifa. The player is not for sale, let's focus on the season."
Katz did not name the clubs behind the approaches, but the timing was pointed: it came the morning after Gonen had produced the standout moment of Saturday's Toto Cup derby at Sammy Ofer Stadium.

Hapoel Haifa raced into a 3-0 lead over their city rivals, with Gonen opening the scoring in the 30th minute with what Israeli outlets described as a genuine wondergoal, curling a 20-metre strike into the top corner after being picked out by Ariel Mendi.
An own goal from Shteinman and a free-kick from Turgeman extended the lead before Maccabi Haifa hit back through Halaili and Azulay inside four minutes, but Hapoel held on for a 3-2 win.

Gonen, 20, operates as Hapoel Haifa's number 10 and has emerged as one of the more eye-catching young talents in Haifa this season, with the club having moved earlier in the year to tie him down to a longer deal rather than risk losing him for a smaller fee.
He remains under contract at the club for the current season plus one further year, giving Hapoel Haifa leverage to resist any approach rather than negotiate from a position of weakness.

Katz also used the interview to praise the club's scouting department, name-checking recruiter Sattov, and stressed that the immediate target is a strong campaign rather than a summer sale — with an eye on reaching the top playoff group.

"Haifa is not Tel Aviv, the derby is more than just a game," Katz added, underlining why keeping hold of a player who has just delivered a derby-defining goal matters as much symbolically as it does on the pitch.

title: Cavaliers and Warriors turn to Mario Hezonja after LeBron picks 76ers
dek: Shams Charania reports both teams have sharply increased their pursuit of the Croatian forward as he clears a buyout clause to leave Real Madrid.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Eurohoops
Hoops Rumors
ESPN (LeBron James signing)

body: The Cleveland Cavaliers and Golden State Warriors have both significantly stepped up their interest in Mario Hezonja, ONE reports, as the Croatian forward edges closer to a return to the NBA after six years in Europe.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania, cited by ONE, the two franchises moved quickly once LeBron James took himself off the market — Hezonja is now described as a genuine target for both, rather than a fallback option.

James ended weeks of speculation on Friday by signing a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, calling it 'my last decision' as he begins a 24th NBA season. His choice freed up cap plans in both Cleveland and the Bay Area, and both front offices pivoted almost immediately to Hezonja.

The 31-year-old has reportedly positioned himself to clear an exit clause with Real Madrid worth around $850,000, clearing the financial path for an NBA move, though ONE notes the payment has not yet been finalized.

The Cavaliers had kept cap space open in the hope of luring James himself; with that gone, they are said to have redirected that flexibility toward Hezonja. The Warriors, for their part, are looking for forward depth and view him as what ONE describes as the most sensible target both professionally and financially given their own tax constraints.

Hezonja was the No. 5 overall pick by the Orlando Magic in 2015 and went on to play for the New York Knicks and Portland Trail Blazers during a five-season NBA career. He then took his game to Greece and Russia for a season apiece before joining Real Madrid, where he has spent the last four years.

His European run has been anything but a step down. Hezonja won a EuroLeague title with Real Madrid in 2023, has earned multiple All-EuroLeague honors, and was named MVP of Spain's Liga Endesa regular season this year — a résumé that helps explain why two NBA contenders are circling.

ONE also reports that Hezonja's agent, Miško Raznatović, posted a cryptic message on social media invoking the 'knightly tradition' of Dubrovnik, the player's hometown — widely read by observers as a coded nod toward the Cavaliers.
Sources close to Hezonja quoted by ONE pushed back on the idea that the NBA buzz is merely leverage for a bigger European contract, insisting his priority is simply to get back to the league.

Nothing is close to done: Hezonja has not chosen a team, and neither Cleveland nor Golden State has confirmed an offer. But with the market unfrozen by James's decision, a resolution is expected to move quickly in the days ahead.

title: Petit says Kane 'disappeared' when it mattered, ruling him out of the Ballon d'Or race
dek: The 1998 World Cup winner argues Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi are all ahead of the Bayern Munich striker despite his prolific season in Germany.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Goal.com
Tribuna.com
Daily Post Nigeria
NPR (England-Argentina semi-final)

body: Emmanuel Petit has delivered a blunt verdict on Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or hopes: as far as the 1998 World Cup winner is concerned, they are already over, because the Bayern Munich striker vanished at the exact moments the award is supposed to be won or lost.

"In the Champions League and with the national team, when it started to be really hard to win, I think he disappeared," Petit said, in comments first carried in Israel by ONE and picked up widely across the European football press this week as the buildup to October's ceremony intensifies.

It is a harsh reading of a season in which Kane was, statistically, one of the most productive strikers in Europe. He scored 61 goals in 51 appearances in all competitions for Bayern, dragging the club to a domestic double of the Bundesliga title and the German Cup.

What eluded him again was the Champions League. Bayern were beaten by Paris Saint-Germain in the semi-finals, losing the first leg 5-4 in Paris before a 1-1 draw in the return sent PSG through 6-5 on aggregate. Kane's equaliser in that second leg arrived in stoppage time, too late to matter.

His summer with England followed a similar arc. Kane finished the World Cup as the Three Lions' leading scorer, but England's run ended in the semi-finals, beaten 1-2 by Argentina after Lionel Messi set up both of Lautaro Martínez's and Enzo Fernández's late goals to complete a comeback. Spain went on to beat Argentina in the final to lift the trophy.

For Petit, that pattern of Kane's numbers piling up in the group stages and the regular season while the biggest games slip away is disqualifying. "There are a few names ahead of him," he said, and he did not hesitate when asked to name them.

Lamine Yamal, who Petit said "had a great World Cup," tops his list, alongside Rodri, who he believes "has been the best player again during this World Cup" after Spain's triumph. Both were central to the team that dethroned Argentina in the final.

Messi himself also gets a mention. "He had a great competition, but he plays for Inter Miami," Petit said, a line that captures how much weight some voters still put on a player's club stage alongside their international form.

Petit knows a little about big-tournament pressure himself. He scored the third goal in France's 3-0 win over Brazil in the 1998 World Cup final, part of a career that also took in Monaco, Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea.
The Ballon d'Or organisers are due to announce this year's winner in October, with Kane, Yamal, Rodri and Messi all expected to feature prominently in the conversation between now and then.

title: Israeli swimmers eye finals as biggest-ever squad heads to European Championships
dek: Thirty-three athletes across pool, open water and artistic swimming travel to Paris, led by defending champion Anastasia Gorbenko and a fourth-placed finisher from Belgrade hungry for a podium.

verificationSources.label: ONE - original report

body: Israel is sending its largest swimming delegation in years to the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, with 33 athletes spread across pool swimming, open water and artistic swimming — and, according to ONE, a single word sums up the ambition inside the camp: finals.

The championships open on July 31 with artistic swimming, followed by open water racing in the Seine from August 4-8. The pool programme, where most of Israel's medal hopes are concentrated, runs August 10-16 and features an 18-strong Israeli squad.

That group is headlined by Anastasia Gorbenko, the defending European champion in both the women's 200m and 400m individual medley after her sweep at the 2024 championships in Belgrade, where she also became the first Israeli woman to win a European swimming title. She arrives in Paris as the standard-bearer for a program that has grown rapidly in depth.

Also central to the pool team is Meiron Cheruti, who finished fourth in the 50m butterfly in Belgrade. ONE reports he wants to go one better this time: "I want to threaten a medal," he said. "I feel I deserve to be on the podium."

The pool roster also includes Denis Luktev, Daria Golobati, Tomer Shoster, Marc Teller, Okan Goldin, Yoav Romano and Daniel Kritchevsky among others, giving Israel a squad with realistic entrants in individual events and relays alike.

Beyond the pool, Israel is fielding an open water team featuring Ofek Adir, Yonatan Achdut, Emily Golos and Rebecca Androwicz in the Seine, while an artistic swimming squad that includes Noya Tzarfati, Ella Steiner and the Makmel sisters opens the entire championships on the meet's first day.

According to ONE, head coach Leonid Kaufman and sports director Yaakov Tomerkin have set the delegation a collective target of five final appearances across the three disciplines — a marker of how much the program's ambitions have risen since Gorbenko's breakthrough generation began delivering results on the continental stage.

The report also notes Israel's relay strength has grown alongside its individual stars, with a national record of 7:06.29 set by a relay quartet at this year's World Championships cited as evidence the depth extends well past the headline names.

With three disciplines competing across more than two weeks in and around the French capital, Paris will be the clearest test yet of whether Israeli swimming's recent surge can be sustained beyond Gorbenko alone — and whether Cheruti and others can turn semi-final appearances into the podium finishes they are now openly chasing.

title: Fitness coach Vidraro contradicts Houdda's account in Tiberias infusions affair
dek: Shlomi Vidraro denies ever clearing the banned infusions given to Ironi Tiberias players, telling investigators he warned against it over WADA concerns — directly at odds with head coach Eliran Houdda's own testimony, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Vidraro's response to Houdda's testimony
Walla Sport - Houdda faces especially heavy punishment
Mako - coach and five players suspended over infusions
Ynet - Ashdod complaint over banned infusions

body: A fresh crack has opened in Ironi Tiberias's banned-infusions affair, with fitness coach Shlomi Vidraro directly contradicting the version of events given by head coach Eliran Houdda in his testimony to investigators, ONE reported.

The dispute sits at the heart of the case that has engulfed the Ligat Ha'al club since early July, when the National Anti-Doping Agency provisionally suspended Houdda, five first-team players, technical director Chen Sol and Vidraro himself over suspected banned intravenous infusions administered to Tiberias players, following a complaint from Ashdod that accused Tiberias of using illegal treatments around the playoff race.

In his own investigation testimony, Houdda said he had checked whether the infusions were permissible before they were carried out, and that the assurance came back to him secondhand. According to his account, Sol told him: "I spoke with Shlomi, there's approval." Houdda added that he had proposed the procedure be carried out at a hospital for proper protocol, but was told it could only be done on the club's own premises.

Vidraro tells a completely different story. ONE reported that the fitness coach produced a message he sent to Sol at the time, warning explicitly against the treatment: "Chen, I checked now, don't get involved, there are WADA matters and that's my recommendation."

The contradiction matters because Houdda, according to Walla Sport, is the figure the anti-doping agency views as most culpable in the affair — facing an 18-to-24-month ban if he accepts a plea deal, or as much as four years if he contests the charges and loses. Any evidence undercutting his defence that the infusions were cleared in advance could weigh heavily against him.

Tiberias itself has denied wrongdoing throughout, insisting the players received a legal saline solution within permitted volumes and under professional supervision. Club owner Aria Kalmenson has gone further, describing the case as manufactured pressure from rivals who wanted the club relegated.

The stakes extend well beyond the individuals named. Reports on the case have detailed a possible six-point deduction for Tiberias next season and restrictions on the club's activity in the January transfer window, on top of whatever sanctions the anti-doping tribunal ultimately imposes on Houdda, Sol, Vidraro and the suspended players.
For now the case remains unresolved, but Vidraro's account — if it holds up — leaves Houdda's version of who signed off on the infusions looking far shakier than it did a fortnight ago.

title: Sherif Kiouf's father: my son is no worse than Glazer or Yermakov
dek: The Maccabi Haifa reserve goalkeeper's move to newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan collapsed after a serious training injury, but his father tells ONE that the club's two higher-profile shot-stoppers have nothing on his son.

verificationSources.label: ONE

Sport5 - Better than Georgi Yermakov? Omri Glazer 2026
Walla Sport - Maccabi Haifa confirms Georgi Yermakov transfer to Metalist Kharkiv

body: Sherif Kiouf had all but completed the paperwork on a return to the top flight with newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan when a serious injury wrecked the move. With the goalkeeper now facing a long spell on the sidelines, it is his father doing the talking to the Israeli press - and he isn't shy about the comparisons being drawn against him.

Speaking to ONE, Kiouf's father argued that his son is not inferior to Omri Glazer or Georgi Yermakov, the two goalkeepers who have defined Maccabi Haifa's position this summer. Asked directly whether Kiouf measures up to that pair, his answer was blunt: "If you ask me I tell you no, he does not fall short of them."

Kiouf, a Druze goalkeeper from Isfiya born in 2001, has been on Maccabi Haifa's books since 2020, working his way up through loan spells at Hapoel Kfar Saba and Hapoel Afula, where he made 44 league appearances, before briefly becoming Haifa's first-choice goalkeeper during the 2023/24 season - the year the club won the championship.

Since then he has settled into a reserve role behind the club's senior goalkeepers, and had reportedly agreed personal terms to join Hapoel Ramat Gan on loan for next season. Ramat Gan, coached by Masai Dago, clinched promotion back to Ligat Ha'al this summer after 13 years in Liga Leumit and were counting on Kiouf to strengthen their goalkeeping department for the step up.

The move fell apart when Kiouf suffered a serious injury during a Maccabi Haifa training match against Hapoel Kfar Saba just as the transfer was being finalized. He now faces an estimated six months out, with hopes of returning before the season is over, and Ramat Gan have been forced to abandon the signing altogether.

The timing is awkward for Kiouf at Haifa. The club has just re-signed Omri Glazer, the Israel international, on a three-year deal reported to be worth around 400,000 euros a season - a move that eases Georgi Yermakov toward the exit. The Ukrainian goalkeeper is reported to be closing in on a switch to Metalist Kharkiv worth roughly 3 million euros, after a single, largely successful season in Israel.

That reshuffle leaves Kiouf even further down the pecking order at Sammy Ofer Stadium, which only sharpens his father's frustration. "The goalkeepers they brought are not better than him," he said, adding that his son has made clear he has no intention of settling for the bench: "He said there is no chance he would stay as a second goalkeeper, he wants to play."

For now, with his transfer on hold and a lengthy rehabilitation ahead, Kiouf's immediate priority is recovering from the injury. Where he plays once he is fit again - and whether Hapoel Ramat Gan or another club revives its interest - remains an open question heading into the new Ligat Ha'al season.

title: Haziza surprised by Haifa exit, agent says he expected to finish his career there
dek: Agent Ronen Katzav says the veteran winger did not expect to leave Maccabi Haifa after seven trophy-laden years, before completing a two-year, $250,000-a-season move to Maccabi Netanya.

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Dolev Haziza didn't expect this summer to end with him leaving Maccabi Haifa. Seven years, three league titles and the captain's armband later, the winger has signed for Maccabi Netanya instead — a move his own agent describes as one he never saw coming.

Speaking to ONE, agent Ronen Katzav said Haziza believed he would finish his career at Haifa. "It's not a regular event when such a significant player leaves before his contract ends," Katzav said, adding that Haziza "thought he would finish his career there, but we need to move forward."

Katzav said there had been several offers on the table, from clubs in Greece as well as in Israel, but that Netanya emerged as "the most interesting and suitable club" for his client. According to ONE, Haziza was caught off guard by how the exit played out and may yet address the situation himself in the coming days.

The move traces back to a squad clear-out overseen by Lior Refaelov, the former Haifa captain and Israel international who was elevated to sporting director at the club this year. Refaelov held individual conversations with several first-team players this summer informing them they were not part of the club's plans for the coming season — Haziza among them, according to Israeli reporting.

Given his standing at the club, Haziza was reportedly given a rare exception: he continued training with Haifa's first team while a new destination was found, rather than being frozen out immediately.

His Haifa career, which began in 2019 after a move from Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv, coincided with arguably the most successful spell in the club's modern history — three consecutive Israeli championships, with Haziza wearing the captain's armband. Last season alone he contributed nine goals and two assists, according to Sport5.
He has also become a fixture for the Israel national team, winning 18 caps since making his debut in November 2019.

At Netanya, Haziza has signed a two-year contract running to the summer of 2028, on a reported salary of $250,000 a season, Sport5 reported. Walla Sport reported separately that Maccabi Haifa is contributing roughly 400,000 shekels toward his outstanding contract as compensation for releasing him early.
Netanya's coaching staff said they were struck by the winger's hunger to open a new chapter and lead a Premier League squad, according to Sport5's report on the signing.

Maccabi Haifa, for its part, described Haziza in a statement as a symbol of "passion, dedication, leadership and genuine connection to the club" — even as head coach Barak Bakhar voiced his own frustration at a press conference over how the exit had been handled, a sign the parting was not entirely amicable despite the warm words.

For Haziza, 31, the switch to Netanya's yellow and black marks the first time since 2019 that he will not be playing in Haifa's green — closing one of the more decorated individual runs of the current Israeli Premier League era, and opening an uncertain new one.

title: M.K. Kfar Saba tie down ever-present defender Tal Banash for another season
dek: The Liga Alef South club has extended the local-born right-back, who started all 23 league matches last season, as part of a wider summer refresh under manager Shimon Alkabetz.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Wikipedia (Hebrew) — Tal Banash

body: M.K. Kfar Saba, the young club representing the Sharon town in Liga Alef South, have announced that defender Tal Banash will remain with them for another season, tying down one of the more reliable performers from a squad that is being reshaped for the coming campaign.

Banash, a Kfar Saba native, came up through the youth ranks at Hapoel Kfar Saba before a well-travelled career that took in spells at Hapoel Tel Aviv and Beitar Jerusalem, among other clubs, in both the top flight and the national league.

The right-back was one of the most durable presences in last season's side, starting all 23 league matches and being withdrawn early in only two of them, for a total of roughly 2,200 minutes on the pitch — a workload the club highlighted in announcing the extension.

M.K. Kfar Saba is a separate entity from the city's better-known Hapoel Kfar Saba, now Maccabi Haifa's satellite club, and from Beitar Kfar Saba, having built its own following in the third tier over the past couple of seasons under manager Shimon Alkabetz, who arrived after a successful stint in charge of Beitar Yavneh.

Banash's new deal is one of several retention moves the club confirmed this summer. Goalkeeper Ben Weitzman, 32, midfielder Ariel Golan, 19, and defender Roni Laufer, 25, have also agreed to stay on for the new campaign.

Alongside the renewals, the club has been active in the transfer market, bringing in defender Ohad Atiya, 28, striker Mor Saado, 20, left-back Ben Levi, 23, and forward Omer Pruchtman, 22, as it builds a squad aimed at pushing higher up the Liga Alef South table.

title: Chuli joins Kiryat Ata as Tyus edges toward a Hapoel Haifa move
dek: The 24-year-old guard leaves Elitzur Yavne for the Premier League, while ONE reports veteran center Alex Tyus is deep in talks to join Hapoel Haifa's National League side.

verificationSources.label: ONE
ONE - Alex Tyus turned down Hapoel Haifa earlier this year
IBBA - Oz Chuli player profile

body: Kiryat Ata has strengthened its backcourt for next season, confirming the signing of Oz Chuli from National League side Elitzur Yavne, where the 24-year-old had captained the team.

Chuli, who stands 1.94m, arrives with a strong statistical case: last season he averaged 14.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.7 steals across 35 games for Yavne. "I'm very happy and excited to start a new chapter in the Premier League," he said after putting pen to paper. "I'm ready to give everything for Kiryat Ata's amazing fans."

The move up a division comes as Kiryat Ata reshuffles its roster. Gal Beytner, who wore the captain's armband last season under coach Eldad Bentov and was valued for his defensive intensity, has left the club after two years, moving instead to Maccabi Rehovot in the National League.

Further south, Hapoel Haifa is working on a far higher-profile addition. ONE reports the club is in advanced negotiations with veteran center Alex Tyus to join its National League roster, though nothing has been signed yet.

Tyus, 38, is one of the most decorated imports-turned-citizens in Israeli basketball history. He won the EuroLeague title with Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2014 and has also played for Real Madrid and Galatasaray during a long European career, alongside a spell at Hapoel Jerusalem.

It is not the first time the two sides have been linked. Hapoel Haifa previously tried to bring Tyus in during the current season, reportedly offering him close to six figures for a season and a half in a bid to make him the highest-paid Israeli player in National League history — an approach Tyus rejected at the time while he was still playing in Turkey.

Alongside the Tyus talks, Hapoel Haifa is also weighing a move for Maxim Romanov, a 25-year-old, 2.01m forward who has come through several National League clubs including Maccabi Kiryat Gat and Maccabi Rishon LeZion.
None of the Hapoel Haifa business is done, but with Kiryat Ata's ins and outs already confirmed, the National League's close season is clearly heating up.

title: Pirlo's appointment as Italy coach frozen over Russian betting sponsorship
dek: ONE reports that FIGC president Giovanni Malagò has paused what looked like a done deal, with Andrea Pirlo's role as an ambassador for the Russian bookmaker Fonbet triggering a political storm in Rome.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Football Italia
il Fatto Quotidiano

body: Andrea Pirlo's coronation as the new coach of Italy looked all but done a day ago. By Saturday, ONE reports, it had been put on ice by the federation's own president over the World Cup-winning midfielder's commercial ties to a Russian betting company.

According to the report, FIGC president Giovanni Malagò moved to suspend sign-off on Pirlo's appointment after it emerged the former Juventus and Milan playmaker is a paid global ambassador for Fonbet, one of Russia's largest bookmakers, a role he has held since October 2025.

The issue is not the gambling sponsorship in isolation — Italian regulations already bar national-team figures from any betting-industry advertising, direct or indirect, and that clause alone would require Pirlo to sever the tie before taking the job. What has escalated the story into a political affair is Fonbet's nationality, given Italy's continued diplomatic freeze with Moscow since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Pirlo reportedly attended a Fonbet promotional event in Moscow as part of the ambassadorship, a detail that Italian outlets say has amplified domestic criticism of the timing and optics of his prospective appointment.

ONE's report notes that Pirlo's legal team frames the Fonbet arrangement as a byproduct of his current coaching job in the United Arab Emirates rather than a standalone deal — pointing out that the club's owner, Sergey Lomakhin, holds substantial interests in the betting company, and arguing that ending Pirlo's Emirati contract would automatically dissolve the sponsorship with it.

Pirlo is said to be seeking a direct meeting with Malagò to explain his position, but the federation has signalled it does not intend to negotiate terms with a coach still under contract elsewhere — leaving the timeline for any resolution unclear.

The appointment had been driven not by Malagò himself but by technical director Paolo Maldini and advisor Leonardo, who according to Italian media pushed for Pirlo once Pep Guardiola turned down approaches to take over the Azzurri. Malagò, elected FIGC president in June after Gabriele Gravina resigned in the wake of Italy's failure to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, had reportedly leaned toward Roberto Mancini before deferring to his technical staff.

Reports in the Italian press this week had Pirlo signing a deal running to 2030, worth roughly €1.5 million a year with bonuses tied to qualifying for the European Championship, reaching the knockout rounds, and qualifying for the World Cup — terms that were expected to be ratified at an FIGC council meeting scheduled for Tuesday, July 28.

That meeting's outcome is now in doubt. Politically, the affair has drawn in figures well beyond football: European Parliament vice-president Pina Picierno has publicly accused Pirlo of lending his prestige to an effort to normalise the Kremlin internationally, according to Italian reporting cited alongside ONE's account.

For now, Italy remains without a permanent coach as it looks toward the next World Cup cycle, with Pirlo's candidacy paused rather than withdrawn — and Maldini and Leonardo still said to be backing him as their first choice once the Fonbet question is resolved.

title: Clubs demand cooling-off period before naturalized internationals count as Israeli in league
dek: Maccabi Tel Aviv's Shimon Mizrahi and Bnei Herzliya's Eldad Akunis want a two-to-three-year wait before players naturalized for the national team can be registered as Israelis in the domestic league, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - דרישה: מתאזרח בנבחרת לא ישחק כישראלי בליגה
Wikipedia - Khadeen Carrington
Walla Sport - נבחרת ישראל אופטימית: מאחורי אזרוח קאדין קרינגטון

body: A quarrel that has simmered in Israeli basketball since Khadeen Carrington first pulled on a national team jersey is heading for a formal reckoning, with ONE reporting that two of the league's most powerful club chairmen want naturalized internationals frozen out of domestic status for years after they take an Israeli passport.

Shimon Mizrahi, the long-serving chairman of Maccabi Tel Aviv, and Eldad Akunis, who heads Bnei Herzliya, are pushing for a cooling-off period of two to three years between a foreign player's naturalization for the national team and his eligibility to be registered as an Israeli, rather than a foreign import, in the domestic league.

The demand is aimed squarely at closing what the two chairmen regard as a loophole first exposed by Carrington's case. The guard, a Trinidadian-American who arrived at Hapoel Jerusalem in 2022, became the first player in the country's history to be naturalized specifically so he could represent the Israeli national team.

Once his citizenship came through, Carrington was registered in the league not as one of Hapoel Jerusalem's quota of foreign players but as a domestic Israeli, freeing up an import slot for the club and, in the eyes of rival executives, handing it a competitive edge that had nothing to do with what happened on court.

According to ONE, the proposal now on the table would prevent any future naturalized player from being counted as Israeli in league play until he has either completed two full cycles in the national team's colors or three years have passed since his citizenship was approved.

The dispute has already gone before arbitration. Retired judge Oded Modrik, acting as arbitrator, has ruled that any such change to the rules requires the written agreement of all 14 clubs in Israel's top flight, with a deadline of August 31, 2026 for that unanimous sign-off to be secured.

That threshold gives every club, including Hapoel Jerusalem, effective veto power over a rule that would directly affect how it uses Carrington and any future naturalized signing. Getting fourteen ownership groups to agree on anything in Israeli basketball is rarely straightforward.

The Israel Basketball Association, now chaired by Amos Frishman, has separately set up a naturalization committee tasked with drafting clearer guidelines for how foreign players are fast-tracked to citizenship for national team purposes, and how their status is then treated back in the league.

The underlying tension is familiar to anyone who has followed Israeli basketball's repeated attempts to bolster the national team: the federation and Interior Ministry have leaned on naturalization to strengthen the side for EuroBasket and World Cup qualifying campaigns, while club owners worry about the knock-on effects for league competitive balance.

Whether the August deadline produces a unanimous agreement, or simply hardens the standoff between clubs that benefit from naturalized talent and those that do not, is likely to shape how Israeli basketball handles its next naturalization case.

The proposal calls for a wait of two to three years — or completion of two full national team campaigns — between a player's naturalization and his eligibility to count as an Israeli, rather than a foreign import, in league play.
The push follows the precedent of Hapoel Jerusalem guard Khadeen Carrington, naturalized to play for Israel's national team and then immediately registered as a domestic player in the league.
Retired judge Oded Modrik, serving as arbitrator, ruled that the rule change requires written agreement from all 14 Israeli Premier League clubs by August 31, 2026.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem land NBA forward Kenny Lofton Jr. after big-money chase
dek: The club raised its offer by 30 percent and flew the 23-year-old to Las Vegas to close the deal, ONE reports, as Jerusalem's Euroleague-chasing spending spree continues.

body: Hapoel Jerusalem have pulled off one of the marquee signings of the Israeli basketball summer, securing NBA forward Kenneth "Kenny" Lofton Jr. after a chase that, according to ONE, ended with the club sweetening its original offer by 30 percent to get the deal done.

ONE reports the contract is worth $1.3 million with significant performance bonuses attached, running through the end of the 2026/27 season. The figure has not been confirmed by other outlets, though the signing itself has been reported widely.

The pursuit, as described by ONE, went well beyond a straightforward negotiation. Jerusalem produced promotional videos showcasing the club's history and ambitions, flew Lofton and his representatives to Las Vegas for three days, and hosted him at owner Matan Adelson's home for a private shooting session on Adelson's home court. The 23-year-old was also invited to watch Conor McGregor fight at T-Mobile Arena, while club officials held separate talks with his father.

General manager Dan Shamir, head coach Saša Obradović and assistant coach Yair Shavit were all directly involved in the recruitment, ONE says — underlining how central the signing is to Jerusalem's plans for the coming season. Notably, this was Jerusalem's second attempt at landing Lofton; the club reportedly tried and failed to sign him two years ago.

Lofton arrives with a resume that has grown steadily more eye-catching since he went undrafted out of Louisiana Tech in 2022. He signed a two-way deal with the Memphis Grizzlies and, in April 2023, produced one of the most remarkable debuts in NBA history: 42 points and 14 rebounds in his first career start, against the Oklahoma City Thunder, making him the first player ever to post 40 points and 10 rebounds in a debut start.

In total he made 49 NBA appearances across spells with Memphis, Philadelphia and Utah. He also won G League Rookie of the Year in 2022-23 and earned two All-G League First Team selections, averaging 23.4 points, 9.9 rebounds and 3.8 assists in that league.

Last season Lofton moved to China's Shanghai Sharks, where he was named CBA MVP and helped the club win the Chinese league championship, averaging 24.4 points, 12.2 rebounds and 6.5 assists. Jerusalem is his first stop in European basketball.

He joins a frontcourt that already includes David Roddy, the former Denver Nuggets forward and 2022 first-round pick, who agreed a 1+1 deal worth $1.5 million per season with Jerusalem this summer, according to Sportando. Roddy played 173 NBA games across four seasons before making the move to Europe.

The two additions cap an ambitious rebuild in the capital that has also brought in Devontae Cacok and Jaleen Smith and secured the re-signing of Jared Harper, while Obradović was hired to lead the project on the bench — all signs of a club explicitly building toward Euroleague qualification.

ONE reports Lofton is currently training at Tracy McGrady's facility in the United States as he prepares for his first season in Israel. "I'm excited to join Hapoel Jerusalem and begin my journey in European basketball. From the very first moment, I was impressed by the club's ambitions," Lofton said, according to Eurohoops. Obradović added that his new forward brings "a rare combination of strength, talent and versatility" to the roster.

title: Baltaksa returns to full training, on track to face Víkingur
dek: The Hapoel Beer Sheva centre-back, sidelined by a head injury sustained before the first leg in Iceland, trained without restrictions on Sunday and is expected to be available for Wednesday's Champions League qualifying return leg in Hungary.

body: Matan Baltaksa took a full, unrestricted training session on Sunday, the clearest sign yet that Hapoel Beer Sheva will have their first-choice centre-back available for Wednesday's Champions League second qualifying round return leg against Víkingur Reykjavík.

Baltaksa was ruled out of the first leg in Iceland after taking a knock to the head in the final training session before the game, with the club's medical staff erring on the side of caution given the concussion protocols now standard across European football.

His absence was keenly felt. Beer Sheva's back line looked short of its usual composure in Reykjavík, and Víkingur snatched a stoppage-time winner to complete a 2-1 victory that leaves the Israeli champions needing to overturn the aggregate deficit in the second leg.

According to ONE, Baltaksa has progressed steadily through his return-to-play process over the past week, working his way from individual rehabilitation drills back into full contact training with the group.

The 30-year-old, who joined Beer Sheva from Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2024 and has since become a regular for the Israel national team, is now expected to be fit for selection unless there is an unforeseen setback before kickoff.

Manager Ran Kozhuch had already shown faith in the squad's depth by starting the game in Iceland without his usual centre-back, but getting Baltaksa's ball-playing range and aerial presence back at the heart of defence will be a significant boost for a side that must now attack a two-goal swing.

As with all of Beer Sheva's continental fixtures since the security-driven relocation of Israeli clubs' home European games, the return leg will not be played at Turner Stadium. The tie shifts instead to Szombathely in Hungary, the venue Beer Sheva have been using as their designated home ground in this season's competition.
The squad is due to fly out to Hungary on Monday to train and prepare on-site before Wednesday's game, giving Baltaksa a final block of sessions to prove his fitness to the coaching staff.

Beer Sheva have never faced Víkingur before this tie, and the Icelandic champions arrive full of confidence after seeing off Győri ETO of Hungary in the previous round. A first-leg deficit of this size is not insurmountable, but it leaves Kozhuch's side with little margin for error at the back — precisely the department Baltaksa's return is designed to shore up.

title: Salah has agreed to join Beşiktaş — but his agent hasn't
dek: ONE reports the free agent has struck personal terms with the Turkish club on a lucrative two-year deal, but a commission stand-off involving his agent, Rami Abbas, is holding up the signing.

body: Mohamed Salah has personally agreed to join Beşiktaş, but the move remains stuck in limbo because his own representative has not signed off on the deal, according to a report by the Israeli outlet ONE.
The Egyptian forward left Liverpool as a free agent this summer, bringing to a close nine trophy-laden seasons at Anfield, and has spent the following weeks weighing his next move.

ONE reports that personal terms are already in place: a two-year contract worth around €12 million per season, with Beşiktaş head coach Vincenzo Italiano understood to have driven the push to land him.
What is holding up the transfer, according to the report, is not Salah himself but his longtime agent, Rami Abbas, who has yet to reach an agreement with the club over his own commission.

ONE reports Abbas initially demanded a 35 percent cut of the deal — roughly €8.4 million — before lowering his figure to €5 million. Beşiktaş, in turn, have put forward a final offer of €4 million, which the agent has so far declined to accept.

The Turkish club is said to be waiting for Abbas to show more flexibility, with Salah currently on vacation and expected to travel to Istanbul once talks with the club's management and coaching staff are further along, per the report.

Turkish reporting this week has broadly matched that picture: Beşiktaş president Serdal Adalı said the club has submitted what it considers its final offer and is waiting on a response, while other outlets have described the commission dispute as the last real obstacle to a deal that had appeared close for days.

Exact figures differ slightly by outlet — some report Abbas's opening commission demand at €7.5 million rather than €8.4 million — but the substance is consistent: personal terms are essentially settled, and the transfer hinges on the agent and the club closing the gap on his cut.

Should it go through, the move would represent a significant pay cut for Salah compared with his reported wages at Liverpool, but it would still rank as one of the most eye-catching free transfers of the summer and a major coup for Süper Lig football.

Elmishli, who stands 1.90m, came up through the Upper Galilee club's youth system and is regarded internally as exactly the kind of homegrown talent the organisation is built to nurture.

Locking in a teenager on a multi-year deal, rather than letting him drift into the free-agent market once his rookie terms expired, fits that identity.

For Elmishli, the deal buys time: three more seasons inside a first-team environment to add muscle, minutes and experience before anyone outside the club is asked to judge whether the early promise translates into a genuine rotation player.

title: Ironi Tiberias doubles down, says federation probe has become 'a campaign of intimidation'
dek: The Liga Ha'al club escalates its fight against association investigator Din Frager, alleging threats, leaks and political interference in a case that could cost it 30 points.

verificationSources.label: ONE - original report
Ynet - Tiberias petitions football tribunal to disqualify investigation
Sport1-Maariv - prosecutor seeks 30-point deduction over alleged double contracts
Channel 14 - Football Association dismisses Tiberias's claims as manufactured drama

body: Ironi Tiberias has escalated its confrontation with the Israel Football Association, issuing a fresh statement accusing the investigator handling its disciplinary case of turning the probe into what the club called "a campaign of intimidation," ONE reported.

The case at the centre of the storm concerns allegations that Tiberias ran a parallel, off-the-books financial and contractual system for four years, including suspected double contracts and document forgery designed to breach the league's salary-cap rules. The Football Association's prosecutor, attorney Gilad Bergman, has asked for a 30-point deduction, one of the heaviest sanctions available in Israeli football.

In its latest statement, Tiberias directed its anger squarely at investigator Din Frager, alleging he threatened to have players' licenses revoked if they refused to cooperate, and that he dangled plea bargains he had no authority to offer, describing them as "false promises made on his own initiative."

The club also claimed that the name of Football Association chairman Moshe "Shino" Zoaretz was invoked during questioning in a manner intended to intimidate those being interviewed, and that details of the case were shared with an outside party, Gal Bar-Am, chief executive of Hapoel Nof HaGalil.

Bar-Am's club has previously been reported as a beneficiary of any points deduction or relegation imposed on Tiberias, since a drop for Tiberias would open a path back to the top flight for Nof HaGalil.

Tiberias further alleged that Bergman himself blurred the line between prosecuting the case and actively directing the investigation, a conflation the club says compromised the process from the start.

The statement summed up the club's position bluntly: "When rushing, threats, politics, connections, exceeding authority and evidence contamination meet in one interrogation room, the result is not an investigation, but a fabricated case."

This is not the first time Tiberias has gone after Frager directly. The club has previously sent him a warning letter through its lawyers demanding his suspension from the case, a formal apology within 72 hours and roughly 100,000 shekels in compensation, while releasing recordings it says show Frager discussing the case improperly with outside parties.

The Football Association has pushed back hard against the club's campaign. Its legal department has previously dismissed Tiberias's claims as an attempt to "create drama out of nothing," characterising the club's public offensive as a coordinated media strategy meant to obstruct investigators, and accusing Tiberias of leaking investigation transcripts itself while complaining about leaks.

Tiberias has already petitioned the Football Association's judicial tribunal in an attempt to have the investigation disqualified and to halt the prosecutor from filing an indictment. No ruling on that petition, nor a decision on the proposed points deduction, has yet been announced.

The saga has run alongside a separate strand of the case involving allegations that Tiberias players received banned intravenous infusions, which prompted a complaint from Ashdod and drew in Israel's national anti-doping authority. Tiberias is currently playing in the top-flight Ligat Ha'al for the 2025/26 season, with the disciplinary case still unresolved.

title: Fans crown Messi player of the World Cup, ahead of Mbappé and Golden Ball winner Rodri
dek: In a reader poll on ONE, Lionel Messi took 36% of the vote as the tournament's stand-out player, finishing ahead of Golden Boot winner Kylian Mbappé and official Golden Ball recipient Rodri.

body: ONE's readers have delivered their own verdict on the best player of the 2026 World Cup — and it isn't the man who took home the Golden Boot or FIFA's official Golden Ball. In a poll of the Israeli sports site's audience, Lionel Messi was voted the tournament's outstanding performer, finishing clear of Kylian Mbappé, Rodri and Jude Bellingham despite Argentina falling short in the final.

Messi collected 36% of the vote, comfortably ahead of the field. ONE credits the Argentine captain, now 39, with eight goals and four assists over the tournament, involvement in a dozen goals in total and a new World Cup record for assists — a remarkable return for a player at the tail end of his career, even in a losing cause.

Mbappé finished second in the reader poll with 24%, despite arriving with the stronger paper case: the France captain scored 10 goals to claim the tournament's Golden Boot outright, two clear of Messi, and set a new World Cup scoring record along the way.

Rodri was third with 21% of the vote. The Spanish midfielder was FIFA's actual pick as player of the tournament, winning the Golden Ball after anchoring a Spain side that conceded remarkably little across the competition on their way to the title.

Bellingham rounded out the poll in fourth on 19%, having scored seven goals and added an assist as England reached the semi-final stage before finishing third — a strong individual tournament that still couldn't match the drama attached to Messi's name.

The poll comes against the backdrop of a final Messi will want to forget on the scoresheet, if not for the occasion itself. Spain beat Argentina in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the winner as Messi and his teammates were denied a second successive world title.

That Messi still walked away with the reading public's vote, ahead of the tournament's official individual honours, says as much about his enduring pull with fans as it does about the numbers behind his campaign. He arrived in this World Cup as an elder statesman and leaves it having outscored every outfield player bar the Golden Boot winner himself.

For ONE's audience, at least, the story of the tournament remained Messi's — a poll result that reflects sentiment as much as statistics, but one that underlines just how much of the conversation around this World Cup he continued to command, all the way to a final he didn't win.

title: Vinicius Jr wants to stay at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest
dek: ONE reports the Brazilian winger's priority is a new Bernabéu contract, not a move to the Premier League champions, as José Mourinho builds his attack around him.

body: Not Arsenal — Vinícius Júnior wants to stay put at Real Madrid. That is the picture painted by ONE, which reports the Brazilian winger's priority this summer is renewing his contract at the Santiago Bernabéu rather than exploring a switch to the newly crowned Premier League champions.

Arsenal have indeed begun sniffing around, according to reporting from The Athletic cited in the ONE piece. But the interest is described as early and exploratory — informal enquiries rather than a concrete approach — with Mikel Arteta's club having internally flagged Vinícius as an aspirational, big-ticket addition rather than an active target with a bid attached.
The winger's own stance, ONE reports via the Spanish paper AS, cuts the speculation short: his preference is to extend and renew at Madrid, not to weigh up a move to England.

Vinícius still has roughly a year to run on his current deal, which expires in June 2027 after he signed a five-year extension back in October 2023 — an contract that included a release clause reported at around €1 billion. Renewal talks between the club and the player's camp had progressed significantly earlier in the year before stalling around the Club World Cup; they are expected to resume once Vinícius returns from his summer break.

Money is the main sticking point. Vinícius is said to be seeking close to €20 million net per season, roughly €5 million above the average he currently earns, which would make him the best-paid player in Madrid's dressing room, above Kylian Mbappé.

The backdrop makes Madrid's determination to keep him easy to understand. Incoming coach José Mourinho has reportedly told the club hierarchy he wants to retain all of his key attacking pieces, with Vinícius pencilled in alongside Mbappé and Jude Bellingham in a front three, supported by Aurélien Tchouaméni in midfield.
Club president Florentino Pérez has already put his own view on record, saying simply that "Vinícius wants to stay at Madrid and I want him to stay."
For now, then, the Arsenal story remains speculative interest rather than a live transfer saga — and by Real Madrid's own telling, one that Vinícius himself has no appetite to entertain.

title: Avi Nimni's son moves up a level with Hapoel Kfar Shalem

body: Amit Nimni, the 19-year-old son of Maccabi Tel Aviv legend Avi Nimni, has taken his first real step into senior Israeli football, signing a one-year contract with Hapoel Kfar Shalem of the Liga Leumit, Israel's second-tier National League, ONE reports.

The move is a genuine step up. Nimni spent last season with Samson Tel Aviv's youth setup, where ONE reports he scored more than 20 goals, while also being handed two senior appearances for the club in Liga Alef South, one tier below where he is now headed.

Hapoel Kfar Shalem, based in the Kfar Shalem quarter of southeast Tel Aviv, are managed by Noam Shoham, who returned to the club for a second spell in charge this year after a previous stint in the dugout. The Hatikva neighbourhood club have bounced between the National League and Liga Alef in recent seasons and will be looking to establish themselves back in the second tier.

According to ONE, Nimni is expected to make his debut for the club in the Toto Cup opener, a home fixture against Kfar Qasem at the Hatikva Neighborhood Stadium, the modest 2,570-capacity ground Kfar Shalem share with Bnei Yehuda.

The surname carries weight in Israeli football. Avi Nimni is Maccabi Tel Aviv's all-time leading scorer, spent much of his 17-season career at the club as captain, and had his number 8 shirt retired after he hung up his boots. He also had spells at Atletico Madrid, on loan at Derby County, and later at Beitar Jerusalem, alongside a long run with the Israel national team.

For his son, the jump from Liga Alef youth football to a National League first-team squad is exactly the kind of opportunity that comes with pressure attached. A one-year deal gives him a season to show he can hold his own in senior football on his own terms, away from the shadow of his father's name.

title: Klopp begins the job all of Germany has been waiting for
dek: The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach starts his tenure as Germany head coach through 2030, brought in to rebuild belief after a shock World Cup exit

verificationSources.label: ONE
CNN
ESPN
Bundesliga.com
Sport5

body: Jürgen Klopp has begun the job that, in the country he left as a player and the one he still calls home, felt inevitable from the moment Germany's World Cup collapsed. ONE's report captures the mood surrounding his unveiling as national team head coach: after years of carefully non-committal answers about a return to the touchline, Klopp has finally said yes to the job the entire country wanted him to take.

His appointment closes weeks of speculation that opened the moment Julian Nagelsmann resigned, immediately after Germany's shock Round of 32 exit from the 2026 World Cup, beaten by Paraguay on penalties. The manner of that collapse, a fancied German squad undone by a side ranked far below them, left the federation searching for more than a tactician. They wanted someone who could restore belief in the shirt.

Klopp has signed through the 2030 World Cup, a deal that also covers Euro 2028, with his tenure formally starting on 15 August 2026. It is a four-year commitment to a team he has never coached at any level, arriving instead with the standing of a man who rebuilt two clubs from crisis into champions.

He brings with him a staff drawn heavily from his Liverpool and Dortmund years. Peter Krawietz, 54, joins from the Red Bull group, having worked alongside Klopp at Mainz, Dortmund and Liverpool for close to two decades and shared in the 2019 Champions League and 2020 Premier League triumphs. Pepijn Lijnders, 43, the Dutch coach who was Klopp's closest lieutenant at Anfield before a recent spell assisting Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, also returns to his side.

Sven Bender, 37, completes the group. He played under Klopp for six years at Dortmund, later coached Germany's under-16 and under-17 sides between 2022 and 2024, and is the only member of the new staff with senior caps for the national team itself.

It amounts to Klopp importing much of the machinery that won him a Champions League and ended Liverpool's 30-year wait for the English title, now dropped into a very different kind of job: not weekly club management, but the periodic assembling of a national squad between major tournaments.

Before Germany, Klopp spent two years away from coaching as Red Bull's global head of soccer, overseeing the group's network of clubs, and worked as a World Cup commentator earlier this year. Those close to him always maintained his retirement from the touchline was a pause rather than an ending, and that the German job in particular had never stopped tempting him.

At Dortmund, he inherited a club sitting 13th in the Bundesliga in 2008 and turned it into back-to-back champions in 2011 and 2012, playing a pressing style that reshaped how the league's biggest clubs approached the game. That reputation, as much as any single trophy, is why the German federation is betting he can drag its national team out of its worst run in a generation.

Ynet, Sport5 and Walla had all reported the deal as good as done in the days before Friday's formal confirmation, with Sport5 describing an agreement in place well before the presentation itself. ONE's framing, that all of Germany had been waiting for this appointment, reflects just how starved the country's football public has been for a unifying figure since Nagelsmann walked away.

At Borussia Dortmund he won back-to-back Bundesliga titles in 2011 and 2012; at Liverpool he won the Champions League in 2019 and the Premier League in 2020.

body: Al-Hilal did not just beat Roma to Crysencio Summerville's signature this week — they made sure everyone knew it, turning their own announcement video into a pointed joke at the Italian club's expense.

The clip opened with the words "All roads lead to..." before the punchline landed: "Riyadh." It was a play on the old saying about Rome, and a not-so-subtle reminder of exactly which European giant had lost the race for the Dutch winger. ONE was among the outlets to flag the dig on Saturday.

The deal itself was substantial. Summerville completed his move from West Ham United on a four-year contract, with Sky Sports and transfer insider Fabrizio Romano both reporting an initial fee of around £55m that could climb past £60m with add-ons — one of the heftier fees paid by a Saudi Pro League club this window.

Roma's interest had been real and sustained. Manager Gian Piero Gasperini identified Summerville, alongside Manchester United and Marseille target Mason Greenwood, as a priority reinforcement for his attack, and the club lodged at least three separate offers for the winger. The last, according to Italian reports, was worth around €46m — well short of what Al-Hilal was ultimately prepared to pay.

It is the second big miss of the window for Gasperini's rebuild, with Roma sources describing Summerville as exactly the kind of direct, pacy wide player the coach wanted to add before the market shuts.

Summerville, 24, made his name at Feyenoord before four seasons in England, first at Leeds United and then West Ham, where he made 34 appearances last season. He also featured for the Netherlands at this summer's World Cup.
"Hi, Crysencio Summerville here. I can't wait to meet the Al Hilal fans, and my teammates, and can't wait to get started," he said in a message posted by the club alongside the announcement.

For Al-Hilal, already stocked with marquee arrivals in recent windows, the Summerville deal — and the cheeky campaign built around it — is the latest reminder of the financial gap the Saudi Pro League can now open on Serie A when it decides it wants a player badly enough.

title: Ironi Tiberias scrape past Sakhnin in Toto Cup opener, but admit: 'it can't continue like this'
dek: A dramatic late turnaround gave the crisis-hit club something to celebrate, but with the head coach and five players suspended in Israel's doping investigation, officials say the situation cannot go on much longer.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Sport5 - preview of the crisis before the Sakhnin game
Haaretz - coach and five players suspended over banned infusions
Ynet - livegame page for the match

body: Ironi Tiberias opened their Toto Cup campaign with a scrappy, ultimately satisfying 2-1 comeback win over Bnei Sakhnin on Saturday, but there was little of the usual pre-season swagger around the club. The team that took the field was patched together from academy kids, foreign trialists and whoever else was still allowed to train, after a doping scandal gutted the squad's leadership just weeks before the new season.

Sakhnin struck first, with Iyad Abu Abeid putting the visitors ahead in the 37th minute. Tiberias needed until the 75th minute to draw level through Ron Unger, and it was Mansour Badji who completed the turnaround just two minutes later to seal the win, according to ONE's report on the match.

Unger, who scored the equalizer, made clear afterwards who the win was really for. "We won also for the suspended coach and players," he said, according to ONE — a line that captured the mood inside a dressing room missing several of its senior figures.

Head coach Eliran Hodeda did not take his place on the touchline. He and five players are among those suspended after Israel's anti-doping authority opened a case into allegedly prohibited intravenous infusions at the club, a scandal that has been reported extensively by Haaretz, Walla Sport, Ynet, Kan and N12 since it broke in early July. Prosecutors in the case have asked for bans ranging from several years to lifetime suspensions for those implicated.

Among those sidelined alongside Hodeda are technical director Chen Sol and captain Guy Hadida, with several other players — including Sambinya, Niv Gotlieb and David Kaltins — also removed from the squad while their own cases are decided, according to Sport5's pre-match report. Loaned player Sameer Parhoud is serving a suspension too.

With the coach unavailable, it fell to assistant Moti Krispil to run the team from the sidelines against Sakhnin. Tiberias were also without left-back Gal Meatuok, who is said to be in separate transfer talks away from the club.

The numbers crunch left Tiberias fielding four foreign players and five academy graduates in a Toto Cup fixture that would normally be used to fine-tune a settled group. New signing Chris Quako started at center-back, with young defender Nahorai Chen also given minutes, per Sport5.

A club official captured the strain of preparing a competitive squad under the circumstances before the match: "It's a crazy situation, the struggle is difficult beyond description. Mentally, holding the players in this situation is hard in itself. The coach is removed, the players' best friends are removed, it hurts professional preparations and only distances players from focusing on football," the official said, according to Sport5.

That same source found a silver lining of sorts, framing the depleted squad as a chance for fringe players to force their way into the picture — an opportunity Tiberias will need several of them to take if the club's suspended figures remain out for any length of time.

For now, a first Toto Cup win offers Tiberias a rare piece of good news in an otherwise turbulent close season. But as Unger's dedication to the absent coach and players made plain, the club knows the underlying problem has not gone away — and, as officials have signalled, results alone will not paper over a situation they say simply cannot continue as it is.

body: Hapoel Umm al-Fahm have gone shopping a long way from home to strengthen their attack for the coming Liga Alef North season, confirming the signing of forward Yishai Buzorgui on a one-year deal, ONE reports.

The 24-year-old arrives from Maccabi Ata Bialik, where he scored eight goals last season, and brings a surname well known in Israeli football circles: Buzorgui is part of a Kiryat Shmona footballing family whose father, Yitzhak, played for Hapoel Kiryat Shmona, and whose brother Alon has also worn the club's colours.

The move to the Wadi Ara club is something of a homecoming for Buzorgui within the division. According to ONE, this will be his fourth stop in Liga Alef North, and he already has local history with the town — he had a brief spell with crosstown rivals Maccabi Umm al-Fahm two seasons ago.

title: Chelsea beat Arsenal to Morgan Rogers in British transfer record
dek: A personal phone call from new manager Xabi Alonso swung a £117 million deal for the Aston Villa forward, according to ONE, leaving Arsenal to look elsewhere.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Sky Sports
ESPN
Chelsea FC (official)

body: Chelsea have won the race for Morgan Rogers, completing a British transfer-record deal for the Aston Villa forward after seeing off a determined chase from Arsenal, ONE reports.

The fee is worth £117 million, according to ONE and multiple English outlets, eclipsing the £116m Manchester City paid Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson earlier this month and making the 23-year-old the most expensive British player in history.
Rogers has signed a seven-year contract at Stamford Bridge running to 2033, with Chelsea's official site confirming the deal on Tuesday after talks that ONE says came together in less than 48 hours.

Arsenal had been quietly favourites for weeks and held long-standing contact with Villa, but ONE reports the Gunners were only willing to value Rogers at around £80m — well short of what Chelsea ultimately paid.

The decisive moment, per ONE's reporting, came when new Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso placed a personal call to Rogers laying out his tactical plans for the player, an approach other English outlets have since corroborated as pivotal in turning his head away from north London.

Rogers is also said to have been drawn by the prospect of reuniting with close friend Cole Palmer, with ONE reporting that Chelsea players took an active role in encouraging the move behind the scenes.

With Villa needing a major sale to stay compliant with Financial Fair Play rules, the England international becomes the headline arrival of Alonso's first summer rebuild at Stamford Bridge, following the earlier signings of Marco Palestra and Geovany Quenda.

Rogers only moved to Villa Park from Middlesbrough for a reported £15m in February 2024, but his rise since has been rapid: 40 goals in 85 Premier League appearances, a PFA Young Player of the Year award, an England call-up, and a Europa League triumph with Villa last season.
Unai Emery had handed Rogers a new contract as recently as November — his third extension in under two years — underlining how highly Villa rated him before financial pressures forced their hand.

Arsenal, still chasing further reinforcements this summer, are reported by ONE to have kept alternative targets under consideration throughout the pursuit, including Julián Álvarez, Bradley Barcola and Eli Kroupi, as insurance against missing out on Rogers.

For Chelsea, the deal underlines the scale of Alonso's ambitions in his opening window in charge — and gives Palmer a familiar face and a versatile new attacking outlet as the Blues shape their squad for the season ahead.

title: De la Fuente says the World Cup belongs to a 'wonderful' Spain, not to him
dek: A week after becoming the oldest coach to win a World Cup, Luis de la Fuente tells ONE why he bristles at being called the tournament's own — and why nobody in his squad gets a place for free.

verificationSources.label: ONE
France 24 — World Cup 2026 final report
FIFA.com — Spain 1-0 Argentina report and highlights
ESPN — De la Fuente's team ethos won the World Cup for Spain

body: Ten days after Spain lifted the World Cup, Luis de la Fuente is still trying to deflect the spotlight away from himself and onto the players who won it. Asked in an interview with ONE about the growing habit of calling the tournament "his" World Cup, the 65-year-old coach did not hide his discomfort.

"It makes me blush," De la Fuente told ONE, "but I want to remind everyone this is the World Cup of a wonderful national team." It is the kind of answer that has defined his four years in charge — credit pushed outward, rarely inward.

The numbers behind that modesty are startling. Spain conceded just a single goal across the entire tournament and, according to De la Fuente's own account to ONE, faced only around ten shots on target in eight matches — a defensive record no previous champion has matched. He described 52 days on the road, from base camp to final, without a single internal problem disrupting the group.

The trophy itself was won the hard way. Spain beat holders Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19, with Ferran Torres converting from close range 39 seconds into the second period of extra time to break a stubborn Argentina side down to ten men. It was Torres' only goal of the tournament, and the third World Cup goal of his career.

The win made Spain champions for the second time, sixteen years after their maiden triumph in 2010, and completed a rare Euro-World Cup double following their 2024 European Championship win. It also made La Roja the first nation to hold both the men's and women's World Cup at once, with the women's team having won in 2023, and it made De la Fuente, at 65, the oldest coach ever to guide a team to the men's title.

In the interview, De la Fuente singled out his youngest players for praise. He described the contributions of Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí — both still teenagers during the tournament — as central to the way Spain played, combining defensive discipline with the attacking freedom that has become the team's trademark under him.

He also used the platform to defend Ferran Torres, who arrived at the tournament under heavy criticism from pundits and supporters over his club form, only to score the goal that decided the final. For De la Fuente, that arc is proof of a coaching philosophy he says is non-negotiable.

"No one has a fixed place, regardless of how long they have been here," he told ONE, explaining that even senior figures such as goalkeeper are picked on current form and consistency rather than reputation. He said his selection decisions are guided by "fairness and honesty, not by names or by age."

Character, he added, matters as much to him as ability — a principle he said applies as much to established internationals like Martín Zubimendi, Éric García, Álvaro Morata and Dani Carvajal as it does to the tournament's breakout stars.

For a coach who has now won a European Championship and a World Cup back to back, De la Fuente's insistence on sharing the credit is unlikely to be taken at face value by everyone in Spain. But as he made clear to ONE, it is the version of the story he intends to keep telling.

title: Barcelona fear losing World Cup hero Ferran Torres as PSG circle
dek: The Spanish forward, fresh off scoring Spain's extra-time World Cup final winner, is stalling over a new Camp Nou contract while Paris Saint-Germain push hard for his signature, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE — "החלוץ מתלבט: ברצלונה חוששת לאבד את פראן טורס"
Yahoo Sports — Barcelona prepare for Ferran Torres exit amid PSG interest
Barca Universal — Barcelona move to keep Spain World Cup hero Ferran Torres amid PSG interest
ESPN — Spain hero Ferran Torres on World Cup winning goal

body: Barcelona have a problem entirely of the good kind: one of their forwards just scored the goal that won Spain the World Cup, and now everybody wants him. ONE reports that the club is increasingly anxious it could lose Ferran Torres, with the 26-year-old still undecided over a new contract at Camp Nou and Paris Saint-Germain waiting in the wings.

Torres's current deal runs only until June 2027, and according to the report he has yet to give Barcelona a positive answer on an extension the club has already put on the table. That hesitation has not gone unnoticed in Paris — PSG have registered serious interest and, per the report, are able to offer financial terms Barcelona simply cannot match given their ongoing wage constraints under La Liga's financial fair play rules.

Adding to the complication, extending Torres's contract would trigger an additional payment of around €8 million ($9m) owed to his former club, Manchester City, under the terms of his 2022 transfer to Barcelona — a bonus clause tied to the length of his stay that further squeezes an already tight budget.

ONE's report ties Torres's mood in part to Barcelona's parallel pursuit of a new No. 9. The club has made Atletico Madrid's Julián Álvarez their priority target to solve a long-running centre-forward problem, and Torres is said to be uneasy about a move that would again push him toward the margins of the attack rather than through the middle, where he has increasingly established himself.

The timing could hardly be more pointed. Torres was Spain's unlikely hero in the 2026 World Cup final on July 19, scoring the extra-time winner in a 1-0 victory over Argentina at New Jersey's MetLife-area venue to give Spain their second world title. The goal, struck from inside the box in the 106th minute after Argentina had been reduced to ten men, transformed a player who had spent much of the tournament fighting for a starting shirt into a national hero.

It capped a strong individual season for Torres at club level too: 21 goals and three assists in 49 appearances for Barcelona, including 16 La Liga goals — a tally that made him Spain's top-scoring player in the division last season, level with teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.

None of that has settled his future. PSG's approach is said to include direct contact from manager Luis Enrique, who knows Torres well from his time overseeing the Spanish national team set-up and has been personally selling the Parisian project to the forward.

Barcelona's dilemma, as ONE frames it, is stark: risk losing a player who has just become a World Cup winner for nothing next summer, or cash in now while his value — freshly inflated by that final goal — is at its peak. Neither option sits comfortably with a club that would clearly prefer to build around him.

For now, nothing is resolved. Torres has not rejected Barcelona's offer outright, nor has he committed to it, and the report stresses this remains a genuine dilemma rather than a done deal in either direction. But with PSG circling and Barcelona's own transfer business complicating matters further, the coming weeks look set to decide where one of the World Cup's biggest breakout stars plays his club football next season.
