title: Robi Shapira Haifa's youth B side crowned Gulf League champions in a double-title season
dek: Mohamed Badran's goals help power a squad built almost from scratch to the Ligat Mafraz crown, completing a rare double for the fan-founded Haifa club alongside its Youth Gimel side's Northern League triumph.

verificationSources.label: ONE report on Robi Shapira Haifa's Youth B Gulf League title
Junior League: Fuad Diab on Robi Shapira's double championship season
Israel Football Association club page for M.S. Robi Shapira Haifa

body: M.S. Robi Shapira Haifa's Youth B team has been crowned champions of the Gulf League, known in Hebrew as Ligat Mafraz, ONE reports -- the second age-group title of the season for a Haifa club built from a fan initiative barely a decade ago.

The numbers behind the run were emphatic. The Youth B squad finished with 15 wins, four draws and just a single defeat from 20 league matches, a record that also delivered the division's most productive attack, with 66 goals scored, and its second-stingiest defense.

Much of the firepower came from Mohamed Badran, a striker who arrived at the club only after the season was already under way and still finished with 18 goals. Faisal Hijazi chipped in another 10, while defender Mohamed Alissa anchored the back line and goalkeeper Mohamed Subah marshaled the box.

Subah's season did not stop there. According to both ONE and a separate Junior League report, the goalkeeper also turned out for the club's Youth Gimel team, which was busy compiling its own title elsewhere in the age groups.

That Youth Gimel side won the Northern League with a remarkable 20 wins from 21 matches, per Junior League, with striker Fuad Diab -- who joined Robi Shapira from Hapoel Haifa last summer -- finishing as the division's top scorer on 28 goals in 18 appearances. Diab also found time to make 11 appearances and score once for the Youth B team during its title push.

"This is an amazing feeling, hard to describe in words. I'm very proud of what we accomplished as a team," Diab told Junior League, singling out the match that clinched the Northern League title against Ma'alot Tarshiha, where he scored and set up a goal, as a moment he will not forget.

Both title-winning age groups now earn promotion to their respective National League divisions for the 2026/27 season, a significant step up for a club that only fielded its first youth teams a decade ago.

Mohamed Bukai, who coached the Youth B champions, credited the scale of the rebuild behind the title. "We constructed an entirely new squad," he said, according to ONE. "Bringing players to a regional-league club without a senior team proved extremely difficult."

M.S. Robi Shapira Haifa grew out of a supporters' initiative founded by Hapoel Haifa fans in the mid-2010s and carries the name of Robi Shapira, the businessman who once owned Hapoel Haifa and built its youth setup into one of the largest in northern Israel. The academy itself was taken over three years ago by coach Baruch Saer, and Bukai is already planning a training camp in Eilat this August to prepare his newly promoted side for life in the National League.

title: Maccabi Haifa confirm Yermakov's exit as Metalist Kharkiv move nears
dek: The Ukrainian goalkeeper is set for a medical before completing his move to Metalist Kharkiv, with Omri Glazer lined up to return to Haifa from Red Star Belgrade.

body: Maccabi Haifa have made it official: goalkeeper Georgiy Yermakov is on his way out of the club, ONE reports, with his move to Ukrainian side Metalist Kharkiv now approaching its final stages.

The club's own send-off was brief and warm. "Thank you Giorgi! We wish you success on your way," Maccabi Haifa said in a statement carried by ONE, closing the book on a stay that lasted barely a year.

According to the report, Yermakov is due to undergo a medical early next week before putting pen to paper on his contract with Metalist. The formalities aside, the substance of the deal has already been thrashed out between the two clubs.

Yermakov arrived at Sammy Ofer Stadium in July 2025 from Oleksandriya for a modest fee of around €100,000, having just been named the outstanding goalkeeper of the 2024/25 Ukrainian Premier League season. Haifa saw him as a long-term successor between the posts; instead, he is leaving after a single campaign.

The numbers around the departure have shifted in the retelling. Ynet reported the Metalist deal is worth in the region of €4 million, including a sell-on percentage for Haifa on any future transfer, while Walla! Sport had earlier described the Israeli club demanding closer to €5 million against bids nearer €2.5 million before the two sides found common ground.

Walla! also reported that Yermakov himself pushed hard for the exit, telling owner Yaakov Shahar directly that he wanted to leave — and that, unlike in previous transfer windows, he was no longer ruling out a return to Ukrainian football to get it done.

Born in Kyiv in 2002, Yermakov moved to Israel with his family, who have Jewish roots, as the war with Russia unfolded, before rebuilding his career through Shakhtar Donetsk's system and then Oleksandriya on the way to his move to Haifa.

Maccabi Haifa are not left short-handed. The club has already lined up Omri Glazer to return from Red Star Belgrade, with Ynet reporting the Israeli international will undergo his own medical before signing a three-year contract in Haifa.

Glazer's homecoming carries its own history: he first played for Maccabi Haifa in the 2020/21 season under Barak Bakhar, the coach still in charge today, before moving on to Hapoel Beer Sheva and then to Red Star in 2023, where recent seasons had reduced him to a fringe role behind the Serbian club's first-choice goalkeeper.
With Yermakov's exit now confirmed and Glazer's return in motion, Haifa's goalkeeping department is being rebuilt around a familiar face just as pre-season preparations intensify.

title: Ganem leads a threadbare Tiberias attack as Sakhnin visit for the Toto Cup opener
dek: Ironi Tiberias began their season at Barel Stadium missing five suspended players and their coach, with new signing Kais Ganem thrown straight into the XI against Bnei Sakhnin.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Sport5 - Tiberias prepares for Sakhnin

body: Ironi Tiberias opened their 2026/27 campaign on Saturday evening the way the club would rather have avoided the headlines entirely: with a threadbare starting XI, a caretaker on the bench and a season already overshadowed by a doping investigation. Bnei Sakhnin were the visitors at Barel Stadium for the opening round of the Toto Cup, and ONE reports new forward Kais Ganem was handed the No. 9 shirt to lead the home attack.

Ganem's arrival was meant to be the good news of Tiberias's off-season. The club announced his signing from Moldova's Sheriff Tiraspol after previous spells in Israel with Hapoel Tel Aviv, Hapoel Beer Sheva and Hapoel Haifa, and Israel Hayom had billed his return to the top flight as a boost up front. Instead he took the field as one of the more experienced faces in a squad gutted by suspensions.

At the other end, Sakhnin's XI carried a familiar, more settled look. ONE's lineup sheet has Eyad Abu Abed starting in central defence alongside Maron Gantous, shielding goalkeeper Raoul Balbrau, with Mateo Cujo and Norberto Carlos anchoring midfield and Ahmad Ibrahim among the attacking options.

The backdrop to Tiberias's weakened team is the club's ongoing "banned infusions" case. Israel's national anti-doping authority provisionally suspended head coach Eliran Chodida and five players — goalkeeper David Klatins, captain Guy Hadida, Niv Gutlib, Sembinya and Yonatan Tafer — on July 5, after Maccabi Ashdod lodged a complaint on June 21 alleging Tiberias players received saline infusions beyond the volume permitted under anti-doping protocol before a league match between the two clubs.

Prosecutors are reportedly seeking sanctions ranging from six years' suspension to a lifetime ban for those implicated, according to Ynet. Tiberias has rejected the allegations, maintaining the infusions were administered within permitted limits and under professional supervision. No final ruling has been issued, and the suspensions handed down so far are provisional rather than findings of guilt.

The practical effect on Saturday was a matchday squad built almost from scratch. Sport5 reported that with the suspended players and coaching staff unavailable, Tiberias could name only four foreign players and five academy graduates among their options, with senior staff stepping in on an interim basis to run preparations and training in Chodida's absence.

Against that backdrop, both promoted-era northern clubs were simply chasing a winning start to the new season in the Toto Cup's regional group stage — for Tiberias, a rare piece of straightforward sporting business in a summer that has been anything but.

title: Hapoel Tel Aviv keeping tabs on Sylvain Francisco as Villeurbanne's finances unravel
dek: The Israeli champions are said to be monitoring the French guard's situation after ASVEL Villeurbanne slashed its budget by more than half, though Francisco previously turned down a move to Israel over security concerns

verificationSources.label: Sport5 report
Eurohoops: Panathinaikos monitoring Francisco amid ASVEL budget crisis

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have not stopped watching Sylvain Francisco, according to a Sport5 report, with the club said to be tracking a financial crisis at ASVEL Villeurbanne that could put the French guard back on the market barely weeks after he signed there.

Francisco, 28, joined Tony Parker's club this summer after triggering a buyout clause to leave Zalgiris Kaunas, agreeing what was reported as a lucrative three-year deal worth around €4.1 million a season. Villeurbanne still owed Zalgiris a €400,000 release fee for the move, and Sport5 reports that payment deadline passed four days ago without the money arriving.

The reason, according to the report, is a dramatic collapse in ASVEL's finances. The Lyon-area club had built its 2026-27 planning around a record €59 million budget, but has now submitted a backup file to France's financial regulator built around roughly €24 million, after funding expected from an Asian investor failed to materialize on schedule. Eurohoops and other French outlets have separately reported the same budget figures in recent days.

With Villeurbanne's ability to honor Francisco's contract now in doubt, several EuroLeague clubs are said to be circling. Sport5 names Panathinaikos and Dubai alongside Hapoel Tel Aviv as suitors monitoring developments, a list that partly overlaps with reporting elsewhere naming Panathinaikos as an active tracker of the situation.

Wattakis is reported to have cited both Zalgiris sources and Francisco's agent, Nikos Spanos, though he stressed the information was fresh and urged caution about treating it as settled.

Francisco arrived at Zalgiris in 2024 and quickly became one of the EuroLeague's most productive guards, averaging over 16 points and close to seven assists a game last season and earning All-EuroLeague First Team recognition before making the jump to Villeurbanne.

He is also believed to retain a separate NBA exit option in his ASVEL contract, giving him a further window to weigh his future even as the club scrambles to stabilize its budget before the new season.

Nothing has been confirmed by Hapoel Tel Aviv, and Sport5's own framing treats the Israeli club's renewed interest as speculative rather than an active negotiation. Whether a security-related refusal that held once still applies if Villeurbanne's project collapses entirely remains an open question the report does not answer.

title: Israel's under-16 water polo team open the World Championship with a win over South Africa
dek: Yahli Rokach starred as Israel rallied from an early deficit to beat South Africa 12-7 at Zagreb's Mladost pool, opening the group stage of the World Aquatics Women's U16 Championships.

body: Israel's under-16 women's water polo team could not have asked for a better start to their World Championship. In their opening group game in Zagreb, the young Israelis beat South Africa 12-7, according to Sport5, giving the squad an immediate lift at the start of an unforgiving group.

The game did not begin the way Israel wanted. South Africa raced out to an early 2-0 lead, catching the Israeli side cold in front of a packed opening-day crowd at the Mladost pool complex on the shores of Jarun Lake.

Israel settled quickly, though, and turned the match around before the first break. By halftime the score had flipped to 6-4 in Israel's favour, and a dominant third quarter — won 10-5 on the day's cumulative tally — put the result beyond reasonable doubt.

Yahli Rokach was named player of the match after finishing as the game's joint-top scorer alongside Uri Grodman, both netting three goals. Yara Huvino Garcia added two more, with Tamara Salmon Michaeli, Inbar Yanko, Alma Tauber and Tamar Orhan each scoring once, Sport5 reported.

The victory came on the opening day of the World Aquatics Women's U16 Water Polo Championships, running from July 25 to July 31 in Zagreb. The Croatian capital is hosting both the men's and women's under-16 editions this summer, with roughly 60 national teams passing through the Mladost venue.
Israel's group is one of the tournament's toughest: alongside South Africa, the team has been drawn with Hungary, one of the traditional powers of women's water polo, plus Mexico and the Netherlands.

"The excitement at the start was evident, and once the girls settled down they showed they're better," head coach Idan Kaftori said after the win, according to Sport5. "Tomorrow we have a super tough match against Hungary, one of the gold medal contenders."
Israel Water Polo Association chairwoman Rona Freund-Amitzur hailed what she called a confidence-building win to open the tournament, Sport5 reported.
Israel's youngsters return to the pool against Hungary next, before closing out the group phase against Mexico and the Netherlands.

body: Hapoel Beer Sheva have officially confirmed that Kings Kangwa is leaving for Panathinaikos, ending months of speculation over the Zambian playmaker's future and delivering the club a windfall as they push for a domestic title defence and a run in Europe.

The Greek club will pay in the region of €3.8 million up front, with add-ons that ONE reports could push the total package to about €4.5 million once bonuses are triggered. It is comfortably the biggest sale in the Israeli club's recent history.

Kangwa will stay with Beer Sheva just long enough to play the return leg of their Champions League qualifying tie against Icelandic champions Vikingur Reykjavik, before flying to Greece for a medical and to put pen to paper on his contract, according to Ynet.

Under UEFA registration rules, he will not be eligible to appear for Panathinaikos until the competition reaches its group stage, so the Greeks are banking on a slower burn rather than an instant impact.

The move came together only after Panathinaikos saw off competition from fellow Greek side AEK Athens, who had also tabled roughly €4 million for the 27-year-old but wanted him to report immediately. Beer Sheva, weighing up their own European fixture list, prioritised the buyer willing to wait.

Kangwa's stock has never been higher. He was named the Israeli Premier League's Best Player of the Season last term, finishing with 12 goals and 9 assists in 21 league appearances and topping the division for successful key passes per 90 minutes, per ONE's reporting on his campaign.
That form underpinned Beer Sheva's title triumph, the club's first championship in eight years, with Kangwa directly involved in roughly a quarter of the team's league goals along the way.

A 43-cap Zambia international, Kangwa arrived in Israel after two spells in eastern Europe, including a run at Red Star Belgrade where he won back-to-back domestic doubles before his move to Beer Sheva.

Greek outlets have already previewed what Panathinaikos are getting: an attacking midfielder capable of what local media there describe as bursting into space and creating chances for teammates in the final third, rather than a pure goalscorer.

For Beer Sheva, the immediate priority remains sporting rather than financial — closing out the tie against Vikingur Reykjavik, in which Kangwa scored their goal in a 2-1 first-leg defeat, before waving off their star man to Athens.

title: Xavi Simons breaks silence on Barcelona exit: 'They didn't believe in me'
dek: The Tottenham midfielder says a lack of faith at Barcelona, not money, pushed him to Paris Saint-Germain in 2019, as he presses on with his recovery from a serious knee injury.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Barca Universal
Sky Sports (ACL injury)

body: Seven years on, Xavi Simons has finally said his piece about the messiest exit of his career. Speaking as he works his way back from a serious knee injury and prepares for his second season at Tottenham Hotspur, the Dutch playmaker addressed head-on the acrimonious 2019 departure from Barcelona's academy that shaped the rest of his career.

"It was clear from the beginning that they did not believe in me," Simons said, recalling the conversation that ended his time at La Masia. "At the time I decided not to speak because I was focused only on the pitch."

According to Simons, the club's message was blunt. "We have other players that we believe in, we want to offer you a contract, but you are not one of the players who is really part of the project," he was told, effectively closing the door on a first-team future at Camp Nou.

What stung more than the rejection itself, he said, was the version of events that followed him for years afterwards: that money, not football reasoning, had driven his move to Paris Saint-Germain. "Stories came out saying that I was leaving for money," Simons said. "I love Barcelona and that version of events hurt me and it also hurt my family, because it was not true."

For a player who had spent his youth inside Barcelona's system, the suggestion that he had simply chased a bigger paycheck cut deep. Simons has consistently maintained that the decision came down to opportunity rather than finance — PSG offered him a route into senior football that Barcelona, by its own admission, was not prepared to guarantee.

That route proved eventful. As a 16-year-old in Paris, Simons trained alongside Lionel Messi, Neymar and Kylian Mbappé, an experience he has previously described as invaluable to his development, even as his path through PSG's first team never fully materialized before loan spells took him elsewhere.

His career found its rhythm at RB Leipzig, first on loan and then permanently from January 2024, where his form as a creative midfielder made him one of the Bundesliga's most sought-after players. Tottenham moved decisively last year, signing him from Leipzig in August 2025 in a deal reported by ESPN and Sky Sports at around £51 million.

The reflection on Barcelona comes at a difficult moment for Simons physically. In April 2026, he ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Tottenham's Premier League win at Wolverhampton Wanderers, going down in the second half and eventually being stretchered off Molineux.

The injury ended his season and, more painfully, ruled him out of the 2026 World Cup with the Netherlands — a tournament he had been expected to play a central role in. He underwent surgery in the weeks that followed and has since been working through rehabilitation with Tottenham's medical staff.

Now, with his sights set on returning for what would be his second full season in north London, Simons appears keen to put both the injury and the old Barcelona narrative behind him — closing the book on a departure that, in his telling, was never about money at all.

body: Atlético Madrid confirmed on Saturday that they have completed the signing of Lee Kang-in from Paris Saint-Germain, ending weeks of speculation and returning the South Korean playmaker to Spain three years after he left La Liga for Ligue 1.

The 25-year-old has signed a contract running through June 2031, according to the club's announcement, and will wear the number 7 shirt at the Metropolitano — a jersey Atlético have traditionally reserved for a player they view as central to their attack.

ONE put the transfer fee at around €40 million, a figure broadly consistent with other reporting on the deal, which was agreed directly between the two clubs rather than through a loan or add-on-heavy structure.

Lee becomes the first South Korean to join one of La Liga's traditional 'big three' — Real Madrid, Barcelona or Atlético — a milestone Korean outlets have been quick to celebrate as a landmark for the country's football.

He leaves Paris on the back of a hugely productive spell: 124 appearances, 16 goals and 16 assists since arriving from Mallorca in the summer of 2023, on top of back-to-back UEFA Champions League titles with PSG.

Before that, Lee came through Valencia's youth academy, making his name in Spain as a teenager before the move to Mallorca and, eventually, the switch to Paris that established him as one of Asian football's most sought-after attacking midfielders.

ONE's report also cited Fabrizio Romano in linking Paris Saint-Germain with a very different kind of midfield addition — an approach for Manchester City's Rodri. The suggestion is that PSG had not planned to prioritise a holding midfielder this window but see Rodri's unresolved contract situation as an opportunity too good to pass up.

That Rodri strand is considerably less settled than the confirmed Lee deal. Much of the recent reporting elsewhere has instead linked Rodri with a return to Spain via Real Madrid, with club president Florentino Pérez said to have taken fresh interest after watching the Spaniard win the 2026 World Cup. Rodri's City contract runs to 2027, and no formal move in either direction has been agreed.

Manchester City, meanwhile, have been busy on other fronts: the club has tied Uzbek defender Abdukodir Khusanov to a new deal through 2031 and is pursuing Chelsea's Pedro Neto, part of a busy window in which Atlético's capture of Lee is, for now, the only one of these stories actually over the line.

title: Israel's U18s edge past Greece in overtime to open EuroBasket campaign

body: Israel's under-18 national team needed extra time to get its European Championship campaign off the ground, but the result was worth the nerves: a 93-84 overtime win over Greece in the group phase opener of the FIBA U18 EuroBasket in Rovereto, Italy.

It was not a comfortable afternoon. Head coach Nadav Zilberstein told ONE that his team looked tense in the opening five minutes before settling into the game, and that the defense tightened notably after the break — improvement that ultimately carried Israel through a extra period against a Greek side that pushed the game to the wire.

The individual story of the day was Aviv Aronov, who scored 30 points and, speaking to ONE afterward, called it the sweetest win of his young career. He said the group had faced significant protests directed at Israel around the tournament, but that the players had stayed unified and focused squarely on performing for their country rather than being knocked off course.

Zilberstein was already looking past the celebration by the time he spoke to reporters. According to ONE, the coach said the squad's attention had turned immediately to Sunday's group game against France, with no time set aside to dwell on the win over Greece.

The FIBA U18 EuroBasket 2026 is being staged across Trento and Rovereto from July 25 to August 2, with Israel drawn in a group phase pool that also includes Greece and Austria. Saturday's win puts Israel on the board before the France game, the next test of a group phase that will decide seeding for the knockout rounds.

Aronov arrives at the tournament as one of Israel's most-watched prospects: FIBA had flagged him among the players to watch heading into the championship, built on his production for Israel's side at the U16 EuroBasket in 2024. The 30-point overtime haul against Greece was his most significant showing yet at this age group.
For now, both coach and star player were keeping the message simple — a hard-fought win banked, and straight on to the next assignment against France with the group phase still to be decided.

body: Barak Bakhar has named his Maccabi Haifa starting eleven for Saturday evening's Haifa derby against Hapoel Haifa, and the headline is not just who is playing but who is wearing the armband: goalkeeper Omri Glazer starts as captain in the Toto Cup opener at Sammy Ofer Stadium, kick-off 20:30.

Glazer's captaincy is a late change forced by injury rather than a settled plan. According to Sport5, defender Pedrão had been pencilled in to lead the side, but a scan on the morning of the match revealed a small tear in his groin muscle, ruling him out and sending him straight into rehabilitation. Glazer, who returned to Maccabi Haifa this summer for a second spell at the club and signed a three-year deal, takes the armband in his stead.

The goalkeeper's recall between the posts was already effectively confirmed before Pedrão's issue emerged. Reserve keeper Sheriff Kayouf was injured in a warm-up friendly against Hapoel Kfar Sava and requires surgery that is expected to keep him out for the rest of the season, leaving Glazer as the clear senior option heading into the new campaign.

Further forward, two of the summer's new faces get their first taste of the fixture. Yair Mordechai, a 22-year-old who arrived on a free transfer from Ironi Kiryat Shmona for a modest development fee after a breakout Ligat Ha'al season, makes his official Maccabi Haifa debut having caught the eye in pre-season friendlies. Yarin Levi also starts, back in green after a two-year loan spell at Beitar Jerusalem.

ONE reports the confirmed Maccabi Haifa XI as: Omri Glazer; Zohar Zasno, Guni Naor, Noam Steifman, Shon Goldberg; Yarin Levi, Eitan Azulai, Yair Mordechai; Iyad Khalaili, Cédric Don and Adam Grimberg, with Don and Grimberg leading the attacking line and Azulai deployed in a linking role between midfield and attack.

There is a human-interest wrinkle in defence. Guni Naor had reportedly been told by the club that he is not part of the plans for next season, according to Maariv's Sport1, yet he was registered for the derby and starts after Pedrão's late withdrawal opened up a spot.

The fixture is the first round of the 2026/27 Toto Cup and doubles as Maccabi Haifa's opening competitive test of the season after a summer of upheaval that included training camps in Hungary and six significant signings to the squad.

History favours the Greens. In their most recent meeting, Maccabi Haifa beat Hapoel Haifa 2-0, and they have won five of the last ten derbies between the two Haifa clubs — a record Bakhar's side will look to extend as they open their season in front of their own supporters.

title: Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem seal historic first European win
dek: Jaielly's early strike sinks Montenegrin champions Budućnost Podgorica as Israel's women's champions record their maiden victory in continental competition.

verificationSources.label: Sport5 report

body: Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem, Israel's reigning women's football champions, wrote a new chapter in the country's sporting history on Saturday, beating two-time Montenegrin champions Budućnost Podgorica 1-0 in a UEFA Women's Champions League qualifying match in Greece — the first European victory an Israeli women's champion club has ever recorded.

The only goal came early. Brazilian forward Jaielly converted in the seventh minute, finishing off a pass from Michaela Warko, and the Jerusalem side held that lead for the remaining 83 minutes against a Budućnost team that arrived at the mini-tournament shaken.

Saturday's game was a classification match rather than a step toward the group stage — Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem's route forward had already ended three days earlier, when they lost 3-1 to hosts PAOK Thessaloniki in Wednesday's opening round. Sport5, which broke the news, called the Budućnost result "consolation of historic proportions": the club's first competitive win at senior European level.

Budućnost themselves had arrived out of sorts. The Podgorica club, Montenegrin champions in each of the last two seasons, had been eliminated from the same group-stage path a day earlier, beaten on penalties by Azerbaijan's Neftçi Baku after 120 goalless minutes.

For Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem the result carries weight beyond the scoreline. A first competitive European win should register in UEFA's coefficient calculations for Israeli women's football, the rankings that help determine how many places — and at what stage — Israeli clubs enter future editions of the Women's Champions League.

It caps a rapid rise for the fan-owned Jerusalem club, whose senior women's section has existed in its current form only since 2020. After two runner-up finishes in the Israeli league and a first trophy, the Athena Cup, in 2023-24, Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem finally won the domestic title in 2025-26 — opening the door to this, their first continental campaign.

That campaign is now over for the season, with the squad set to return home to prepare for the new Israeli league season. But the win in Greece leaves the club, and the wider Israeli women's game, with proof that a team playing its first European football can still leave the group with something to show for it.

body: Lazio are reportedly preparing to submit a formal offer for Stav Lemkin, with Sport5 reporting on Friday that the Rome club see the Israeli center-back as an option to strengthen their defence this summer.

Lemkin, 23, made his move to FC Twente permanent last summer, with the Dutch club paying Shakhtar Donetsk roughly €1.5 million for his signature after he had spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Maccabi Tel Aviv, where he first came through the youth ranks.

The defender went on to establish himself at Twente, making 29 appearances across the Eredivisie and Dutch Cup last season. He is under contract in Enschede through 2028 and is valued at around €6 million by Transfermarkt.
According to Sport5, Lemkin also holds Spanish citizenship, a detail that would ease any move to Serie A by sparing him a non-EU work-permit slot at Lazio.

Italian outlets have separately linked Lazio with Lemkin as a defensive option, though reporting from Lazionews.eu and TuttoMercatoWeb frames the interest as contingent on the club's ongoing negotiations to sell Alessio Romagnoli to Al Sadd — Lemkin would likely arrive only if that departure goes through.

Should the move materialise, Lemkin would become the third Israeli playing in Serie A this season, joining midfielder Omri Gandelman at Lecce and winger Manor Solomon, who has been on loan at Fiorentina.

Lemkin has represented Israel at senior level after coming through the country's youth national teams, and a switch to one of Italy's traditional clubs would mark a significant step up for the young defender.
Nothing is yet official on either side, and Twente have given no indication of willingness to sell a player who was a first-team regular for them last season.

title: Arsenal weigh audacious move for Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior
dek: Sport5, citing The Athletic's David Ornstein, reports the Premier League champions have internal backing to pursue the Brazilian winger if his Real Madrid contract talks stall.

body: Arsenal have identified Vinícius Júnior as a genuine summer target, with Sport5 reporting — citing The Athletic's David Ornstein — that the newly crowned Premier League champions are exploring a move for the Real Madrid and Brazil winger.

The interest is described as being at an early stage. No talks have taken place between the two clubs, but the idea already has "approval at all levels" inside the Emirates hierarchy, according to the report, meaning there is no guarantee it develops into an actual bid.

The timing is no coincidence. Arsenal have just sold Leandro Trossard to Beşiktaş and are watching Gabriel Martinelli's form dip well below the levels he showed a couple of seasons ago, leaving manager Mikel Arteta short of a genuine difference-maker out wide. The club did bring in Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge as extra depth, but he is not viewed as the marquee reinforcement the left flank still needs.

Vinícius, 26, is entering the final year of his Real Madrid contract, which runs until June 2027, and renewal talks with the club have not progressed. His camp is said to be seeking close to €30 million a year, while Real Madrid's improved offer sits nearer €25 million net per season — up from an earlier proposal of around €20 million.
Real Madrid are reportedly reluctant to risk losing him for nothing in 2027 and would be prepared to sanction a sale next summer if no new deal is signed, which is what has put Arsenal on alert.

Since arriving from Flamengo in the summer of 2018, Vinícius has made 375 appearances for Real Madrid, scoring 128 goals and adding 100 assists — a return that places him among the most productive attackers in Europe over the past several seasons.

He was among Real Madrid's most reliable performers again in 2025/26, scoring 22 goals and providing 14 assists in 53 appearances across all competitions, and he added four goals for Brazil during the World Cup.

Any move would still represent a significant financial stretch for Arsenal, who would likely need to break their existing wage structure to accommodate a player of Vinícius's profile and salary expectations. Real Madrid's clear priority, for now, remains keeping him at the Bernabéu.

Arsenal's aggressive approach to this transfer window has already been on display: they missed out on Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers, who instead moved to Chelsea in a deal reported at £117 million, underlining how seriously the champions are shopping for attacking reinforcements.

For now, this remains a name on Arsenal's wish list rather than a live negotiation — but with Vinícius's Real Madrid future genuinely uncertain for the first time in his career, it is a story worth watching closely as the window progresses.

body: Manchester City have thrown their hat into one of the most frenetic transfer chases of the European summer, according to a report by ONE, entering the race to sign RB Leipzig's teenage winger Yan Diomande.

Citing German journalist Philipp Hinze of Sky Sports Germany, ONE reports that City have verbally told Leipzig's leadership they are prepared to submit an offer worth around €100 million for the 19-year-old Ivorian, matching the sums already tabled by two of Europe's traditional heavyweights.

Both Real Madrid and Liverpool have already had bids in that region turned down by Leipzig this summer, with the Bundesliga club making clear that admiration for Diomande's talent runs well ahead of any willingness to sell on the cheap.

Leipzig's stance, according to multiple reports corroborating the ONE story, is that anything short of roughly €120 million is unlikely to shift a player they signed from Leganés for a reported €20 million only last year.
Paris Saint-Germain remain in the picture too, long seen as keen admirers of the winger, though no formal PSG bid has yet been confirmed to Leipzig.

For City, the interest fits a pattern: Pep Guardiola's side have repeatedly gone after young, explosive wide players in recent windows, and Diomande's blend of pace and end product has made him one of the most sought-after teenagers in Europe this year.

The winger enjoyed a breakout campaign in Leipzig colours, contributing 12 goals in the Bundesliga, before starring for Ivory Coast at the 2026 World Cup, where he was one of the tournament's most eye-catching young performers.

Nothing is close to done, however. City's approach, as described in the report, remains a verbal indication of intent rather than a submitted bid, and Leipzig have so far shown no sign of budging on their asking price for a player who still has years left on his contract.

title: Ninety minutes of frustration: the bind trapping Liel Abada in Charlotte
dek: The Israeli winger scored and drove Charlotte FC forward all night against Atlanta United, then was hooked before full time yet again — ONE reports it is now a settled pattern, not a one-off.

verificationSources.label: ONE - 90 דקות של תסכול: המלכוד של ליאל עבדה בארה"ב
Atlanta United FC - match recap, Charlotte FC 2-2 Atlanta United

body: Liel Abada was, on any honest reading of Tuesday night's scoreline, the best player on the pitch for Charlotte FC. He scored, he ran at Atlanta United's defence all evening, and he still didn't see out the 90 minutes — hauled off in the 63rd minute of a match his side led twice before somehow only drawing.

Charlotte had raced into a 2-0 lead at home in their first match back from the World Cup break, Kerwin Vargas opening the scoring before Abada doubled it, rising to head in a Pep Biel cross from the back post just before half-time. Atlanta United then clawed the game back, with a goal from Elías Báez and a Miguel Almirón strike in the 76th minute completing a 2-2 comeback. By then, ONE notes, Abada was already back on the bench — substituted with more than 25 minutes still to play despite being, in the outlet's words, the most prominent player on the pitch.

It is, according to ONE, a pattern rather than an anomaly. The Israeli outlet reports that since August 2025 the winger has started just seven league matches for Charlotte, accumulating only 624 minutes across that stretch. This season, ONE says, he has made ten appearances and started five of them — and been substituted before full time in every single one.
The numbers ONE lays out for his time in North Carolina overall are stark: across 78 appearances in Charlotte colours, Abada has been permitted to complete a full 90 minutes on only eight occasions.

Charlotte head coach Dean Smith has himself acknowledged the scrutiny around Abada. "I was really pleased for Liel last night because there's been some questions about him," Smith said after the Atlanta draw, according to The Charlotte Ledger, pointing to a spell in which Abada had not scored in league play since August 3, 2025 before Tuesday's header ended the drought.

That same report notes that clubs in England's Championship have been credited with interest in the 24-year-old designated player, and that Charlotte view a sale as realistic enough that it would free up a coveted DP slot for the club to reinvest elsewhere this summer.

ONE frames the underlying story as one of a talented player repeatedly caught in circumstances beyond his footballing control. It recalls that Abada's departure from Celtic was accelerated by the furore around Palestinian flags displayed by sections of the Celtic support, pushing him toward an unplanned move to MLS in 2024 rather than a more conventional European step up.

The outlet also reports that a move to a major German club broke down at a late stage after players in that squad objected to signing an Israeli international — one more instance, in ONE's telling, of Abada's career being shaped by forces well outside the width of a football pitch.

His Charlotte contract runs through December, with the club holding an option into 2027, according to Spotrac — meaning the club, not just suitors abroad, will have a say in how soon this chapter closes.

For now, the header against Atlanta was a reminder of why Charlotte paid a club-record fee to sign him in the first place. Whether it is enough to change how he is used, rather than simply how he is remembered, is the question ONE leaves hanging over the Israeli winger's American spell.

title: KuCoin becomes exclusive crypto partner of Pogačar's UAE Team Emirates at the Tour de France
dek: The exchange's branding has been riding on the team's buses and support cars throughout July as Tadej Pogačar closes in on a fifth Tour de France title.

body: Cryptocurrency exchange KuCoin has become the official and exclusive crypto partner of Tadej Pogačar's UAE Team Emirates-XRG, with the company's branding appearing across the team's buses, support vehicles and fleet cars throughout this year's Tour de France, Sport5 reported.

Under the deal, KuCoin holds exclusive rights in three categories: cryptocurrency exchanges, blockchain trading platforms and crypto wallet services, meaning no rival crypto brand can appear on the team's kit or vehicles for the duration of the agreement.

The sponsorship made its public debut this month as the world's biggest cycling race rolled out from Barcelona on July 4, giving KuCoin visibility on what the exchange itself called cycling's grandest stage.

The timing has proven especially valuable. Pogačar, the team's talisman, arrives at the race's final stage in Paris on Sunday with a commanding lead of 7:11 over Belgium's Remco Evenepoel in the general classification after stage 19, putting him on course for a fifth Tour de France title that would equal the record for the modern era.
"We are incredibly proud to partner with UAE Team Emirates-XRG and launch this collaboration on cycling's grandest stage," KuCoin chief executive BC Wong said in a statement announcing the tie-up.

Wong framed the partnership as a natural fit between two fields built on precision and long-term planning, arguing that professional cycling and the digital-asset industry both depend on coordinated teams working toward a shared goal over a long horizon.

KuCoin said further joint initiatives involving UAE Team Emirates-XRG and Pogačar specifically will be unveiled later in the season, though no details of those plans, or the financial terms of the sponsorship itself, have yet been made public.

The deal adds another high-profile crypto sponsor to the Tour de France peloton, a trend that has accelerated in recent seasons as digital-asset firms have chased the global television audience and prestige that cycling's biggest race delivers each July.

body: The Haifa derby is back to open the season, and the bookmakers have already picked a side. With Maccabi Haifa hosting Hapoel Haifa at Sami Ofer Stadium tonight in the opening round of the 2026/27 Toto Cup, Winner's odds published by ONE make the reigning champions overwhelming favorites at 1.4, against 5.1 for Hapoel and 3.75 for a draw.

title: LeBron James picks the 76ers in his most 'Decision'-like move since 2010
dek: At 41, and after seriously weighing retirement, James turns down the Cavaliers and Heat to chase a fifth ring in Philadelphia on a veteran's-minimum deal.

verificationSources.label: ESPN
NBA.com
CBS Sports
NBC News
PhillyVoice

body: LeBron James, at 41, has made what may be the most consequential move of his career since the original 'Decision' in 2010 — this time picking the Philadelphia 76ers as the fourth team of his historic run, ESPN and NBA.com reported.

According to ESPN, James will sign a two-year contract worth roughly $8 million, the NBA's veteran minimum for a player with more than ten years of service, reportedly with a player option for the second season.

The deal ends weeks of speculation that trailed him through free agency. James reportedly also weighed a return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, where his career began, and the Miami Heat, where he won two of his four championships, while the Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves were mentioned as suitors too.

Unlike 2010, when he used a live ESPN special to announce he was 'taking his talents to South Beach', James explained this move in a statement carried by multiple US outlets: "This is my last decision. I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice, I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."

He also revealed how close he came to walking away entirely after the Lakers' season ended: "I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game."

What separates this decision from Miami in 2010 is that James is not walking in to reshape a roster around himself. Philadelphia's contender was largely built before he arrived: the Sixers had already acquired Jaylen Brown in an offseason trade that also saw them move on from Paul George's contract, according to PhillyVoice and CBS Sports.

That leaves head coach Nick Nurse with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, rookie guard VJ Edgecombe, Brown and now James all on one roster — a starting five CBS Sports described as potentially the most talented in the league.

Reports out of Philadelphia indicated Nurse was the only coach James spoke with directly during his deliberations, a detail that underlines how much the fit with an existing group, rather than his own leverage, shaped the choice.

The financial contrast with his recent past is stark. James is walking away from a Lakers salary reported at close to $52 million last season to play for roughly $4 million a year in Philadelphia — a pay cut he has framed publicly as evidence he is chasing a fifth championship rather than another contract.
Pennsylvania's governor marked the news by declaring 'LeBron James Day', Philadelphia outlets reported, a measure of the reaction in a city that has not won an NBA title since 1983.

For followers of the league in Israel, James remains a familiar name beyond the box score: he drew attention at this year's All-Star Game for warm comments about Israel and Israeli All-Star Deni Avdija, saying he hoped to visit the country one day. Whether that curiosity now extends to a Sixers team chasing a title will be one of the subplots of his 24th NBA season.

title: Defender Nitai Gigi returns to Maccabi Netanya on a long-term youth deal

body: Maccabi Netanya have strengthened their Youth A squad ahead of the new season, agreeing a three-year contract with defender Nitai Gigi, ONE reports.

Gigi, who plays in the 2010 age group, is not a stranger at the club — he previously spent time in Maccabi Netanya's academy at Under-15 level before moving on, and his new deal marks a return rather than a first arrival.

His youth path has taken in several clubs. Gigi began at Hapoel Yokneam before switching to Maccabi Haifa's Nahalal-based youth setup at Under-12 level, then featured for Nahalal Yizrael's inaugural Under-11 side, before a spell with Maccabi Netanya's Under-15s and, most recently, Nahalal Yizrael's 2010 age group.

That last stint produced a strong campaign. Gigi made 28 appearances for Nahalal Yizrael last season, starting 22 of them and playing the full 90 minutes in 17, while scoring once and picking up four yellow cards, according to ONE.
The team's season had late drama of its own — Nahalal Yizrael secured their place in the top division with a 2-1 away win over Hapoel Haifa, the report noted.
Gigi's agent, Itzik Tapiro, represented him in negotiating the move back to Netanya.

The club's Youth A squad enters the new season looking to build on a mixed 2025/26 campaign, in which it finished fifth in the premier youth league and lost the cup final 1-6 to Hapoel Tel Aviv. The squad is currently at a training camp in Bulgaria under coach Yuval Akiva.

title: Money, depth and madness: Hapoel Tel Aviv must reach the Final Four
dek: Owner Ofer Yanai has bankrolled the biggest spending spree in the club's history, and ONE reports the bill leaves Hapoel with essentially one acceptable outcome next EuroLeague season — the Final Four.

verificationSources.label: ONE - כסף, עומק וטירוף: הפועל חייבת להגיע לפיינל פור

body: Hapoel Tel Aviv have never spent like this. As the club builds its roster for the 2026-27 EuroLeague season, ONE reports that owner Ofer Yanai has financed the priciest squad in the team's history — and argues the outlay leaves the club with essentially one acceptable outcome come next spring: a place in the Final Four.

The spending has been channelled through sporting director Georgios Chinas, and the marquee example is center Daniel Oturu. His contract has been extended, with Hapoel fending off rival offers reported at $1.7 million a year by paying him around $2.4 million annually — a package ONE says beat the market by roughly $2.1 million over three seasons.

Forward Zach LeDay arrived on a similar scale, joining after two seasons at Olimpia Milano on a deal ONE puts at close to $2.8 million a year. Other additions, the outlet reports, were signed at fees around $3 million despite market valuations closer to $1.5-1.6 million — numbers Hapoel's spending is accused of helping inflate across European basketball more broadly.

Yet ONE's central argument is that the money has not bought balance. Vasilis Micic and Tomas Satoransky give Hapoel real strength at center, and LeDay's arrival deepens the four spot, but the backcourt remains a concern even after all the outlay — expensive pieces stacked in some areas while others stay thin.

Guard Tamir Blatt is the clearest illustration. He joined Hapoel from city rivals Maccabi Tel Aviv in what was widely described as a swap deal with Yam Madar moving the other way, on a contract reported elsewhere at around €1.6 million over three seasons. But ONE reports his role at Hapoel remains murky, with conflicting accounts of what was actually offered and agreed — an unresolved situation for a player who ranked eighth in the league for assists last season and has a track record of delivering in the EuroLeague.

The Blatt uncertainty carries an extra sting because of who left in the other direction. Madar, Hapoel's backcourt leader, signed a three-year deal with Maccabi through 2028/29 after concluding he would not get the playing time and recognition he wanted in Tel Aviv — a departure ONE frames as a genuine loss dressed up as a trade.

All of this sits against EuroLeague's licensing structure, which ONE says requires clubs to reach the playoff quarterfinals regularly simply to justify their place in the competition. The outlet's reading of the rules is stark: by the 2027/28 season, reaching the Final Four on its own will not guarantee Hapoel's continued participation — only winning the title, securing a wildcard, or locking in a multi-year license would settle the club's long-term status.

Set against a budget this large and a roster this expensive, ONE's verdict is blunt: anything short of the Final Four next season would amount to a resounding failure for Hapoel Tel Aviv, whatever shape the rest of the campaign takes.

title: Report: Lazio eye Israel defender Stav Lemkin as Twente stay in doubt
dek: Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb names the Israel international as a defensive option for the Rome club, barely a year after his move to the Eredivisie

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Stav Lemkin's name has surfaced in Italy, with Lazio reportedly weighing up the Israel international as they look to refresh an ageing back line ahead of the rest of the transfer window.

ONE, citing the Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb, reports that the Rome club sees the 23-year-old Twente centre-back as one of several defensive options under consideration. The report frames Lemkin as a name on Lazio's radar rather than a player they have moved for, with no bid or fee mentioned.

The interest, as reported, stems from uncertainty at the heart of Lazio's defence. Alessio Romagnoli's proposed move to Qatari club Al-Sadd has stalled — a deal that had appeared close before talks slowed amid the Gulf state's period of mourning following the death of the former Emir — leaving his long-term future at the club unresolved. Lazio are said to want to "thicken and refresh" their back line regardless of how the Romagnoli situation resolves itself.

It is a striking twist for a player who only completed his move to the Eredivisie a year ago. Lemkin joined Twente from Shakhtar Donetsk last summer in a deal reported at around €1.5 million, ending a spell in Ukraine that began in July 2023 after he broke through at Hapoel Tel Aviv.

His path to Enschede ran through Israeli football's biggest stage on the way: after his Hapoel Tel Aviv debut in April 2022, Shakhtar sent him on loan to Maccabi Tel Aviv for the 2024-25 season, where he featured regularly before completing his switch to Twente.

This past season he was a fixture for Twente, making 29 appearances across all competitions for around 2,430 minutes and scoring once — a workload that has clearly caught scouts' attention beyond the Netherlands.

A separate report on the Dutch fan site Twenteinsite.nl, sourced to forum discussion around the club, similarly floated Lazio's interest, suggesting the Serie A side view Lemkin as a fit given their ageing centre-back options behind new arrival Danilho Doekhi. That account, however, rests on unverified forum commentary rather than reporting from an established outlet, and should be read as considerably softer than the Tuttomercatoweb line picked up by ONE.

Nothing here amounts to an approach, let alone an agreement, and Lemkin is understood to be settled at Twente for now. But at a time when Lazio are actively rebuilding their defence, his name entering the conversation in Italy is notable in its own right for a player who has risen fast through Israeli, Ukrainian and now Dutch football in the space of three years.

title: Hapoel Jerusalem claim first-ever European win with victory over Budućnost
dek: Jaielly's early strike settled a third-place classification match in Greece, giving the Jerusalem club a historic maiden win in Women's Champions League qualifying.

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem's women finished their maiden European campaign with a moment worth savouring: a 1-0 win over Montenegrin champions Budućnost Podgorica in a third-place classification match at the first qualifying round of the 2026/27 UEFA Women's Champions League, played in Greece on Saturday.

It was the only goal the Jerusalem side needed and it came almost immediately. Brazilian attacker Jaielly, wearing the number 7 shirt, put her team ahead inside the seventh minute and the lead held all the way to the final whistle.

The win itself carried no bearing on qualification. Both sides had already been eliminated from advancing to the second qualifying round after finishing on the losing end of their semi-finals earlier in the week — Jerusalem going down 3-1 to hosts PAOK Thessaloniki on July 22, Budućnost falling in the other semi-final of the four-team mini-tournament.

But ONE described the result as historic in its own right: it is the first competitive European victory in the history of Hapoel Jerusalem's women's section, in only the club's debut appearance in continental competition.

There is also a practical dividend. The win banks Hapoel Jerusalem's first UEFA coefficient points as a women's team, a currency that will factor into the seeding for future European qualifying draws even though this campaign is now over.

The achievement caps a rapid rise for a club that only established a senior women's team ahead of the 2020/21 season, entering at the third tier of Israeli football. Since then the side has finished runners-up in the league twice, won its first Israeli championship last season and lifted the Athena Cup, before this summer's step up to European qualifying.

Jerusalem travelled to Greece with an 18-player squad and had put in three weeks of double training sessions to prepare, according to earlier reporting, aiming to become the first Israeli women's club to reach the second qualifying round under the competition's newer format. That target was missed this time, but a first European win — and the ranking points that come with it — gives the club a tangible marker to build on.

title: Real Madrid pivot from Olise to Diomande as Leipzig fee nears €120m
dek: Sport5 reports Real Madrid have abandoned their long chase for Bayern Munich's Michael Olise and are closing in on a deal worth around €115-120m for RB Leipzig's teenage winger Yan Diomande.

verificationSources.label: Sport5

body: Real Madrid's search for a marquee attacking reinforcement this summer has taken a decisive turn. Sport5 reports the club has effectively given up on Michael Olise and is now closing in on a deal for RB Leipzig's teenage winger Yan Diomande, with the fee expected to land somewhere between €115m and €120m.

Olise had been described, according to the report, as Florentino Pérez's personal dream signing for much of the year. But Bayern Munich have refused to even open negotiations for the French international, and Madrid's hierarchy have concluded that a move simply is not realistic this window.
That resistance from Munich pushed Real Madrid's recruitment staff toward Diomande, a 19-year-old Ivorian winger who has emerged as one of the Bundesliga's breakout stars over the past year.

Madrid's first formal offer, worth a fixed €90m plus €10m in add-ons, was rejected by Leipzig, who had been holding out for a fee closer to €130m fixed. RB Leipzig's sporting director Marcel Schäfer publicly insisted the club's intention was for Diomande to stay for at least another season, telling reporters at the time: "Our clear intention is that Yan Diomande will play for RB Leipzig next season."

The gap between the two sides has narrowed considerably since then. Sport5's figure of €115-120m tracks with reporting from Goal.com and other outlets, which describe the clubs as putting the finishing touches on an agreement in that range, including bonuses.

Diomande enjoyed a breakout campaign at Leipzig, contributing 12 goals and eight assists in 33 Bundesliga appearances and picking up the division's Rookie of the Season award. Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain have also been credited with interest in the winger earlier in the window, but reporting consistently points to Real Madrid as his preferred destination.

Should the fee be finalised in the range Sport5 describes, Diomande would rank among the most expensive teenage transfers in football history and would arrive at the Santiago Bernabéu as one of Madrid's headline additions of the summer.

The final number has not been confirmed by either club, and reports elsewhere have placed Real Madrid's improved offer anywhere from €100m to €120m — a reminder that, until documents are signed, the exact figure remains a moving target in this transfer saga.

title: Spanish press praise Orian Goren after Israeli teenager's Barcelona debut
dek: The 17-year-old La Masia midfielder came off the bench in a preseason friendly against CE Europa, and Barcelona's own beat reporters liked what they saw

verificationSources.label: Sport5 - "At 17: Orian Goren made his Barcelona debut"

body: Orian Goren has waited years for this moment, and on Friday he finally got it: a first appearance in Barcelona's senior shirt, and immediate approval from the Catalan press that watches that shirt most closely.

The 17-year-old Israeli midfielder was sent on by Hansi Flick at half-time of Barcelona's preseason friendly against CE Europa, part of a wave of academy substitutions the German coach used to run the rule over his La Masia prospects. Barcelona won the closed-doors match 4-1 at the Joan Gamper training ground, with goals from Ibrahim Diarra, Hector Fort, Ebrima Tunkara and Alex Gonzalez either side of a CE Europa reply.

ONE reports that Sport, one of Barcelona's two dedicated daily football papers, singled out Goren among the youngsters given a chance, writing that he "had a positive impact" during his time on the pitch and "registered good minutes." It is exactly the kind of notice a teenager three years into his time at La Masia hopes to attract.

Goren joined Barcelona's academy in 2023 after coming through the youth ranks at Maccabi Petah Tikva, and the club's staff have long rated him among the most gifted attacking midfielders in his age group, comparing his vision and passing range to graduates like Andres Iniesta and Pedri. He can play centrally or off the left and has already featured for Barcelona in the UEFA Youth League.

Born in Savyon, Goren has represented Israel at both under-17 and under-19 level, scoring once in seven appearances for the U17s. Friday's cameo was only a preseason friendly, and Flick used the second half largely to test fringe and reserve players rather than chase a result, but for an Israeli prospect being watched closely back home, a debut in Barcelona's first-team shirt - and a favourable Spanish write-up alongside it - is a real marker of progress.

Israeli football has sent academy graduates to Barcelona before without them making the step up to Camp Nou; Guy Asulin trained with Pep Guardiola's squad in preseason in 2009 without it leading to a first-team breakthrough. Goren's supporters will hope his path proves different, but for now the compliments from Barcelona's own press corps are the headline.

title: Daniel Peretz plays down dramatic-looking wrist splint after Southampton win

body: Daniel Peretz has moved to calm any alarm over the bulky splint strapped to his right wrist during Southampton's pre-season friendly in Germany, insisting the get-up "only looks dramatic" and is nothing new.

The Israeli international started in goal as Southampton beat Eintracht Braunschweig 1-0 on Friday, keeping a clean sheet through the first half before making way at the break as Russell Martin's side worked through their squad on tour.

Photos of Peretz warming up with the guard visible on his hand quickly did the rounds among Saints supporters online, with one fan account posting a picture of the goalkeeper arriving at the stadium with the cast in plain view.

Asked about it afterwards, Peretz played it down. According to ONE, he said he felt good and that the brace was purely protective, stressing the issue was carried over from the closing weeks of last season rather than a fresh knock picked up in training or the game itself.

The 26-year-old spoke warmly about being back among his teammates and in front of Southampton's travelling fans in Germany, saying the squad relishes a packed schedule and expects a strong season with the fanbase's support as the club prepares for its return to the Premier League.

Peretz completed a permanent move to Southampton from Bayern Munich on July 1, signing a four-year contract through 2030 after an eye-catching loan spell split between Hamburger SV and St Mary's last season, in which he made 26 appearances and helped fire the club up the Championship table.
Southampton confirmed the deal as their first signing of the summer, with the goalkeeper immediately calling for unity in the squad as the club pushes to establish itself back in the top flight.

For now, the wrist guard appears to be little more than a pre-season talking point, with Peretz set to continue as Southampton's first-choice goalkeeper through the remainder of their preparations in Germany.

title: Rodri agrees personal terms with Real Madrid, but a fee standoff with Manchester City remains
dek: Spain's World Cup-winning captain wants to move to the Bernabéu this summer and has accepted Madrid's contract offer, but Manchester City have yet to sanction any sale, according to transfer reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Rodri has made his position clear to those around him: he wants to leave Manchester City for Real Madrid this summer, and according to ONE, citing Italian transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, he has already agreed personal terms with the Spanish club on a contract running to 2030.

The report describes a player who has made no special demands of Madrid, accepting the salary and conditions on offer, with a single aim in mind: returning home and pulling on the white shirt before the transfer window closes.

The interest is not new, but it has hardened dramatically since Rodri's performances for Spain at the 2026 World Cup. He captained La Roja to the title, beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final, and was named winner of the Golden Ball as the tournament's outstanding player — an award that comes on top of the Ballon d'Or he won in 2024.

That form is said to have shifted the thinking of Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez, who had previously been reluctant to move for the 30-year-old given his age and Manchester City's known reluctance to sell a player so central to Pep Guardiola's team.

The football case for Rodri fits a gap Madrid have carried since Toni Kroos and Luka Modrić left the club: a genuine controlling midfielder able to dictate tempo, shield the back line and bring the game-management the club has missed in Europe's biggest matches.

Where the deal stalls is money. ONE's figure for what would satisfy City sits at around €45 million. Other reporting this week, including from Yahoo Sports and FootballTransfers, suggests Madrid have effectively capped their offer near €50 million while City's valuation has been pitched far higher, with figures as steep as £84 million to £100 million floated in the English press.

That gap matters because Manchester City are not desperate sellers. Rodri is contracted until June 2027, and the club have already tabled a new long-term extension that he has so far neither accepted nor rejected, according to multiple outlets tracking the situation.

As things stand, there has been no formal club-to-club negotiation between Madrid and City over a fee, only interest from Madrid's side and swirling reports of Rodri's own preference. Real Madrid are said to want to push things along quickly, wary that other clubs could enter the picture the longer the situation drags.

For now, the story is exactly what ONE's headline suggests: the player's will to go is there, but the road to actually getting the deal done — persuading Manchester City to sell one of their most important midfielders for a fee they consider fair — is still a long one.

title: More misfortune for Pedrão as groin tear rules him out of Haifa derby
dek: The Brazilian centre-back, still working his way back from a serious knee ligament injury, will miss Maccabi Haifa's Toto Cup opener against Hapoel Haifa after a small adductor tear was confirmed by ultrasound on Saturday morning.

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Pedrão's run of bad luck has struck again. Hours before Maccabi Haifa's first competitive match of the season, ONE reports the Brazilian centre-back has been ruled out with a small tear in his groin muscle, diagnosed on ultrasound this Saturday morning.

The club had been planning to start Pedrão in the Carmel derby against Hapoel Haifa, but the scan changed those plans. He has already begun treatment and a rehabilitation process, though no return date has been given.

The match itself is a significant one for Maccabi Haifa: their opening fixture of the season, a Toto Cup derby against city rivals Hapoel Haifa, kicking off at 20:30 on Saturday at Sammy Ofer Stadium.

With Pedrão out, goalkeeper Omri Glazer returns to the side and will wear the captain's armband, while defender Yirin Loy also comes back into the lineup. Yair Mardochay, a recent arrival from Hapoel Kiryat Shmona, is set for his official debut in midfield.

Pedrão is not the only absentee. Manuel Benson and Yilal Batailly are both sidelined through injury, and several of the club's newly signed foreign players are still being integrated gradually into the squad rather than thrown straight into the derby.
In attack, Adam Grinberg is favoured to start ahead of veteran forward Guy Malamed, who is expected to be held in reserve for the second half, while Iad Khalayle is set to start on the left wing.

title: Can you build real muscle with light weights and lots of reps?
dek: A ONE fitness explainer says the old heavy-weight-only rule for muscle growth doesn't hold up — but the story has no news event, athlete or team behind it.

verificationSources.label: ONE - ניתן להגדיל שריר עם הרבה חזרות ומשקל נמוך?

body: A gym-floor debate that has run for decades is getting fresh attention: can lifting light weights for high repetitions actually build muscle, or is heavy iron the only real path to growth?

In a fitness explainer, ONE lays out the traditional bodybuilding doctrine — that roughly 8-12 reps at a heavy load creates the mechanical tension needed to stimulate hypertrophy, and that anything lighter is essentially cardio in disguise.

The piece argues that view is outdated. Citing a broader body of exercise-science research from recent years, ONE reports that the real driver of muscle growth is not the number on the plate but how close a set is taken to muscular failure and how much genuine effort it demands.

The mechanism explained is straightforward: a light-weight, high-rep set initially recruits the body's slow-twitch fibres, but as those fibres fatigue, the nervous system is forced to call in fast-twitch fibres — the ones with the greatest capacity for growth — to finish the set.
That, according to the article, is why sets pushed close to failure with a lighter bar can ultimately trigger a similar hypertrophy response to a heavier, lower-rep set.

ONE lists real advantages to the lighter-weight approach: less stress on joints and ligaments, easier technique control, and a metabolic, 'pump'-driven training effect that carries its own hormonal and cellular benefits. It is flagged as particularly useful for older lifters, the injured, or anyone managing chronic pain.

The trade-offs are also spelled out. Training light-to-failure demands real mental toughness and produces intense muscular burn, alongside greater overall systemic and cardiovascular fatigue than a traditional heavy set. The article is clear that this method is not the way to build maximal strength or a bigger one-rep max — heavy loading still wins there.

The piece is bylined by Shai Lev, ONE's fitness editor since 2013, who is also a basketball coach, gym instructor and certified TRX trainer, and reads as general training advice rather than a report on any competition, athlete or event.

title: Not just a championship: the challenges awaiting LeBron James in Philadelphia
dek: James, 41, has called joining the 76ers his "last decision" - but fitting into a stacked roster, finding answers on defence and living up to Philadelphia's brutal fan pressure all come before any title talk.

verificationSources.label: ONE
ESPN
NBA.com
NBC Sports Philadelphia

body: LeBron James called it his "last decision," and it turned out to be the most startling one of his career: after a decade on the Lakers, the 41-year-old is joining the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million contract, choosing them over the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat and other contenders. But as ONE lays out, signing the deal was the easy part - fitting into his new team, staying healthy and surviving one of America's toughest fan bases may be a far bigger test than winning a fifth ring.

James arrives with a resume that speaks for itself: a four-time NBA champion, four-time MVP, 22-time All-Star and the league's all-time leading scorer. But last season's numbers told a more human story - 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists across 60 games, his lowest scoring average since his rookie year, with 22 games missed to back and foot problems.

In Philadelphia he joins arguably the most talented roster he has played on in more than two decades, alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and rising guard VJ Edgecombe. That talent is also the problem. Most of those players are used to having the ball in their hands, and head coach Nick Nurse now has to work out who gives up minutes, touches and shots to make room for a 41-year-old former MVP.

ONE draws the comparison to LeBron's arrival in Miami alongside Dwyane Wade - a process that took time and friction before the roles settled. Nurse, by reputation an excellent tactician, is reported by ONE to be less sure-footed when it comes to discipline and man-management, a dynamic that will be tested immediately with this many voices in one locker room.

A former coach quoted in the piece describes James as possessing elite-level basketball intelligence and professionalism - but notes that at this stage of his career, he no longer wants to be the one carrying the whole team on his own. That shift matters for a Sixers side that has spent years waiting for someone else to share the leadership load with Embiid.

Defence is the other open question. James is no longer the dominant defender he once was, Embiid continues to battle recurring physical issues, and much of the defensive burden already falls on Brown. Philadelphia will need answers against the league's biggest physical threats - centres like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo - and its most dangerous guards, from Stephen Curry to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

The move also scatters James's family across the country. His son Bronny stays behind with the Lakers, continuing his own NBA career on the other coast, while wife Savannah and daughter Zhuri adjust to a new base and younger son Bryce continues his college career at the University of Arizona.

Philadelphia's supporters are, by reputation, among the most demanding in American sport. The Sixers have not won a championship since 1983 and have not reached the NBA Finals since 2001. Anything short of genuine contention will invite the kind of scrutiny James has rarely faced in this form, even during his most difficult seasons in Los Angeles.

There is a quieter thread running through the move too: James reunites in the front office with Mike Gansey, Philadelphia's president of basketball operations, who competed against him for Ohio's Mr. Basketball award as a high schooler more than two decades ago and finished runner-up to him in 2001.

Health, more than talent, may end up deciding how this season is remembered. Embiid's injury history remains the single biggest variable in any Sixers plan, James is managing the wear of a 23rd NBA season, and Brown has had his own issues with his Achilles and wrist. If all three stay on the floor together, Philadelphia has a genuine top-tier roster. If not, the questions about fit and leadership will only get louder.

title: Manchester United plot a £2 billion, 100,000-seat stadium to replace Old Trafford
dek: The club is pressing ahead with plans for what would be Britain's biggest stadium, built 350 metres from its current home as part of a wider Trafford Wharfside regeneration led by Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

verificationSources.label: ONE
ESPN
Al Jazeera
Yahoo Sports
Football Insider

body: Manchester United's ambitions for a new home have crystallised into something startling in scale: a 100,000-seat stadium, initially costed at around £2 billion, that would be the largest in Britain and would sit almost within touching distance of the ground it replaces.

ONE reports that the new arena is planned for a site roughly 350 metres from the current Old Trafford, on industrial land at what the club calls the Trafford Wharfside district — ground that, according to the report, previously hosted a go-kart track. Independent reporting places the plot between John Gilbert Way, Wharfside Way and Europa Way, just north-west of the existing stadium.

The design brief has already shifted once in public. Foster + Partners, the architecture practice United appointed for the project, first unveiled a dramatic canopy-topped concept; more recent images have shown a more conventional bowl-shaped ground, though the club has stressed those renderings are not final either.

Collette Roche, chief executive of the stadium development company, framed the latest step — publication of the Wharfside Masterplan — as "another significant milestone in our journey to create a new world-class home for Manchester United at the heart of a vibrant and transformational district for Trafford and Greater Manchester."

The project is not just a football venue. United and their development partners are pitching a full district around it: a tree-lined boulevard styled on Wembley's approach for matchday crowds, waterfront bars and restaurants, a rebuilt tram station, and residential towers overlooking the Manchester Ship Canal. Separate reporting puts the wider scheme at 15,000 new homes and 48,000 local jobs, with the club claiming it could generate £7.3 billion a year for the UK economy.

None of that comes cheap, and the financing question hangs over the entire venture. United's own accounts show total debt approaching £1.3 billion, a legacy largely traced to the Glazer family's leveraged 2004 takeover, and the club is currently paying upwards of £30 million a season in interest alone. United's leadership insists the new stadium will ultimately pay for itself through higher matchday and commercial revenue, funnelling extra income back into the playing squad, but analysts have flagged that lenders may push the Glazers and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to put up more of their own capital than first envisaged.

Ratcliffe, the INEOS billionaire who took a controlling stake in football operations in 2024, has been the driving force pushing the timeline forward. The stated goal is a "spade in the ground" by the end of 2026, with the stadium targeted for completion in time for the 2030-31 season.

Fan groups are watching the process closely, and not uncritically. Duncan Drasdo, chief executive of the Manchester United Supporters' Trust, has said the priority is to avoid the pitfalls other clubs have hit when leaving historic homes: "We want to make sure we end up with an atmospheric stadium, not a soulless bowl, as we've seen with other clubs when they've moved to a new ground."

What happens to the old Old Trafford remains an open question. ONE reports that its fate — full demolition, partial preservation, or conversion into housing — has not been formally decided, and will likely be settled only once the new stadium plans are locked in.

According to the report, detailed designs are expected to be ready by late 2026 or early 2027, after which they would go to formal submission with planning committees. A public consultation with fans, residents and local businesses is due to begin shortly, a step that will shape everything from the boulevard's design to how the club manages the disruption of building a stadium of this size a few hundred metres from a live, matchday-operating ground.

For a club that has spent much of the past decade playing catch-up off the pitch as well as on it, the stadium has become the clearest marker of how Ratcliffe's ownership wants United to be judged — not just by trophies, but by whether it can deliver Britain's biggest football ground without the debt burden swallowing the project whole.

title: Daniel Mérida wins maiden ATP title after years he could not afford a coach
dek: The 21-year-old Spaniard beat Damir Džumhur in Umag for his first tour-level trophy, a breakthrough built on budget flights, shared hotel rooms and years of self-funded travel.

verificationSources.label: ATP Tour — Merida joins Alcaraz & Sinner in Umag title history
ATP Tour — Daniel Merida player overview
