body: José Mourinho's second era in charge of Real Madrid began quietly and nervily on Friday, with the club needing a stoppage-heavy penalty to see off third-tier Alcorcón 1-0 in a preseason friendly at the Alfredo Di Stéfano Stadium, ONE reports.

It is thirteen years since the Portuguese last patrolled a Real Madrid touchline, and this reintroduction offered little of the theatre associated with his first spell. Mourinho watched from the bench with minimal instruction, cutting a low-key figure as his side toiled for long stretches against lower-division opposition.

The breakthrough almost came in the first minute. Franco Mastantuono, the Argentine winger signed from River Plate, drove down the right and won a penalty inside 51 seconds of kick-off - only for Arda Güler to see his effort saved, leaving the game goalless deep into the second half.

Real Madrid were finally rewarded for their pressure in the 81st minute, when a second penalty was awarded and dispatched by Yáñez, one of several academy players introduced as Mourinho emptied his bench.

Mastantuono was the outstanding performer on the night regardless of the missed spot-kick, according to ONE, repeatedly threatening down the flank and involved in most of the team's meaningful attacking moments both with and without the ball.
Eduardo Camavinga and academy midfielder Gonzalo Brahim also drew praise for their contributions, while Güler was credited with confident, inventive play in possession even after his penalty miss.

Around the 70-minute mark, Mourinho withdrew his entire starting line-up in one go, handing further minutes to a batch of academy prospects for the closing stages - a pattern typical of pre-season friendlies but also an early signal of how the new coach intends to use these matches to assess his squad depth.

The match itself was played under difficult conditions, with heavy smoke from wildfires affecting the Madrid region visible over the stadium; ONE reported that the club halted its broadcast and withdrew media from pitchside access after around 20 minutes.

Mourinho's return to the Santiago Bernabéu institution was confirmed by the club in June, with the 63-year-old, who won two league titles and a Copa del Rey during his first spell between 2010 and 2013, tasked with resetting a squad now built around a new generation including Mastantuono, Güler and the promoted academy contingent.

Friday's narrow win over Alcorcón was only the first of several pre-season fixtures before Real Madrid open their 2026-27 campaign, giving Mourinho a handful of further run-outs to settle on his first-choice XI.

body: Orian Goren, the 17-year-old Israeli midfielder who has spent the past three years rising through La Masia, got his first minutes in a Barcelona senior shirt on Friday, coming off the bench in a 4-1 preseason win over Catalan side CE Europa.

ONE reports that Goren was introduced in the second half at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper, Barcelona's training complex, in a match played behind closed doors as the club opened its 2026-27 preseason schedule. Head coach Hansi Flick fielded a squad drawn heavily from La Masia and the reserve ranks, with most first-team regulars still to report for training.

It is another marker in a rapid rise for Goren, who was born in Savyon in March 2009 and joined Maccabi Petah Tikva's youth setup at the age of eight. His family relocated to Spain when he was 14, and he passed Barcelona's academy trials to join La Masia in 2023 — going on to sign his first professional contract with the club at 16.

Spanish outlets covering Barcelona's academy have repeatedly flagged Goren as one of the standout prospects of his age group at the club, drawing comparisons to Andrés Iniesta and Pedri for his passing range and game intelligence. He was among the youngest players included in Flick's preseason party this summer, alongside 2010-born teenager Ebrima Tunkara.

Goren has already represented Israel at youth level, debuting for the under-17s in March 2025 during European Championship qualifying and featuring for the under-19s since. Friday's appearance does not amount to a competitive senior debut, but it is his first time on the pitch alongside Barcelona's first-team environment in a match setting.

ONE notes that Goren is expected to keep training with the senior group through the rest of preseason camp as he continues trying to catch Flick's eye before the squad reconverges around its established stars.

body: Israel's Under-16 girls' water polo team dives into its first world championship on Saturday, opening the group phase of the World Aquatics Women's U16 Water Polo Championship against South Africa at Zagreb's Mladost swimming and water polo centre, Sport5 reports.

There is no easing in: the Israelis are back in the water later the same day for a second group match against Hungary, one of the sport's traditional powers, before facing Mexico on Sunday and closing out the preliminary round against the Netherlands on Monday.

The championship runs from July 25-31 in the Croatian capital, a city with a long water polo pedigree that is doubling up this summer - the equivalent boys' U16 event follows at the same Mladost venue in early August. Qualification for the knockout stage will be determined once all group matches are complete.

Head coach Idan Kaftori, who also serves as an assistant with Israel's senior women's national team, described it as a considerable honour to lead the squad at a world championship, according to Sport5.

He was candid about the challenges facing his group too, noting the squad is carrying "a light injury issue" heading into the tournament and that its youth makes competing against more seasoned rivals "a considerable challenge."

Kaftori was clear-eyed about where the value lies at this level. "The primary objective is for the athletes to learn, gain experience, and compete on their sport's biggest stage for their age group," he said.
The squad has put in six weeks of dedicated preparation for the tournament, including a warm-up trip to Greece, as it takes its first real step into senior-style international competition.

body: Kings Kangwa, the Zambian midfielder who powered Hapoel Beer Sheva to back-to-back trophies, is closing in on a move to Panathinaikos, ONE reports, with the two sides agreeing a four-year contract that would run until the summer of 2030.

According to ONE, Beer Sheva are set to bank around €4m for the 27-year-old, with other Israeli outlets citing Greek sources putting the total nearer €4.5m once bonuses are folded in — one of the largest fees the champions have ever received for a player.
The agreement also reportedly includes a 25% sell-on clause, meaning Beer Sheva would take a cut of any future transfer should Panathinaikos move him on again down the line.
Kangwa himself stands to see his wages roughly triple. ONE reports he is in line for close to €1m a season in Athens, up from his current terms in Beer Sheva.

He is expected to play one last match in Beer Sheva colours before departing: the second leg of the club's Champions League qualifying tie away — sorry, at home — to Víkingur Reykjavík, after which he would fly to Greece for a medical and to sign the contract.

That fixture carries extra weight of its own. Beer Sheva lost the first leg 2-1 in Iceland, with Kangwa scoring the equaliser after intercepting a pass from Niv Yehoshua, and now need a strong response to keep their European qualifying campaign alive.

The move caps a genuine chase for his signature. AEK Athens also pursued Kangwa and reportedly offered around €3.5m, according to Walla and Sport1-Maariv, before Panathinaikos raised their bid and won the race.
Kangwa joined Beer Sheva in July 2024 from Red Star Belgrade for a reported €800,000, after earlier spells with Arsenal Tula in Russia and a loan at Kortrijk in Belgium.
Since arriving in Israel he has been central to the club's most successful stretch in years, helping Beer Sheva complete the league and State Cup double.
None of the financial terms have been confirmed by either club, and the move remains pending Kangwa's medical examination in Athens — but Israeli reports are treating the transfer as all but done.

title: NBA stunned as LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers

body: LeBron James's long-running free agency saga ended on Friday with a genuine stunner: the NBA's all-time leading scorer is joining the Philadelphia 76ers, not the Cleveland Cavaliers, the Miami Heat or any of the other suitors who had spent weeks being cast as favourites.

James announced the move himself on X, calling it his "last decision" — a nod to the way he has framed his biggest career choices before — after ESPN and NBA.com reported the terms: a two-year contract worth around $8 million, including a player option for the second season.

The number is jarring set against what he was earning twelve months ago. James took in more than $52 million in his final season with the Lakers, so a near-minimum deal in Philadelphia is a striking statement that, at 41 and heading into his 24th NBA season, chasing one more championship now outweighs chasing another maximum paycheck.

Until this week, Cleveland, Miami, Golden State and Minnesota were the four teams most consistently linked with James as his market played out, with reporters tracking his search for a contender rather than a payday. Philadelphia was rarely mentioned as the frontrunner, which is precisely why the announcement caught so much of the league off guard.

The 76ers now assemble a startling collection of talent around James: former MVP Joel Embiid, two-time All-Star Tyrese Maxey, and Jaylen Brown, the former Finals MVP whom Philadelphia acquired from Boston earlier in the same offseason. Rookie guard VJ Edgecombe rounds out a potential starting five that outlets on both sides of the Atlantic immediately began describing as a title-calibre unit.

Reaction inside the 76ers' own locker room came fast. Brown, who had stayed largely quiet through James's monthslong free-agency search while Maxey and Embiid led the public recruiting push, posted simply "#throwtheballup" on X — the same phrase he used when he first learned of his own trade to Philadelphia, a deliberate callback signalling the two stars are aligned.

Maxey's reaction was more chaotic. Caught mid-workout when the news broke, he filmed himself screaming, then posted an Instagram story joking that he was "like coach Cal" — a reference to John Calipari, his college coach at Kentucky — half-crediting his own recruiting pitch for helping land James.

The wider basketball world reacted with the kind of disbelief usually reserved for trade-deadline blockbusters. ONE reported that the announcement shocked the NBA community precisely because almost no one had Philadelphia near the top of their list of likely destinations, with pundits scrambling within hours to recast the Sixers as instant championship contenders for 2026-27.

It caps an extraordinary run of additions for Philadelphia, who now go into training camp with arguably the league's most talked-about roster overhaul of the summer — and with James, at an age when most of his contemporaries have long since retired, choosing to bet what remains of his career on it.

body: UFC featherweight Jean Silva sat down for more than an hour with Israeli fans this week, appearing as the marquee guest on the 50th episode of "Knockout," the combat-sports podcast that ONE says has become, in its first year on air, a genuine home for Israel's MMA community.

Hosts Yaniv Kaminski and Olga Rubin were joined by Ilai Brazili, the unbeaten Israeli fighter who trains alongside Silva at the Fighting Nerds gym in Brazil, for a wide-ranging conversation that mixed hard biography with lighter, behind-the-scenes UFC stories.

Silva, ranked in the world's top six featherweights, walked the hosts through the financial hardship and sacrifice that marked his early years chasing a career in Brazilian MMA before he broke into the UFC, according to the podcast.

He also spoke about his ambitions to eventually fight for the UFC featherweight title, and about the role his wife has played in helping him manage the balancing act between his personal life and a demanding professional schedule, ONE reported.

A recurring theme was his friendship with Brazili, a bond the pair described as having grown across language and cultural lines through their shared training camp at Fighting Nerds - the São Paulo gym, founded by Caio Borralho and coach Pablo Sucupira, that has become one of the UFC's most talked-about pipelines of young talent.
Silva also reflected on his impressions of Israel itself, telling the hosts he had been struck by the warmth of the reception he received from local fans during his visit, per the podcast.

The timing of the episode is no coincidence. Brazili is set to headline a GFN event at Tel Aviv's Menora Mivtachim Arena on Monday, July 27, against Brazilian ex-UFC fighter Lucas Almeida - his first professional fight on Israeli soil after a frustrating run of cancelled and postponed bouts.

Brazili confirmed that Silva will work his corner for that fight, giving the Israeli a training partner ranked among the UFC's elite in his corner as he pushes for the kind of statement win that fighters and fans alike believe would finally open the door to a UFC contract.

For a podcast just reaching its 50th instalment, landing a top-10 UFC featherweight as a guest - on the eve of his own trip to work an Israeli fighter's corner - is a marker of how far Israel's MMA media scene has come in a single year.

title: LeBron James signs with the 76ers as Pennsylvania declares 'LeBron James Day'
dek: The 41-year-old's move to Philadelphia, sealed days after the 76ers traded for Jaylen Brown, ends eight years in Los Angeles and reshapes the NBA title race.

verificationSources.label: ESPN
CNN
NBA.com

body: After twenty-five days of speculation that gripped the NBA, LeBron James has made his choice: at 41, the game's all-time leading scorer is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers, closing the book on an eight-year run with the Los Angeles Lakers.

The deal, a two-year contract worth roughly eight million dollars with a player option, was confirmed by his agent Rich Paul to ESPN's Shams Charania. Philadelphia becomes the fourth franchise of James's career, after Cleveland, Miami and Los Angeles.

"This is my last decision," James said in explaining the move. "I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."

He added that he believes he can "help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team" and called it a chance to "energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time," according to CBS Sports.

The timing was no accident. Days before James committed, the 76ers pulled off a blockbuster of their own, sending Paul George and four draft picks to the Boston Celtics for 2024 Finals MVP Jaylen Brown. That move, ONE reports, reshaped the calculus for James and his camp — Paul had reportedly discussed his client's free agency with 27 different teams before Philadelphia emerged as the landing spot.

James now joins a roster built around Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey, with Brown giving the Sixers a third All-Star-calibre scorer. Bookmakers reacted instantly: Philadelphia's championship odds, which sat near 60-to-1 before the Brown trade, shortened to around 9-to-1 once James's signing was announced, according to ONE.

Part of the pull to Philadelphia, per multiple US reports, was personal. Sixers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey grew up in Ohio and faced a teenage James on the high school court in 2001, when James was named the state's Mr. Basketball. The two later worked together in Cleveland, including during the Cavaliers' 2016 championship run.

Pennsylvania's governor did not let the moment pass quietly. Josh Shapiro, a self-described "die-hard Sixers fan," declared July 24 "LeBron James Day" across the state. "By the power vested in me as the Governor of the great Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and a die-hard Sixers fan… I hereby proclaim today to be LEBRON JAMES DAY," he wrote.

The stakes for Philadelphia are steep. The franchise has not won an NBA title since 1983 and has not reached the Finals since 2001 — a drought that predates James's entire professional career and one the front office is clearly betting he can help end.

For James, it is a fifth attempt at a championship beyond the four he already won with Miami and Cleveland, and a wager that, even at 41, he has enough left to be the difference for a team that has spent over four decades searching for a way back to the top.

body: Chelsea's summer spending shows no sign of slowing. Maxence Lacroix, Crystal Palace's French centre-back, was in west London on Friday to undergo a medical ahead of a move worth in the region of £52 million (roughly €55m), according to ONE and multiple outlets tracking the deal.

Lacroix, 26, is expected to sign a six-year contract taking him through to 2032. He joined Palace from Wolfsburg in 2024 and made himself indispensable at Selhurst Park, racking up close to 100 appearances across two seasons and playing a central role in the club's Conference League triumph.

He has also broken into the France squad, appearing for Les Bleus at this summer's World Cup. His departure would mark Chelsea's seventh signing of the window, part of a defensive rebuild that has continued at pace since the Premier League season ended.

Elsewhere, Inter Milan have moved on a different centre-back. ONE reports that the Serie A champions have made direct contact with representatives for Cristian Romero, the Tottenham captain, as speculation over his future intensifies following Argentina's World Cup campaign.

According to Fabrizio Romano, cited by ONE, the move is "very expensive and not straightforward" — Inter will need to negotiate down both Tottenham's asking price and the financial package required to satisfy the player, but the club regard Romero as their priority defensive target.

Other reporting this week has Tottenham demanding at least €50 million for the 28-year-old, with Romero's agent said to have travelled to Milan as talks intensified. Romano has been unequivocal about the player's outlook at Spurs: "It's over between Romero and Tottenham... he's leaving, that's the intention."

Barcelona and Chelsea have also been credited with interest in Romero, but reports from Italy and England suggest he is more inclined to push through a move to Inter than to hold out for a switch to Catalonia.

Romero arrived at Tottenham from Atalanta in 2022 and has since become one of the club's most influential defenders, taking the captain's armband and helping Spurs to their first major trophy in years when they lifted the Europa League last season.

Neither deal is finalised, and ONE's report frames both as developing situations rather than done business — Lacroix's medical is the clearer step toward completion, while the Romero pursuit remains at the negotiating stage.

title: Pogačar shatters Pantani's Alpe d'Huez record to seal Tour de France stranglehold
dek: The yellow jersey erased a three-and-a-half-minute deficit to win stage 19 solo, becoming only the second race leader to triumph on the legendary climb and smashing a near-30-year-old ascent record in the process.

verificationSources.label: Cyclinguptodate — Stage 19 results

body: Tadej Pogačar delivered one of the defining rides of this Tour de France on Friday, hauling back a breakaway that had led by more than three minutes to win stage 19 alone atop Alpe d'Huez, extending a general classification lead that now looks all but unassailable with two stages remaining.

The 127.9km leg from Gap was the shortest road stage of the race but among its most brutal, tackling the Col Bayard, the Col du Noyer and the Col d'Ornon before the tourists' favourite finale: 13.8km at an average of 8.1%, its 21 numbered hairpins climbing to 1,850m. A 42-rider move went clear early, including several riders inside the top 20 overall, and by the base of the final climb the gap to the yellow jersey group had swollen past three minutes.

Pogačar responded with a sustained, isolated attack launched roughly 12-13km from the summit, clawing back the deficit switchback by switchback with help from teammate Adam Yates before catching what remained of the lead group, Lenny Martínez and Richard Carapaz, inside the final two kilometres. He dropped them for good around 800 metres from the line to win alone in 3:17:57.

The manner of the victory was as striking as the result. Pogačar's timed ascent of Alpe d'Huez, 35 minutes 27 seconds, broke the mythical climb record of 36:50 that Marco Pantani had set in 1997 and which had stood for nearly three decades. He is also only the second rider ever to win a Tour stage on Alpe d'Huez while wearing the yellow jersey, following Geraint Thomas in 2018.

Martínez (Bahrain Victorious) held on for second, six seconds back, with Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) third at nine seconds. Sepp Kuss and Tobias Halland Johannessen rounded out the day's leading group, while Remco Evenepoel came home sixth on the stage, more than two and a half minutes down on the climb alone, as Isaac del Toro and Mattias Skjelmose followed him in.
"It's very cool to win up here, it was a crazy atmosphere, all the climbing," Pogačar said afterwards, capping his fifth stage win of this Tour and the 26th of his career since his debut in 2020.

In the general classification, Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) now leads Evenepoel (Red Bull-BORA-hansgrohe) by 7 minutes 11 seconds, with Isaac del Toro (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) third at 9:42 and Paul Seixas (Decathlon CMA CGM) fourth at 10:06. Lenny Martínez climbed to fifth overall at 13:00, nine seconds clear of Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) in sixth, while Juan Ayuso slipped to seventh after losing time on the final ascent.

The day also reshaped the secondary jerseys. Richard Carapaz seized the polka-dot jersey after sweeping maximum points on the Col d'Ornon, snatching the mountains lead. Mads Pedersen tightened his grip on the green jersey after winning the intermediate sprint, taking his points tally to 502 against Jasper Philipsen's 445, with Biniam Girmay a distant third on 361. Isaac del Toro, 22, continues to wear the white jersey as best young rider, sitting third overall for his UAE Team Emirates-XRG team.
With the Alps now behind the peloton and only a handful of stages left before Paris, Pogačar's Alpe d'Huez masterclass looked less like a mountain stage and more like a coronation.

title: Guardiola turns down Italy job, leaving Maldini to chase plan B
dek: The Catalan coach rebuffed a lucrative pitch to lead the Azzurri's rebuild, with Andrea Pirlo now the frontrunner to take over.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Il Fatto Quotidiano

body: Pep Guardiola has told the Italian federation he will not become the Azzurri's next head coach, ONE reports, closing off what would have been the most eye-catching appointment in national-team football and leaving Paolo Maldini to restart his search.

According to the report, the Federazione Italiana Giuoco Calcio offered Guardiola around €10 million a year to take charge, but the Catalan coach's camp was seeking closer to €20 million — a gap Italian outlets including Tuttosport and Il Fatto Quotidiano say ultimately could not be bridged.

Maldini, now Italy's technical director, and his advisor Leonardo had travelled to meet Guardiola in Barcelona and pitched him on far more than a coaching post: a long-term project built around him to rebuild Italian football through to the 2030 World Cup.

Guardiola thanked the pair for their confidence but said he did not feel ready to commit, according to the Italian reporting — a version consistent with ONE's account that talks concluded without an agreement after last week's meeting.

It would have been the first national-team job of Guardiola's coaching career, one built entirely in club football with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and, most recently, a decade at Manchester City that ended this year. Several Italian outlets note he had planned to step away from the touchline for a period before considering any return.

The vacancy exists because Gennaro Gattuso resigned as Italy coach after the Azzurri were eliminated on penalties by Bosnia and Herzegovina in their World Cup play-off, meaning Italy will miss the 2026 tournament. Under-21 coach Silvio Baldini stepped in as caretaker for June's friendlies against Luxembourg and Greece.

With Guardiola out of the picture, ONE cites journalist Gianluca Di Marzio in naming Andrea Pirlo, currently in charge of Italy's youth setup, as the leading alternative, alongside former Napoli coach Antonio Conte and Euro 2020-winning coach Roberto Mancini.

Italian reports suggest Pirlo has emerged as the clear favourite to be handed the rebuilding job, with Maldini and Leonardo now expected to move quickly given Italy's next competitive fixtures are approaching.
No timetable for a final decision has been confirmed, but the federation is under pressure to appoint a permanent coach well before Italy's next qualifying campaign begins.

title: Bakhar says Maccabi Haifa's crest "speaks for itself" ahead of Toto Cup opener against Hapoel Haifa
dek: Head coach Barak Bakhar and sport director Lior Refaelov used their pre-season press conference to preview Saturday's Haifa derby, new signings and a promise of a tighter defence.

verificationSources.label: ONE - כל עונה היא מבחן. אליפות? הסמל מדבר בעד עצמו

body: Barak Bakhar sat down alongside sport director Lior Refaelov on the eve of Maccabi Haifa's 2026/27 campaign and reached for the club's oldest asset when the question of expectations came up: the crest on the shirt.

"The club's crest speaks for itself, I don't need to talk about expectations," Bakhar said, according to ONE, brushing aside a direct question about whether this squad is built to challenge for the championship.

The comment set the tone for a press conference otherwise focused on the here and now: Saturday's Toto Cup opener against city rivals Hapoel Haifa, kicking off at 20:30 in the first instalment of this season's Haifa derby.

Bakhar framed the season ahead in blunt terms. "Every season is a test," he said, arguing that judging a campaign purely by trophies misses the daily grind of squad-building, form and fitness that any Israeli top-flight coach has to manage.

He pointed to what he called a deliberate close-season priority: adding character to the dressing room. "We brought in three or four players with personality that was missing," Bakhar said, without naming all of them individually in the quotes ONE published.

One arrival he did single out was Bruninho, the club's new attacking recruit. "He's a player the fans will love, he searches for goals, and we're giving him time to adapt," Bakhar said, tempering hype with a reminder that integration takes patience.

The coach also praised the development of Yarin Levi, saying the young player "made tremendous progress" over the close season and "knows he's not perfect" but has worked diligently to close the gap. Pedrão was described as continuing his recovery from injury.

On the balance between youth and experience, Bakhar was cautious rather than triumphant, saying the club needs "to balance things, not throw everyone in at once" as academy graduates push for minutes alongside senior professionals.

Defensively, Bakhar was candid about last season's shortcomings. "We weren't balanced last season. Our goal is to be much better defensively," he said, identifying it as the clearest area for improvement heading into the new campaign.

Behind the scenes, the club has also refreshed its coaching staff, bringing in David Marten as assistant coach and Lidor Ganon as fitness coach, while winger Dolev Haziza has left the club during the transfer window.

Saturday's fixture at Sammy Ofer Stadium is a Toto Cup group match rather than a league fixture, but as the traditional season curtain-raiser and a derby against Hapoel Haifa, it gives Bakhar an early public test of the retooled squad he described in Haifa on Thursday.

title: Maresca faces the media at Manchester City: 'Every manager would want Rodri'
dek: In his first press conference as Pep Guardiola's successor, the Italian confirmed Rodri will have back surgery on Monday and dismissed the swirling Real Madrid speculation around his World Cup-winning midfielder.

verificationSources.label: ONE — original report
beIN Sports
Yahoo Sports

body: Enzo Maresca finally faced the media as Manchester City's manager on Thursday, and it took only a few questions before the conversation turned to the one storyline hanging over his new job: whether his first City season is about to begin without Rodri in it.

"Around big players there are always rumors, so I'm not worried about that," Maresca said, according to ONE. "Every manager would want Rodri in their team, because he is a player of the highest level." The comment was as close as the new boss came to acknowledging the noise around a possible Rodri exit to Real Madrid this window.

Maresca also put a firm date on the Spaniard's next steps. "He will have back surgery on Monday," he said. "After that he needs vacation, rest, recovery, and then he will come back to us." That points to the operation taking place on July 27, with no announced timetable for a return to training.

The context is hard to ignore. Rodri captained Spain to World Cup glory this summer and picked up the tournament's Golden Ball as its outstanding player, only to need surgery on a back complaint weeks later. His City contract runs only to the summer of 2027, and Spanish reports have persistently linked him with a return home to Real Madrid, even if nothing concrete has been reported between the two clubs.

Maresca chose not to fight that speculation head-on, framing it instead as the inevitable price of coaching one of the world's outstanding midfielders. His tone suggested confidence that Rodri's rehabilitation, not a transfer saga, will be the more pressing issue in the coming months.

On the bigger question of his own appointment, Maresca was fulsome in his praise for the man he is replacing. "It is a great privilege to replace Pep, and the fact that the club chose me is an enormous honor," he said, before adding: "I consider Pep the best manager in the world in the last 20-25 years."

Maresca arrives at the Etihad Stadium with a resume built quickly and impressively. He led Leicester City to the Championship title in 2023-24, then moved to Chelsea, where he won the UEFA Conference League and the FIFA Club World Cup across the following two seasons before City came calling to replace Guardiola this summer.

It is a considerable brief to inherit: nearly a decade of trophies under Guardiola, and a squad whose defensive-midfield identity has been built almost entirely around Rodri since his arrival from Atlético Madrid. Managing that transition — with his best pivot facing surgery rather than pre-season training — will be Maresca's first real test before a ball is even kicked.

title: LeBron James joins the 76ers, reshaping the balance of power in the East
dek: The 41-year-old's bargain two-year deal ends eight seasons with the Lakers and pairs him with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE
ESPN
NBC News
Yahoo Sports - 76ers hire Mike Gansey
Yahoo Sports - projected lineup

body: LeBron James is leaving the Los Angeles Lakers. After eight seasons in purple and gold that included the franchise's 17th championship in the pandemic-bubble title run of 2020, the 41-year-old has signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, closing off months of speculation that had tied him to the Cleveland Cavaliers, the Miami Heat and the Golden State Warriors.

The terms tell their own story. James has agreed to a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, starting at just under $3.9 million this season — a steep drop from the roughly $53 million he earned with the Lakers last year. For a player who has rarely lacked leverage, this is a deal built around one thing only: a shot at a fifth championship ring.

ONE frames the move as a shift in the balance of power in the Eastern Conference, and the roster around James explains why. Philadelphia now pairs him with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, the five-time All-Star acquired from the Boston Celtics earlier this summer in a trade that sent Paul George and four draft picks to Boston. A projected starting five of Maxey, rookie guard VJ Edgecombe, Brown, James and Embiid would carry two Finals MVPs and multiple former All-Stars in a single lineup.

James explained the decision in his own words, saying he had been ready to walk away after last season before reconsidering. "I thought I was done when the season ended," he said. "I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game." He added: "I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship. I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team." He called it, simply, "my last decision."

The recruitment carries a personal thread. Mike Gansey, hired in May as Philadelphia's new president of basketball operations in place of Daryl Morey, has known James since their days in Ohio and worked alongside him during his second Cleveland stint, the one that ended with the Cavaliers' 2016 championship. He rebuilt the roster within weeks of taking the job, with landing James as the headline move.

There is also an agency thread running through the deal. James and Maxey are both represented by Rich Paul's Klutch Sports Group, and Maxey is reported to have joined Embiid and Brown in actively lobbying James to choose Philadelphia. Paul has said publicly that acquiring Brown "changed everything" in making the 76ers a viable landing spot for his client.

On the floor, James arrives not as a saviour but as a complementary piece — a role reversal that would have been unthinkable a few years ago. He is coming off a season in which he averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds in 60 games for the Lakers and earned his 22nd career All-Star selection. In Philadelphia, he is expected to slot in at power forward, help orchestrate the offense and lean on his experience in high-leverage moments rather than carry the scoring load.

The obvious risk sits with Embiid. The 76ers' former MVP centre has played only 96 regular-season games across the last three seasons because of injury, and any title hopes built around this roster depend heavily on his health holding up through a full campaign.

This is now the fourth franchise of James's career, after two stints in Cleveland, a run in Miami and eight years in Los Angeles, and it arrives as he chases a fifth championship before retirement. Few players have reshaped the league's landscape as often as he has, and the Eastern Conference now has to reckon with a Philadelphia roster that, on paper, has few peers — provided Embiid can stay on the floor to make use of it.

For the teams that missed out — Cleveland, Miami and Golden State were all reported to have pursued him — the summer ends with nothing to show for their interest. For the Lakers, it closes a chapter that delivered a championship and eight years of relevance. For Philadelphia, training camp now opens under the heaviest expectations the franchise has carried in a generation, built almost entirely inside a single, frantic offseason.

title: Pogačar smashes 30-year-old Alpe d'Huez record on stage 19
dek: The Slovenian's imperious ascent shattered Marco Pantani's 1995 mark and pushed his overall lead past seven minutes with two days of the Tour de France left.

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Tadej Pogačar did not just win another mountain stage of the Tour de France on Thursday. He rewrote a piece of cycling history that had stood since before he was born, tearing up Alpe d'Huez's 21 hairpins in a time nobody had ever come close to.

The Slovenian covered the mythical 13.1-kilometre climb, which averages 8.1%, in 35 minutes and 27 seconds at the end of stage 19's 128km run from Megève. That obliterated the reference mark of 36:50 set by Marco Pantani in 1995, a time so revered that generations of climbers had been measured against it and found wanting.

Pogačar's margin over the Italian legend, more than a minute, is startling given how much faster professional cycling has become in the three decades since, with better roads, lighter bikes and radios replacing the primitive conditions of Pantani's era.

The victory was his fifth stage win of this Tour de France, underlining a level of dominance rarely seen on the biggest stage of the sport. It came after UAE Team Emirates-XRG's leader had trailed the day's breakaway by more than three minutes on the road to the foot of the climb.

He hunted the escapees down methodically before launching his decisive attack roughly 11.7km from the summit, on the lower slopes where Alpe d'Huez's switchbacks first bite. From there it was a procession, the Slovenian pulling away in front of the thousands of fans who had turned the mountain into a wall of noise.

Lenny Martinez, riding for Bahrain Victorious, held on for second place, with Richard Carapaz of EF Education-EasyPost completing the podium after both had been dropped inside the final kilometre of their own escape.

Behind them, the general classification picture barely stirred, because there was little left to contest. Remco Evenepoel, still the closest challenger overall, could only finish sixth on the stage itself, 2 minutes 40 seconds slower than the man in yellow.

That gap on the day stretched Pogačar's overall advantage to 7 minutes 11 seconds heading into the race's final weekend, a cushion that all but guarantees him a fifth Tour de France title barring disaster.
Isaac del Toro sits third overall, 9:42 down, while Paul Seixas is fourth and now just 24 seconds behind the Mexican rider in the fight for the last spot on the Paris podium.

Two stages remain, including one more high-mountain test on Saturday before the traditional processional finish on the Champs-Élysées. For Pogačar, Alpe d'Huez was less a contest than a coronation — a record that had survived Lance Armstrong, Alberto Contador and every other great climber of the modern era finally falling to a rider who, at 27, is redefining what is possible on two wheels.

title: LeBron James has earned $1.7 billion since turning pro, ONE reports
dek: As the NBA's only sitting billionaire signs a minimum-salary deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, ONE breaks down the Nike, Liverpool and SpringHill deals behind his fortune.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Sportico
Forbes - SpringHill/Nike deal
Fortune - 76ers contract

body: LeBron James just agreed to a minimum-salary contract with the Philadelphia 76ers, the kind of pay cut that would rattle most 40-year-olds changing teams. James can shrug it off: according to a breakdown published by ONE, he has earned roughly $1.7 billion since turning professional in 2003 — and only a fraction of it came from playing basketball.

Of that total, ONE reports, about $550 million came from NBA salaries across 23 seasons, while some $1.15 billion has flowed in from endorsements, licensing, merchandise, investments and media ventures — the off-court machine that has made James one of the wealthiest athletes in history regardless of what any single team pays him to play.

Even this past season, business dwarfed basketball. ONE puts his 2025-26 earnings at an estimated $132.6 million, with $80 million of that generated away from the court, enough to reclaim his spot as the NBA's highest earner after Stephen Curry briefly overtook him.

The foundation was Nike. The company signed James to a deal worth more than $100 million before he had played a single NBA minute, then tore up convention in 2015 with a lifetime contract that his manager, Maverick Carter, said would pay out at least $1 billion over James's career — a commitment previously reserved for Michael Jordan. Coca-Cola and Upper Deck were among his other early sponsors, according to the report.

It is James's investment portfolio, though, that has done the heaviest lifting for his net worth over the past decade. The standout is a 2011 stake in Liverpool, taken through Fenway Sports Group when the Premier League club was valued at around $550 million. ONE puts Liverpool's current valuation at roughly $5.74 billion, a return that independent business reporting has separately described as one of the most lucrative investments in modern sports.

His media company, SpringHill — the operation built around SpringHill Entertainment and the Uninterrupted platform — was valued at $725 million when James sold a minority stake in 2021 to investors including RedBird Capital, Fenway Sports Group and Nike, a deal later folded into the production company Fulwell 73.

All of it, ONE reports, places James fourth on the list of history's highest-earning athletes once inflation is factored in, behind Michael Jordan, Tiger Woods and Cristiano Ronaldo — a ranking built less on box scores than on two decades of shrewd off-court deal-making.

The figures land at a pointed moment. James this week signed a one-year, minimum-salary contract with the 76ers, a deal reported by Forbes and Sportico to pay him a fraction of his usual NBA salary. For the league's only sitting billionaire, that pay cut barely registers against an empire built to run independently of his playing contract.

title: Eli Ohana breaks his silence on reports Netanyahu wants him on the Likud list
dek: The former Beitar Jerusalem and Israel striker admits the political arena "burns" in him, but says no formal approach has been made and recalls how his brief 2015 stint with Naftali Bennett's party ended in days.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Walla News
Walla News

body: Eli Ohana, the man Beitar Jerusalem fans still call "the King," has finally addressed the reports that Benjamin Netanyahu is weighing him for a reserved spot on the Likud election list — and rather than the flat denial he gave days earlier, he now admits the idea genuinely tempts him.

"The political arena has burned inside me for years — I might very much want this, but not at any price," Ohana told ONE, in his fullest comments yet on speculation that has swirled since Channel 12 first reported Netanyahu was considering securing him a slot on the party's Knesset list.

It marks a shift from earlier in the week, when Ohana was confronted live on his own 103FM radio show and insisted he knew nothing about it. "I don't know what you're talking about. No one has spoken to me," he said on air, an answer his co-host publicly doubted at the time.

According to Ohana's account to ONE, it was not Netanyahu himself who made contact but Amit Segal, the veteran political commentator turned Likud figure, who reached out on the party's behalf. Ohana said several other people have called him in recent days about the idea, though he does not know most of them personally.
His wife, Adi, is said to be divided on the prospect — wary of what political life would mean for the family, but ready to back him if he ultimately decides to go for it.

Ohana has been here before. Eleven years ago he agreed to join Naftali Bennett's Jewish Home party for the 2015 election, taking the number ten spot on its list, only for the arrangement to collapse within days and for him to step back almost as quickly as he had signed on.
That experience, he indicated, is why he is in no rush this time: he wants to "listen and decide" only once — and if — a formal offer actually lands, rather than react to reports and rumours.

Likud minister Eli Cohen has already weighed in publicly in Ohana's favour, calling him "a symbol" and saying he would be worthy of one of the prime minister's reserved list spots, according to Walla News.

The timing adds intrigue: Netanyahu is reported to have only around four secured spots left to hand out on the Likud list, and it remains unclear whether the party will even hold primaries given the current security situation — a separate reserved slot floated for Tali Gvaili, mother of October 7 victim Ronnie Gvaili, has also stalled, per Mako.

Now 62, Ohana remains one of Israeli football's most storied figures — a prolific striker for Beitar Jerusalem and the national team through the 1980s and 90s — and today a fixture of Israeli sports media as a pundit and radio host. Whether he adds a Knesset seat to that résumé, he insists, is a decision still very much up in the air.

title: Kangwa set to triple his wages in €4.5m Panathinaikos move from Beer Sheva
dek: Zambian midfielder agrees four-year deal in Athens after a prolific season that made him one of the Israeli league's most coveted players, ONE reports

body: Kings Kangwa is about to get a very significant pay rise. ONE reports that the Zambian midfielder has agreed to leave Hapoel Beer Sheva for Panathinaikos on a four-year contract through the summer of 2030, with a new salary of around €1 million a year — roughly triple what he was earning in Israel.

The move is also a windfall for Beer Sheva. According to the report, Panathinaikos will pay a total of €4.5 million for Kangwa: €3.8 million upfront plus a further €700,000 in performance-related bonuses.

It is a striking return on investment. Beer Sheva signed Kangwa from Red Star Belgrade in the summer of 2024 for roughly €800,000, and the 27-year-old repaid that outlay many times over on the pitch, becoming one of the Israeli Premier League's most productive midfielders.
ONE notes he made 40 appearances in all competitions last season, scoring 12 goals and adding 11 assists — numbers that explain why a club of Panathinaikos's stature moved to secure him.

The Greek giants reportedly reached an initial understanding with Kangwa as far back as May, with sporting director Stefanos Koutoulis credited by the outlet as the driving force behind the pursuit. Kangwa is set to fly to Athens for a medical and to put pen to paper once his commitments in Israel are finished.

Those commitments include one more assignment in a Beer Sheva shirt: the club's Champions League second qualifying round tie against Iceland's Víkingur Reykjavík. Beer Sheva lost the first leg 2-1 in Reykjavík on July 21, leaving Kozuk's side needing to overturn the deficit at home before Kangwa's move to Greece is finalised.

Kangwa's route to this payday has wound through several countries. Born in Kasama, Zambia, he had a brief spell with Beer Sheva as a teenager back in 2017 before returning home, then went on to play for Arsenal Tula in Russia and Red Star Belgrade in Serbia, with a loan stint at Belgium's Kortrijk along the way, before rejoining Beer Sheva permanently in 2024.

He is a regular for the Zambia national team, for whom his older brother Evans also plays. For Beer Sheva, his departure represents both a substantial financial boost and the loss of a player who had become central to the team's attacking play — a trade-off Israeli clubs increasingly face once a breakout talent catches the eye of Europe's bigger leagues.

title: American forward David Green joins Kiryat Ata

body: Ironi Lati Kiryat Ata have added an American forward with a proven college scoring record to their roster, signing David Green ahead of the new Israeli Premier League season, ONE reports.

Green, 24, stands 2.01m (6-foot-7) and plays power forward. Kiryat Ata's coaching staff see him as a genuine multi-tool piece — someone who can put the ball on the floor, attack the rim, shoot it from range and still do damage with his back to the basket.

He arrives having just wrapped up a standout year at the University of Tulsa, where he averaged 15.9 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists a game. The production earned him a spot on the American Athletic Conference's First Team and All-Rookie Team, along with all-tournament honours at the NIT.

Before Tulsa, Green spent two seasons at the University of Rhode Island, where he was already established as one of the Rams' go-to scorers — 14.2 points and 5.9 rebounds a game in 2024/25, after leading the team with 14.3 points and 4.2 rebounds the year before. Independent US college basketball records also list stops at Louisiana Tech and Hofstra earlier in his career.

"He's a highly versatile power forward with a wide skill set — a player who can handle the ball, attack the rim, shoot from outside, play post-up and score in multiple ways," Kiryat Ata coach Eldad Bentov said of the new signing, according to ONE, adding that Green's competitive streak should translate well to the physicality of Israeli basketball.

Bentov himself is entering his fourth straight season in charge at Kiryat Ata, having risen through the club as an assistant before taking over as head coach. Under him the club has reached the Israeli top flight and gone as far as the playoff and State Cup semi-finals in recent campaigns.

No contract length was disclosed in the report. Green's arrival gives Kiryat Ata another experienced American frontcourt option as they look to build a squad capable of competing again near the top of the table in 2026/27.

title: Israeli prospect David Moses set for move to Florida Atlantic
dek: The 18-year-old forward-center is leaving Ramat Hasharon for US college basketball after a breakout playoff run, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Sport5

body: David Moses, an 18-year-old forward-center who spent the past three seasons rising through Ramat Hasharon's junior and senior ranks, is on his way to Florida Atlantic University, according to a report by ONE.

The 2.10-metre (6-foot-11) prospect wrapped up his youth league campaign with numbers that marked him as one of the most closely watched teenagers in Israeli basketball, then used a strong late-season audition with Ramat Hasharon's senior team to put an exclamation point on his final months at home.

In the Israeli youth Super League, Moses averaged 24.1 points and 11.4 rebounds over 18 games, shooting an efficient 62.6% on two-point attempts and 40.4% from three-point range — a shooting split that is rare for a player his size.

Head coach Gai Kantor folded him into Ramat Hasharon's senior rotation as the club pushed through the National League playoffs, and Moses answered with 9.5 points and 4.7 rebounds in 16.5 minutes per game across 16 senior appearances.

His role grew as the games mattered more. Over Ramat Hasharon's final four league fixtures he produced 14.3 points and 7.5 rebounds in just over 20 minutes a night, and he peaked with 21 points and 13 rebounds in a playoff outing against Nahariya.

That combination — a near-seven-footer capable of stepping outside and shooting it, with the physicality to compete against grown men in a senior professional league — is precisely what has made his profile a magnet for interest from American programs, ONE reports.

Florida Atlantic, an American Athletic Conference program based in Boca Raton that reached the Final Four in 2023, would give Moses a pathway to high-level US college competition and more exposure to NBA scouts than Israel's domestic system typically offers at his age. The move has not yet been confirmed publicly by the university itself.

Moses fits a pattern that has become familiar in Israeli basketball's current generation, with teenage prospects increasingly opting for American college programs rather than staying in the domestic system through their draft-eligible years.

For Ramat Hasharon, his departure closes out a rapid three-year development arc that began when he joined the club with limited competitive experience between ninth and tenth grade, and ends with him regarded as one of the most promising talents to come through the Israeli junior pipeline in years.

Kangwa's departure leaves a considerable creative gap for Be'er Sheva to fill as they continue their European campaign, but for the player himself it marks a step up to one of Greek football's traditional powers, backed by a vocal support base he was already courting before his first training session in Athens.

title: Tax authority demands tens of millions of shekels from Maccabi Tel Aviv
dek: The Israeli Tax Authority is pursuing a claim of around 80 million shekels against the club over historic foreign-player deductions, ONE reports, including housing costs linked to a spell based in Belgrade.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv's off-field headache just got significantly more expensive. The Israeli Tax Authority is demanding roughly 80 million shekels from the club, according to a report by ONE, in a dispute that reaches back several years over the taxation of foreign players.

The claim centres on deductions the club took for foreign players' housing costs during a period based in Belgrade, as well as wage-tax obligations tied to its overseas signings, ONE reported. The Tax Authority disputes whether those deductions and payments were handled correctly under Israeli law.

Maccabi is not the first Israeli Premier League club to run into this kind of scrutiny. ONE noted that Hapoel Tel Aviv previously reached a settlement with the Tax Authority over a similar dispute concerning foreign-player taxation, and that other top-flight clubs have faced comparable claims in recent years.

Approached by ONE for comment, Maccabi Tel Aviv kept its response brief: "Maccabi is a private company that does not conduct its affairs through the media." The club did not dispute or confirm the specific figure.

According to the report, any eventual resolution is expected to see the sum paid off in instalments over several years rather than as a single lump payment, with the final settlement figure still subject to negotiation between the club and the authorities.

The tax claim lands during an already difficult stretch off the pitch for one of Israeli football's most decorated institutions, adding another financial pressure point alongside the club's other well-documented budgetary strains in recent seasons.

No official statement has been issued by the Israeli Tax Authority itself, and the precise assessment years have not been made public. As with any unresolved tax dispute, the figure reported by ONE reflects the authority's opening demand rather than a final, agreed liability.

title: Paredes says Messi had already decided the World Cup final would be his last for Argentina
dek: The Boca Juniors midfielder told DSports that his national team colleague had made up his mind before the loss to Spain — though Messi himself has yet to confirm anything.

verificationSources.label: ONE
World Soccer Talk
Infocielo
ESPN (final result)

body: Five days after Spain broke Argentine hearts in extra time at MetLife Stadium, the clearest word yet on Lionel Messi's international future has come not from the man himself, but from a teammate.

Leandro Paredes, speaking to DSports in the mixed zone at La Bombonera after Boca Juniors' 1-0 Copa Sudamericana win over O'Higgins, said he believes Messi had already resolved, before a ball was kicked in the final, that the game against Spain would be his last in an Argentina shirt.

"It hurts, because we didn't want that last match to arrive," Paredes said. "He had made a decision, which was for that to be his last match with the Argentina national team. Hopefully not, hopefully he can keep playing." He added that the choice would rest with Messi alone: "Whatever makes him happy will surely make us happy too."

The final itself ended in the cruellest way for Argentina. Spain won 1-0 after extra time on July 19, Ferran Torres converting in the 106th minute to end Argentina's bid for a fourth star. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez set a World Cup final record with 11 saves in a losing effort, unable to prevent Spain from lifting the trophy for the second time.

Messi played every minute of the 120, appearing in his third World Cup final after 2014 and 2022 — a feat matched previously only by Brazil's Cafu. It was the one major final that had eluded him at club or country level as a winner, and this time it slipped away in stoppage time of extra time.

Messi has not made any public declaration about retiring from the national team. In his own comments after the match, carried by Walla Sport, he said only that "the pain is huge, it will take time to heal the wound," stopping well short of confirming Paredes's account.

Reporting elsewhere has been less definitive. Some outlets, including beIN Sports, have suggested Messi may yet delay any international retirement and could instead be honoured with a proper farewell match at a later date — underlining that, for now, this remains a teammate's reading of the situation rather than a confirmed decision from Messi.

Argentina's manager and squad have offered similar caution in the days since the final, with coach Lionel Scaloni also declining to commit to his own future. For a team that won the 2021 Copa América and the 2022 World Cup with Messi at its core, the uncertainty over whether Sunday's final was truly his last international appearance now hangs over the entire setup.
Nothing changes that fact until Messi says so himself — but Paredes's account, from inside the dressing room, is the strongest signal yet that the captain may already have made peace with the ending.

title: LeBron James signs with Philadelphia 76ers, ending eight-year Lakers spell
dek: The 41-year-old picked the Sixers over Cleveland and Miami on a two-year, $8 million deal, saying he still loves the game and has more to give in his 24th NBA season.

verificationSources.label: ONE
ESPN
NBC News
NBC Sports Philadelphia

body: LeBron James is changing teams for the first time since 2018. The 41-year-old has agreed to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers, closing out an eight-year run with the Los Angeles Lakers and opening what will be his 24th season in the NBA, ONE reported, with the move quickly confirmed across the American sports press.

The deal is a two-year contract worth $8 million, with a player option for the second season, according to Rich Paul of Klutch Sports Group, James's longtime agent, in reporting first carried by ESPN's Shams Charania. It represents an enormous pay cut for a player who earned more than $52 million with the Lakers last season, underlining that this move was not about money.

James made the announcement himself, on X on Friday, ending weeks of speculation that had trailed him since he informed the Lakers in late June that he intended to explore his options once the season ended.

"I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game," James wrote. "I still truly love this game, and I have more to give." It was a pointed echo of the uncertainty he had voiced only weeks earlier, when he suggested his final game for the Lakers might have been the last of his career.

He framed the choice of Philadelphia in ambitious terms: "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team, and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time."

The Sixers had been widely reported as favourites in recent weeks, helped by an aggressive recruiting push from inside the locker room. Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown — acquired from the Boston Celtics earlier in the summer — were all described as active in lobbying James to join, alongside the front office.

Philadelphia beat out competition from at least ten interested teams, including two clubs with deep personal ties to James: the Cleveland Cavaliers, the franchise of his native Northeast Ohio, and the Miami Heat, where he won two championships. In his announcement, James thanked Los Angeles, Miami — which he said "will always be in my heart" — and Northeast Ohio, which he called "always home."

The move slots James into a Sixers roster already built around Embiid's health and Maxey's scoring, now reinforced by Brown's two-way ability on the wing and rising guard VJ Edgecombe. Philadelphia's front office has made no secret of its intent to build a genuine title contender around that core before Embiid's prime years run out.

For the Lakers, the departure closes a chapter that began in 2018 and delivered the 2020 NBA championship inside the pandemic bubble, along with four playoff runs and the sight of James breaking the league's all-time scoring record in a Lakers uniform. Los Angeles now enters the post-LeBron era for the first time in eight years.

At 41, James remains the league's oldest active player by some distance, and his decision to keep going — on a modest, incentive-light deal rather than chase one final marquee payday — was framed by American outlets as evidence that competing for a fifth ring, not a farewell tour, is what persuaded him to sign on for one more run.

Netanya, who had been interested in the winger for some time, moved to close the deal soon after.

Haziza arrived at Maccabi Haifa in the summer of 2019 from Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv, joining a club looking to rebuild toward the top of the table. He went on to make 182 appearances and score 33 goals, eventually wearing the captain's armband.

It turned into one of the most successful spells in the club's modern history. Haifa won three Israeli championships, the Toto Cup and the Super Cup during his time there, and in 2022/23 reached the Champions League group stage for the first time in the club's history.

Haziza pointed to that European campaign, and a match against Paris Saint-Germain in particular, as a personal career highlight, according to the ONE report — a rare, glamorous night on the club's biggest stage.
In his farewell message he thanked Maccabi Haifa's supporters, saying the connection with the fans had felt special from the moment he arrived and would stay with him always.
There is a neat symmetry to where he ends up. Haziza was born in Netanya, and his move brings him back to his home city's club for the next chapter of his career, on a deal running to 2028.
He has also represented Israel's senior national team since 2019, adding an international dimension to a résumé now closing one chapter at Sammy Ofer Stadium and opening another at Netanya Stadium.

title: Manchester City weigh move for Barcelona's Marc Bernal as a long-term Rodri successor

body: Manchester City have begun making inquiries over Marc Bernal, the Barcelona midfielder being talked up as a long-term replacement for Rodri, according to a report by ONE.

The 19-year-old, who has emerged as a fixture in Hansi Flick's plans after a long recovery from a serious ACL injury, is understood to have caught City's eye as the club maps out its midfield rebuild amid uncertainty over Rodri's future in Manchester.

ONE reports City are the first of several interested Premier League clubs to move beyond mere monitoring and sound out an approach, with Arsenal and Chelsea also said to be tracking Bernal's progress. Atlético Madrid have been mentioned as admirers domestically.

Any deal, however, faces a formidable obstacle: Bernal signed a contract extension with Barcelona through 2029 carrying a release clause reported at €500 million, giving the Catalan club total control over his future. Barcelona have shown no inclination to negotiate a sale.
Bernal has previously made his own position clear, telling reporters he sees Barcelona as his home and has rejected interest from Arsenal, Manchester United and Chelsea in the past, per Yahoo Sports.

Flick is said to hold enormous confidence in the teenager, viewing his development as one of his biggest successes since arriving at Camp Nou, and considers a departure highly unlikely in the near term.

The Spaniard's rise has drawn comparisons to Sergio Busquets, the Barcelona icon whose retirement left a void in the club's midfield identity. At 6ft 4in, Bernal shares Busquets' physical stature and reputation as a reader of the game who rarely gives the ball away.

Pep Guardiola, whose own City side is searching for Rodri's eventual successor, has previously described Bernal as 'extraordinary' after facing him in a pre-season friendly, a compliment that has only sharpened English interest in the youngster.

ONE adds that Bernal's salary remains modest relative to his standing in Flick's first team, and that Barcelona intends to bring forward contract-upgrade talks originally pencilled in for September, partly in response to the growing external interest.

Bernal was also included in Spain coach Luis de la Fuente's expanded World Cup squad and has featured in preparation fixtures, underlining how far his stock has risen since the injury that sidelined him for the best part of a year.

For now the story remains speculative: City have made contact rather than a formal bid, and with a nine-figure release clause and a player publicly committed to Barcelona, any move would likely take years rather than one transfer window to materialise.

title: Mark van Bommel appointed new Belgium head coach
dek: The former PSV, Wolfsburg and Antwerp boss succeeds Rudi Garcia and will lead the Red Devils into Nations League action against Italy in September.

verificationSources.label: Euronews
Goal.com

body: Belgium's football federation confirmed Mark van Bommel as the new head coach of the national team on Thursday, ONE reported, ending a search that began the moment Rudi Garcia's tenure ran out at the World Cup.

The 49-year-old Dutchman has signed through the end of Euro 2028, which Britain and Ireland will co-host, and is due to formally take up the post on August 15 before diving straight into Nations League preparations.

Garcia's contract was not renewed after Belgium's exit from the 2026 World Cup, where the Red Devils fell in the quarterfinals to eventual champions Spain. The Belgian federation had been searching for a coach who could reshape the squad without abandoning its remaining pockets of talent.

Van Bommel arrives with a playing pedigree few candidates could match: 79 caps for the Netherlands, a runner-up medal from the 2010 World Cup final, and championships won in the Netherlands, Spain, Germany and Italy across a career at PSV, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and AC Milan.

His coaching path has been steadier than spectacular in places — spells at PSV Eindhoven and Wolfsburg produced mixed results — but it was at Royal Antwerp where he made his name as a manager, guiding the club to the Belgian Pro League and Cup double in 2023, the team's first league title since 1957.

He will be joined on the Belgium bench by three fellow Dutchmen: Boudewijn Zenden, the former Liverpool and Barcelona winger, ex-AZ Alkmaar midfielder Maarten Martens, and the experienced Reinier Robbemond. ONE also noted van Bommel previously assisted his father-in-law, Bert van Marwijk, with the Saudi Arabia and Australia national teams.

"This is a great honor for me to be appointed Belgium national team coach," van Bommel said in comments carried by ONE. "Together with my team we will build a disciplined, ambitious and brave team capable of competing with the best national teams in the world."

Van Bommel's first assignment will be a stern one: an away trip to Rome to face Italy in the Nations League on September 25, immediately testing how quickly he can imprint his ideas on a Belgian squad still searching for direction after its golden generation's slow fade.

body: Beitar Ma'ale Adumim's Boys B side has won its way back into national youth football, sealing the Judean Shfela regional championship and, with it, promotion to Israel's new national U-17 league, ONE reports.
The margin was comfortable rather than dramatic: Ma'ale Adumim finished four points clear of Maccabi Gan Yavne, who took second, with Maccabi Ironi Ashdod completing the podium in third.

The team topped the table across two full rounds of fixtures, going 10-2-0 in the first and following up with a 9-0-3 record in the second — form good enough to hold off the chasing pack for the duration of the campaign.

The numbers behind the title tell their own story. Ma'ale Adumim scored 88 league goals, the second-highest tally in the division, while conceding only 17 — comfortably the meanest defence anyone in the Shfela group could field this season.

Much of the attacking output ran through captain Harel Abergil, who finished as the league's outright top scorer with 23 goals. At the back, goalkeeper Ido Ofer was central to a defensive record few sides came close to matching.

Coach Shai Cohen, a familiar figure in Jerusalem-area youth football after previous spells in charge of Beitar and Hapoel Jerusalem's junior sides, guided the promotion push. "We're happy with the achievement, but we hoped to do this more convincingly," Cohen said, according to ONE, crediting fitness coach Yaki Yuniov's conditioning work for the squad's stamina through a long season.

The promotion carries extra weight locally: it marks Ma'ale Adumim's first return to national-level youth competition since the 2021-22 season, giving the club's development pathway a tangible marker of progress heading into 2026-27.

title: How long should you rest between sets at the gym?
dek: A training explainer from ONE breaks down why the right rest interval depends on whether you are chasing strength, size or endurance.

verificationSources.label: ONE - כמה זמן צריך לנוח בין סט לסט באימון במכון?

body: How long should you actually wait before starting your next set? It is one of the most common questions in any weight room, and according to a training explainer published by ONE, the honest answer is that there is no single correct number for everyone.

The rest period, ONE reports, should be matched to the specific training goal. For pure strength and maximum power work — heavy compound lifts such as squats, deadlifts and bench presses — the recommendation is a lengthy three to five minutes between sets, because the central nervous system needs more time than the muscle itself to be ready to produce maximal force again.

For muscle growth, or hypertrophy training, the window narrows to roughly one and a half to three minutes. Resting less than a minute, the article notes, does not allow full recovery and tends to reduce the number of repetitions achievable in the following set, while the optimal range balances physiological recovery with keeping the muscle under enough mechanical tension.

Training for muscular endurance calls for the shortest breaks of all, around 30 to 90 seconds. Short rest intervals force the muscles and cardiovascular system to work through accumulated fatigue and improve lactate clearance, though they require dropping to noticeably lighter weights to sustain the higher volume.

The exercise itself matters too, according to ONE: compound movements that recruit large muscle groups demand more recovery time than isolated, single-joint exercises. Individual factors such as training experience, age and personal physiology also shift how much rest a lifter genuinely needs — beginners, the piece cautions, may feel ready to go again quickly even though their form has not fully recovered.

The practical takeaway is simple. Rather than guessing, ONE recommends using a stopwatch or gym timer to stay consistent and avoid starting the next set too soon, since the right amount of rest is ultimately dictated by the goal of the session, the complexity of the movement and the individual doing the lifting.
facts: Recommended rest for strength/maximum power work (squats, deadlifts, bench press): 3-5 minutes.
Recommended rest for muscle hypertrophy (growth) training: 1.5-3 minutes.
Recommended rest for muscular endurance training: 30-90 seconds.
Rest periods under one minute are said to limit recovery and reduce achievable repetitions in the next set.
Compound, multi-joint exercises are said to require longer recovery than isolated exercises.
The article recommends timing rest periods with a stopwatch/timer rather than estimating.

body: Arik Shtilman, the Rapyd co-founder and chief executive who already sponsors Maccabi Tel Aviv's basketball team, has gone from backer to would-be buyer. ONE reports he has submitted a non-binding offer worth roughly $100 million to purchase the Recanati family's entire 58% controlling stake in the club.

According to ONE, Shtilman's letter to Udi and Shai Recanati frames the move as loyalty rather than a hostile approach. He describes himself as committed to the club's future after years as a fan and its central sponsor, and pledges to invest personal time, resources and "significant capital" in Maccabi's long-term success.

The bid lands only weeks after the Recanati family exercised its right of first refusal to buy out the Federman family's Fedanco Sport holding for around $50 million, ending the Federmans' long era at the club and lifting the Recanatis' stake to 58%.

That sale effectively unwound an agreement Shtilman had reached in May to buy half of Fedanco Sport himself and join Maccabi's board, part of a wider plan to inject $30 million into the club alongside additional investors. The Recanatis' decision to activate their first-refusal rights shut that route down entirely.
Shtilman is no stranger to Maccabi's finances. Rapyd has been the club's shirt and naming sponsor since 2024, with the team playing domestically and in the EuroLeague as Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv.

ONE reports the new offer covers the Recanati family's full 58% holding, or alternatively a controlling core of it, and proposes a 30-day due-diligence window with completion targeted within 90 days — a tight timeline that signals how quickly Shtilman wants to move.

The picture is complicated by a parallel process ONE says is already under way: the Recanati family is reportedly in separate talks to sell around half of its stake to American investor Jason Levin for roughly $50 million, a deal that would also see Levin take Maccabi's seat on the EuroLeague's board of shareholders in place of Danny Federman.

ONE further reports that Guy Harel, the former Maccabi Jerusalem chief executive who also acts as an agent for Maccabi Tel Aviv head coach Oded Katz, helped facilitate contact between the Recanatis and Levin.

Neither the Recanati family nor Shtilman has commented publicly on the $100 million offer, and it is unclear whether the family — having just taken outright control after years as one of the club's three traditional power centres — has any appetite to sell out so soon.

Maccabi Tel Aviv is a six-time EuroLeague champion and the dominant force in Israeli basketball, so any change of control would rank among the largest ownership transactions in the country's sporting history — and would turn a sponsor into an owner almost overnight.

body: Hapoel Machane Yehuda have wrapped up their Liga Bet promotion campaign with a piece of housekeeping: striker Yair Shpungin, whose goals down the stretch helped drag the Petah Tikva club up to Liga Alef, has agreed to stay on for the step up, the club confirmed on Friday.

Shpungin's route to the promotion was unusual. The 30-year-old spent the first half of the season with Beitar Tel Aviv/Holon, where he scored four goals, before switching to Machane Yehuda mid-campaign. He was prolific in his new colours too, netting five more and adding assists as the club finished top of its Liga Bet South A group.

The combined haul made him one of the division's most productive forwards across the season, and manager Rami Tzvi, who remains in charge for the Liga Alef campaign, wanted him kept rather than let go after the job was done.

It is familiar territory for Shpungin. A product of the Hapoel Tel Aviv youth academy, he has built a reputation as something of a promotion specialist in Israel's lower divisions, having previously played a part in Maccabi Herzliya's rise to Liga Alef in the 2022/23 season and in Hapoel Kfar Shalem's promotion in 2019/20, among other clubs he has turned out for on the way up.

He will not be the only attacking threat Machane Yehuda take into the new season. Forward Avi Chai top-scored for the club with ten goals, while midfielder Tal Atar chipped in with three, giving the squad a spread of goals that ONE credited as central to the title-winning campaign.

For Hapoel Machane Yehuda, the promotion ends a seven-season stretch in Liga Bet and returns the club to the third tier of Israeli football. Keeping hold of Shpungin, according to the club, is meant to give them a proven scorer as they try to establish themselves rather than bounce straight back down.

title: Klopp warns he will quit as Germany coach if media targets his family
dek: In his first press conference since replacing Julian Nagelsmann, the new head coach drew a hard line on privacy — and said he would walk away without compensation if the federation ever decides it no longer wants him.

verificationSources.label: ONE
