body: Maccabi Tel Aviv have drawn a clear line for their foreign contingent this summer: prove yourselves in Europe first, and only then will the club entertain talk of selling you on.

The message was laid out on the second episode of ONE's official Maccabi Tel Aviv podcast, hosted by Raz Amir and Avi Nemani, which described the club's stance toward its international players in blunt terms — first guarantee the team's place in European competition, and only afterwards will anyone discuss a sale.

Three names were specifically tied to that directive: centre-back Tyrese Asante, winger Hélio Varela and defender Christian Blitz, all understood by the podcast to have been given the same instruction as interest in their futures builds elsewhere.
Blitz's situation carries an added layer of concern — the podcast flagged an injury the club is monitoring closely, with his fitness for the coming European fixtures still to be confirmed.

Asante, a Dutch-born defender of Ghanaian descent, and Varela, a Cape Verde international winger who arrived from Belgian side Gent and scored at this year's World Cup for his country, have both established themselves as first-team regulars under new coach Kenny Miller.

The policy is easy to justify after Wednesday's result. Maccabi routed Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0 away in the first leg of the Europa League's second qualifying round, with Sayed Abu Farhat scoring twice — including a penalty — either side of goals from Dor Peretz, Sagiv Yehezkel and Issouf Sissoko.

The win leaves the tie all but decided before the return fixture, which Maccabi will host on July 30 not in Tel Aviv but at the Adjarabet Arena in Batumi, Georgia — the venue the club has used for home European matches this season.

The podcast also credited Miller, the former Scotland and Rangers striker who took interim charge in January before being confirmed as full-time head coach in June, with building an unusually quick understanding with his squad, pointing to the connection struck up almost from his first sessions in charge as reason for optimism heading into the campaign.

Miller led Maccabi to the State Cup last season — the club's first domestic cup in five years — after they slipped to third place in both the regular season and the championship playoffs, missing out on retaining the league title. He followed that with a 3-1 Super Cup win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva this month, his first piece of silverware since being handed the job permanently.

On the recruitment side, the club continues to push to close a deal for Slovenian striker Ester Sokler, with the podcast describing the transfer from Serbia's Radnički 1923 as being on its way. Israeli reports have put the fee at roughly one million euros, with Maccabi hoping to have the 27-year-old, who scored 16 goals last season, registered in time for the European qualifiers.

title: Sissokho scores first Maccabi Tel Aviv goal as yellow-and-blue rout Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0

body: Issouf Sissokho waited almost two years for his first Maccabi Tel Aviv goal, and when it finally arrived on Thursday night it came in the most emphatic circumstances possible — a 5-0 demolition of Sheriff Tiraspol in the first leg of their Europa League second qualifying round tie.

The Malian defensive midfielder, who signed from Bordeaux in August 2024, struck in the 78th minute in Tiraspol to put the finishing touch on a rout that leaves Maccabi in near-total control of the tie ahead of next week's return leg.

"I'm very happy with this goal," Sissokho said afterwards, according to Maccabi Tel Aviv's official site. "We need to keep working hard." The club's reported headline captured the moment succinctly: he was delighted with his opener and hopeful there will be more to come.

Sissokho's strike was the last of five on a night when Maccabi never let Sheriff settle. Sayed Abu Farchi opened the scoring inside five minutes and added a second from the penalty spot in the 74th, either side of goals from Dor Peretz in the 29th minute and Sagiv Yehezkel in the 53rd.

For Abu Farchi, who has quickly become one of the team's most reliable forwards, the brace continued a strong run of form, though ONE reports he was careful not to get carried away by the scoreline. He stressed that only half the tie has been played and that Maccabi still need to finish the job at home next week to confirm their progress to the next qualifying round.

The scale of the win away from home nonetheless hands Kenny Miller's side a commanding cushion. A four-goal aggregate advantage of this size is rarely squandered in continental qualifiers, but Israeli clubs have been stung by complacency in Europe before, which explains the measured tone from the dressing room despite the scoreline.

For Sissokho personally, the goal marks a breakthrough moment. Since arriving in Israel as a defensive-minded holding midfielder, he has been used primarily for his ball-winning and distribution rather than as a goal threat, making Thursday's contribution in Moldova his first for the club in yellow and blue.

Maccabi now turn their attention to the second leg, needing only to avoid an unlikely collapse to advance in Europe's second-tier club competition and continue building on last week's Israeli Super Cup success over Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

title: Bulgarian press turns on Ludogorets after Hapoel Tel Aviv rout
dek: Sofia's sports media reacted with fury to Ludogorets' 2-0 first-leg loss to Hapoel Tel Aviv, calling the Bulgarian champions toothless and warning they need a near-miracle to survive their Conference League qualifier.

body: A morning after their team's flattest European night in years, Bulgaria's sports pages did not go easy on Ludogorets Razgrad. Following Thursday's 2-0 first-leg defeat to Hapoel Tel Aviv in the Conference League's second qualifying round, several of the country's biggest outlets tore into the perennial champions, describing a side without ideas and, in the words of one, already standing with "a foot and a half outside Europe," according to a roundup published by ONE.

The Bulgarian press did not mince words. One of the country's largest sports sites wrote that Ludogorets had "taken a beating from the Israelis" and now face elimination unless urgent changes are made before the return leg, ONE reported. Another described the team as "lacking ideas, powerless, and with their backs against the wall," arguing Hapoel could have won by an even wider margin given how little Ludogorets threatened going forward.

The defeat was also an unwelcome start for Thomas Reis, the German coach who took charge of Ludogorets earlier this month after leaving Turkish side Samsunspor. Thursday's game in Hungary was his competitive debut on the Ludogorets bench, and by the Bulgarian media's account, it was a chastening one — a team many still consider the Balkans' benchmark side left toothless in attack.

On the pitch, the story was straightforward. Hapoel Tel Aviv took the lead through Omri Altman in first-half stoppage time, then sealed the win with a second goal from Chico — the Brazilian-born defender Francisco Alves da Silva Neto — in the 89th minute. The match was played not in Israel but at the DVTK Stadion in Miskolc, northeastern Hungary, in front of roughly 6,000 spectators, since Israeli clubs are currently unable to host European fixtures on home soil for security reasons.

For Hapoel, the win carried outsized significance well beyond the scoreline. It marked the club's first appearance in continental competition in 12 years, a return that follows a turbulent stretch featuring an ownership overhaul, financial collapse and two relegations before the club fought its way back to Israel's top flight and, now, back onto a European stage.

Ludogorets, by contrast, arrive at the second leg under real pressure. The club has won the Bulgarian league in all but one season since 2012 and is used to treating qualifying rounds as a formality. Bulgarian commentators quoted by ONE argued the team will need a markedly better performance — and at least two away goals — simply to keep the tie alive.

The return leg is scheduled for July 30 at Ludogorets' own ground in Razgrad, where the Bulgarian side will have to overturn the two-goal deficit to advance. Reis will have just over a week to address whatever went wrong in Hungary before his side's European season is potentially over before it truly began.

title: Beitar Jerusalem fans attacked outside stadium before Larnaca clash
dek: Israeli supporters were assaulted in a car park near the AEK Arena roughly an hour before kickoff, with several hurt and arrests on both sides; Beitar went on to win the Conference League qualifier 1-0.

verificationSources.label: Ynetnews - Clash between Beitar and Larnaca fans

body: Violence broke out in a car park beside the AEK Arena in Larnaca on Thursday evening, roughly an hour before Beitar Jerusalem's Conference League qualifier against AEK Larnaca, after a group of home supporters set upon Israeli fans arriving for the match, ONE reported.

Several Beitar supporters were hurt in the assault, including facial injuries, according to ONE. Two of the Israelis required medical treatment but not intensive care, and one Cypriot fan was also injured in the melee before police and stadium security moved in to separate the two groups.

"Larnaca supporters attacked us. We have fans who are bleeding," ONE quoted Beitar fans at the scene as saying. They described being set upon at the stadium entrance while members of La Familia, the club's main ultras group, had already gone inside to prepare their pre-match choreography.

Accounts of the arrests varied slightly by outlet. ONE reported that six Cypriot suspects were detained along with one Israeli, while Ynet, citing its own sourcing, put the figure at seven Cypriots and two Beitar supporters arrested. Both versions agree that police moved to make multiple arrests on each side as they worked to restore order before kickoff.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir condemned the attack, calling it, per ONE, "a serious event that demonstrates antisemitism rising in Europe," and urged Cypriot authorities to "act decisively against the rioters and ensure the safety of Israelis."

The warning signs had been building for hours. Israel's Diaspora and Combating Antisemitism Ministry said Thursday evening it was monitoring reports of violent altercations around the fixture and cautioned that clashes between the two sets of fans could still escalate, according to the Jerusalem Post.

Tension had already flared the night before travel-day incidents at the team's hotel. Beitar Jerusalem issued a statement denying Cypriot media reports that its own supporters had vandalized property on Larnaca's streets, saying the local police commander confirmed to the club that Beitar fans caused no damage in the city. The club instead said tear gas deployed by police was used against AEK Larnaca supporters who "initiated an attempt to confront" the visiting fans. Management at the team's hotel, the Radisson, separately reported graffiti and a smell of cannabis smoke in the courtyard overnight, per Ynet.
The match itself went ahead as scheduled at the AEK Arena – Georgios Karapatakis, AEK Larnaca's home ground since 2016, in the second qualifying round of the Conference League.
On the pitch, Beitar Jerusalem came away with a 1-0 win, with Bryan Cravely scoring the only goal of the match in the 77th minute, according to Ynet.
The return leg is scheduled for Thursday, July 30, with Beitar's home fixture set to be staged in Romania rather than Israel, Ynet reported, though the exact venue has not yet been specified.

title: Otamendi bows out of Argentina duty after World Cup final heartbreak
dek: The 38-year-old centre-back came off the bench in the defeat to Spain and confirmed his international career is over, leaving Lionel Messi as the last man standing from Argentina's 2014 World Cup squad.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Otamendi retires from Argentina after World Cup final
NBC News - World Cup final live blog, Spain 1-0 Argentina
ESPN - Spain 1-0 Argentina match report
World Soccer Talk - Otamendi announces Argentina retirement, leaves Messi as last 2014 survivor

body: Nicolás Otamendi's Argentina career is over, and it ended in about the cruellest way a defender could imagine: as a first-half substitute in a World Cup final his side went on to lose. The 38-year-old confirmed his international retirement in the aftermath of Sunday's defeat to Spain, ONE reported.

Spain won the 2026 final 1-0 at New York/New Jersey Stadium, with Ferran Torres settling a tense, goalless contest deep into extra time in the 106th minute. It was Spain's second World Cup title, after 2010, and it denied Argentina the chance to defend the crown Lionel Messi and company won in Qatar four years earlier.

Otamendi's part in the final was itself dramatic. He was thrown on in the first half to replace the injured Lisandro Martínez and, according to ONE, was involved in a heated flashpoint with Spain's Rodri as tempers frayed in a match that stayed level until the closing minutes of extra time.

Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez was the closest thing his side had to a hero, making a string of saves — a World Cup final record, by several counts — to keep the score down before Torres finally broke through.

Speaking after the match, Otamendi made clear the final whistle also closed the book on his time in an Argentina shirt. "I'm leaving with my head held high, knowing this team fought until the last second," he said, in comments carried by ONE. "Since I was a child I dreamed of wearing the Argentina national team shirt... I leave in peace of mind, knowing I gave everything. The titles remain in history, but love for these colours lasts forever."

The decision was not entirely a surprise. Otamendi had signalled before the tournament that this World Cup would be his last with the national side, telling reporters at the time that "after the World Cup, a cycle with the national team comes to an end... I'll just be another fan."

He leaves with 130 caps to his name, a run that began in April 2009 when he was first called up by Diego Maradona. Along the way he won the 2022 World Cup and a Copa América with Argentina, cementing himself as one of the most durable defenders of his generation. His departure leaves Messi as the only player from Argentina's 2014 World Cup squad still turning out for the national team.

In this tournament itself, Otamendi's involvement was more understudy than starter — he made seven appearances across Argentina's eight games but started just once, with his role largely that of a senior voice in the squad and, when called upon, emergency cover, as it was for the final.

His playing career, though, goes on. Otamendi had already lined up his next chapter before the World Cup, signing an 18-month deal with boyhood club River Plate after leaving Benfica on a free transfer. The move, in place since late May, sees him return to Argentine domestic football for the first time in 16 years, calling it a lifelong dream after growing up supporting the Buenos Aires club.

For a defender who built his reputation over spells in Portugal, Spain and England before captaining Benfica, going home to River Plate now carries a different kind of finality — the last international chapter closed on the biggest stage of all, with the club chapter of retirement still very much to be written.

title: Belić's Return Lasts Eight Minutes as Maccabi Rout Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0
dek: Kristijan Belić was helped off in tears just minutes after coming on, but Maccabi Tel Aviv brushed that aside to hammer Sheriff Tiraspol in their Conference League qualifier.

body: Kristijan Belić's night as a Maccabi Tel Aviv substitute lasted barely eight minutes. Sent on in the 64th minute of Thursday's Conference League second qualifying round first leg against Sheriff Tiraspol, the Serbian midfielder went down clutching an injury just six minutes later and had to be helped off the pitch in the 72nd, according to ONE.

The outlet reported that Belić lay on the turf for close to two minutes signalling he could not continue, before leaving the field in visible distress, "crying in frustration" as he was escorted away. Dan Glazer came on in his place.

It capped a frustrating few days for the 24-year-old, who had already been battling a knock heading into the match. Sport1 reported that Belić failed to complete Thursday morning's session in full, leaving his availability in doubt right up to kickoff.

None of it took the shine off Maccabi's evening. The yellows were ruthless in Moldova, racing into a 2-0 lead inside the opening half-hour through Saied Abu Farhia and Dor Peretz, before Sagiv Jehezkel, a second Abu Farhia goal from the penalty spot and Issouf Sissokho turned a comfortable lead into a rout by the final whistle.

A 5-0 first-leg score in a two-legged European qualifier all but settles the tie before Maccabi even host the return fixture, sparing Kenny Miller's side any late nerves over Belić's fitness for the second leg — though the club will now be assessing the extent of the injury.

Belić arrived at Maccabi last summer on loan from AZ Alkmaar, having previously come through Partizan Belgrade and represented Serbia at senior international level. The club has since exercised its option to sign him permanently, on a contract running through 2029, making him one of the squad's more significant long-term investments — and adding weight to any concern over a fresh injury setback.

title: Tiberias Turns to Youth Chief Ozen After Head Coach Suspended in Saline-Drip Case
dek: With Eliran Hudeda provisionally suspended amid an anti-doping investigation into IV fluids given to players, Ironi Tiberias have handed the reins to academy director Maurice Ozen for at least a month.

verificationSources.label: ONE - מוריס אוזן יאמן את עירוני טבריה בחודשה הקרוב
Sport5 - מוריס אוזן יאמן את טבריה באופן זמני

body: Ironi Tiberias have turned to one of their own to steady the ship: Maurice Ozen, the club's youth-department technical director, has been installed as interim first-team coach for at least the coming month, ONE reported.

The move is a direct consequence of the club's biggest off-field crisis in years. Israel's National Anti-Doping Authority has provisionally suspended regular head coach Eliran Hudeda pending the outcome of an investigation into intravenous fluids administered to players, leaving the dugout empty at a critical point in the season.

The case was triggered by a complaint from Ashdod, who alleged that Tiberias players received more than 100cc of saline solution during a break in a playoff match - a volume the complaint says breaches the limits set by the World Anti-Doping Agency for permitted infusions.

Suspended alongside Hudeda are technical director Chen Sol, a member of the fitness staff, and five players - David Kaltins, Guy Hadida, Niv Gutleib, Sambinha and Yonatan Tefer - according to Walla Sport and other Israeli outlets that have followed the case closely.

Tiberias have pushed back hard on the allegations. In a defense filing reported by Ynet, the club argued the saline given was a clean, legal solution administered within the volume permitted under WADA regulations, and not a doping violation at all.

Reporting around the case has suggested the five suspended players are likely to be cleared or face only minimal sanction, with Hudeda himself viewed by the disciplinary process as the central figure in the affair - one reason the club felt compelled to find an immediate solution in the dugout rather than wait out a lengthy suspension.

That solution is Ozen, a well-known figure in Tiberias' recent history. He is remembered locally as the only coach to take a team from Liga Alef and eliminate a Liga Leumit club from a promotion playoff twice in the same series, a feat he pulled off against Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem on the way to lifting Tiberias into the National League.

For his interim spell on the bench, Ozen will be assisted by fitness coach Ehud Ben Shushan and assistant coach Moti Krispiel, who is still completing his coaching certification, per Sport5's doublepass.

The timing could hardly be worse for the club sportingly. Tiberias have been fighting to preserve their place in Ligat Ha'al through the closing playoff rounds, and the saline affair has already cost them financially, with the club implementing salary cuts across the staff after sponsors pulled back in the wake of the scandal.

Club ownership has pushed back publicly against how the case has unfolded, framing it, in comments carried by ONE, as a process handled in haste rather than one built on solid evidence - a stance the club intends to press when the matter reaches the sports tribunal.

For now, Ozen's mandate is explicitly short-term. Should Hudeda's suspension extend well beyond the initial period, Tiberias have indicated they will look at appointing a permanent replacement rather than leaving the academy director to carry the senior team indefinitely.

dek: Play was suspended for five minutes in Hungary after Israeli fans lit smoke grenades and flares during Hapoel's first continental fixture in 12 years, leaving the club exposed to possible UEFA censure.

body: Five minutes into what was supposed to be a triumphant return to European football, Hapoel Tel Aviv's Conference League opener against Ludogorets Razgrad was brought to a halt on Thursday evening, after smoke from flares lit by the club's own supporters drifted across the pitch and forced the referee to stop play, ONE reported.

Swiss referee Alessandro Dudic suspended the match as the haze thickened around the edge of the box, according to ONE, and did not allow it to restart until the smoke had cleared roughly five minutes later.

The stoppage came on a night that was meant to be a celebration in its own right. It was Hapoel's first fixture in continental competition in 12 years, ending a long absence from Europe for one of Israel's most storied clubs.

There was never any prospect of it feeling like a true home game, though. With Israeli clubs currently unable to host European matches on home soil for security reasons, Hapoel's nominal "home" leg was staged instead at the Diósgyőri Stadion in Miskolc, in northeastern Hungary.

That did not stop the travelling support from turning out in force. ONE reported that roughly 30 buses carried thousands of Hapoel fans on the two-and-a-half-hour drive from Budapest to Miskolc for kickoff.

It was that same travelling crowd that produced the pyrotechnics which brought the game to a standstill — a recurring flashpoint at European away days involving Israeli supporters, and one that now leaves the club exposed to possible disciplinary proceedings from UEFA over the use of flares and smoke grenades inside the stadium, per ONE's report.

The match is the first leg of a second qualifying round tie in the Conference League. Ludogorets, the dominant force in Bulgarian football for well over a decade, will host the return fixture on July 30 at their own ground in Razgrad.

A full-time result was not yet confirmed at the time of writing. This report covers the confirmed details of the flare-related stoppage as reported by ONE, rather than the eventual outcome of the tie's opening leg.

title: Gloukh opens his season's account as Ajax rout Vojvodina 4-1

body: Oscar Gloukh got his season up and running on Thursday night, scoring Ajax's third goal in a commanding 4-1 win away to FK Vojvodina in the first leg of their Conference League second qualifying round tie, ONE reported.

The Israel international's goal came in the 52nd minute in Novi Sad. Winger Mika Godts drove in from the left and slipped a pass into the box, and Gloukh needed only two touches — one to control, one to finish — beating Vojvodina goalkeeper Rosic with a firm strike into the middle of the goal.

It capped an eventful evening for the Dutch side. Davy Klaassen had put Ajax ahead inside three minutes, before Vojvodina's Petar Sukačev levelled it in the 28th. Steven Berghuis restored the lead just before half-time, Gloukh made it 3-1 after the break, and substitute Mohamed Abdalla added a fourth deep into stoppage time.

Gloukh, who started the match, was withdrawn in the 69th minute, with Ajax's coaching staff managing his minutes with the second leg — scheduled for next Thursday at the Johan Cruijff ArenA in Amsterdam — already in view.
The result gives Ajax a comfortable cushion heading into that home leg, as they aim to progress through Europe's third-tier club competition and reach the league phase.
It was also a landmark night for two of the club's other new arrivals: Henrique and Abdalla both made their competitive debuts for Ajax, with Abdalla marking his with the final goal of the rout.

Gloukh joined Ajax from Red Bull Salzburg last August for a reported fee of around €14.75 million, potentially rising to €17.25 million with add-ons, signing a five-year contract. He came through the Maccabi Tel Aviv youth academy before moving to Salzburg in January 2023.

In his first season in Amsterdam, the 22-year-old contributed six goals and six assists in the Eredivisie and added three goals in the Champions League — numbers that made him one of the more productive newcomers in Dutch football last year, and a big reason expectations are high again this season.

title: Kiryat Yam add Bognim and Agbaria as they aim for another playoff push

body: Kiryat Yam have made their first significant moves of the summer, bringing in forward Itay Bognim from Hapoel Haifa and left back Fares Agbaria from newly promoted Hapoel Ramat Gan, ONE reports, as the north-coast club looks to build on a strong debut Liga Leumit campaign.

Bognim, 25, leaves Hapoel Haifa after six years at the club, the last five of them as a senior squad member following his debut as a substitute against Beitar Jerusalem in January 2021. He managed one league goal for Haifa last season, but ONE describes him as a genuinely talented attacking player, and he arrives at Kiryat Yam to join an attacking group that already features Sako Silla, Ashley Copido and Ilya Potkin.

Agbaria, 21, is a different kind of addition: a left-sided defender who spent the past season on loan at Hapoel Ramat Gan and played a significant role in that club's promotion to Ligat Ha'al, scoring twice in the deciding playoff matches that sealed it. Ramat Gan's promotion was itself a notable story - the club returned to Israel's top flight in May after 13 straight seasons in Liga Leumit.

Agbaria's move to Kiryat Yam is a step down a division in terms of where he'll be playing next season, but it puts him at a club with real ambitions of its own and gives him another shot at regular senior football after a breakout loan spell.

Kiryat Yam's own rise has been rapid enough to rival Ramat Gan's. Re-established in 2021 after an earlier incarnation folded, the club shot up from Liga Gimel through the lower divisions, highlighted by an unbeaten debut season in which it won every one of its 22 games and scored well over a hundred goals. It arrived in Liga Leumit for the first time only last season.

According to ONE, the club's stated aim now is to reach the upper playoff bracket again after an impressive first campaign in the division, and the Bognim and Agbaria signings are being framed as reinforcements toward that end - proven experience up front, and a defender arriving fresh from tasting promotion himself.
Neither deal comes with financial terms disclosed, and Kiryat Yam's business is expected to continue as preseason approaches.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv Thrash Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0 to Open European Campaign
dek: Kenny Miller hails a "fantastic" away display in Moldova as Sayed Abu Farhi's brace and goals from Dor Peretz, Sagiv Yehezkel and Issouf Sissokho put Maccabi in near-total control of their Europa League qualifier.

verificationSources.label: Sofascore match report
ESPN match center

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv opened their 2026-27 European campaign with real authority, hammering Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0 away in the first leg of the Europa League second qualifying round on Thursday night at the Sheriff Stadium in Tiraspol, Moldova.

The visitors were ahead inside five minutes through young striker Sayed Abu Farhi, and Dor Peretz doubled the lead in the 29th minute to send Kenny Miller's side in at the break with a commanding cushion.

Maccabi kept their foot down after the restart. Sagiv Yehezkel made it 3-0 in the 73rd minute, Abu Farhi completed his brace from the penalty spot a minute later, and Issouf Sissokho rounded off the scoring in the 78th to leave a five-goal aggregate lead to defend in the return leg.
"We were the better team tonight," Miller said afterwards, quoted by ONE. "We scored five goals and could have scored even more."
The Scottish manager pointed to the fast start as the platform for the rout. "We opened the match very well with an early goal, and we should have scored more in the first half," he said.

He did allow himself one note of caution amid the celebration. "The only downside was towards the end of the match, where we perhaps felt too comfortable," Miller said, wary of any late lapse even with the tie all but settled.
But he was unequivocal about the bigger picture. "This was a fantastic away performance in Europe, and you cannot be disappointed with a 5-0 victory," he said.

The result leaves Maccabi in near-total control ahead of the return leg on Thursday, July 30 — which, as with most "home" European fixtures for Israeli clubs at present, will be staged at a neutral venue in Batumi, Georgia rather than at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv.
Advancing on aggregate would send Maccabi into the Europa League's third qualifying round; only a dramatic reversal in Batumi would instead drop them into the Conference League path.
For Miller, the scoreline offers an early marker that his squad can carry momentum into Europe as the club builds toward the new Israeli Premier League season.

title: Beitar Jerusalem take slender lead to Europe after Carabalí's free-kick sinks ten-man Larnaca
dek: A rare goal from centre-back Brayan Carabalí gave new coach Almog Cohen a winning start in Europe, as Beitar Jerusalem beat AEK Larnaca 1-0 away in the Conference League second qualifying round.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Walla Sport
Sport1 (Maariv)

body: Beitar Jerusalem opened their European campaign with exactly the kind of result they needed: a disciplined, occasionally nervy 1-0 win away to AEK Larnaca in the first leg of their Conference League second qualifying round tie on Thursday night in Cyprus.

The only goal came in the 77th minute, and it came from an unlikely source. Centre-back Brayan Carabalí stepped up to a free kick just outside the box and curled it into the corner, wrong-footing the Larnaca goalkeeper for what several Israeli outlets described as a rare strike from the Colombian defender.

The set piece was a direct consequence of AEK Larnaca being reduced to ten men two minutes earlier. Dutch defender Mike van der Hoorn was sent off in the 75th minute for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity, handing Beitar both the man advantage and the position from which Carabalí struck.

According to Sport1's match report, Beitar had already begun to take control of the game from around the half-hour mark, with Daniel Worku and Noam Mouche driving play in midfield before a round of substitutions after the hour — among them Timo Mozzi — added fresh legs to the visitors' attack.

Just as notable as the goal was the clean sheet. Beitar were without Luka Gadrani, Carabalí's regular partner at the back who has been central to what has been one of the sturdier defensive pairings in Israeli football, but held firm regardless against a Cypriot side that pushed for an equalizer once down to ten men.

The win was also a personal landmark. It was Almog Cohen's first victory since taking charge of Beitar Jerusalem, having moved from the club's sporting director role to the touchline in May after Barak Yitzhaki's departure as head coach — his managerial debut coming in Europe rather than the domestic league.

ONE reported that the trip to Cyprus was overshadowed by incidents of crowd violence involving fans before kickoff, with Beitar supporters targeted in the build-up to the match — a sour note around a tie that otherwise went the visitors' way on the pitch.

Beitar now carry their one-goal advantage into next week's second leg, which is scheduled to be played in Ploiești, Romania rather than Israel, continuing the arrangement under which Israeli clubs have staged their UEFA home fixtures at neutral venues abroad because of the security situation at home.

A place in the next qualifying round is now well within reach, though Cohen's side will know a narrow first-leg lead in a two-legged European tie is far from decisive, and they will need to manage the return fixture carefully against opponents who will throw everything at reversing the scoreline.

title: Blazers coach Nori's first season seen hinging on Deni Avdija's leap
dek: ONE reports that NBA analyst Andrew Carlson believes new Portland head coach Micah Nori's debut season will be shaped above all by how far Deni Avdija progresses, alongside Ja Morant's integration and a short-term contract that leaves little room for error.

verificationSources.label: ONE - report on Nori, Avdija and Portland's outlook
ESPN - Trail Blazers hiring Micah Nori as coach

body: Portland's rebuild has a new coach and a new co-star point guard this summer, but according to ONE, the man who will make or break Micah Nori's first season on the Trail Blazers bench is still the same one who carried the team through last year's chaos: Deni Avdija.

ONE cites NBA analyst Andrew Carlson, who covers the Minnesota Timberwolves for SI's On SI network, as saying the central question for Portland this season 'is really how big a leap Deni Avdija makes this season, how Ja Morant fits in, and how the roster around them strengthens.' Carlson added that if Nori finds the right rotation and Morant returns to his best form, he could see Portland winning a playoff series.
It is a notable vote of confidence in Avdija specifically, at a moment when Portland's coaching staff, roster and front office have all been rebuilt within the space of a single off-season.

Nori, 52, was formally hired as head coach in late June after five seasons as Minnesota's lead assistant under Chris Finch, a stint that made him one of the most sought-after assistants in the league. He replaces Tiago Splitter, who had been serving as interim coach since October 2025, when Chauncey Billups was arrested as part of an FBI investigation into an illegal gambling operation. Splitter steered Portland to a 42-40 record and the franchise's first playoff appearance since 2021, before the Trail Blazers were eliminated in the first round by San Antonio.

Carlson, per ONE, was unsurprised by Nori's promotion, calling him 'one of the most respected assistant coaches in the league' and pointing to his skill at in-game management as his biggest asset alongside his ability to connect with players.

He was more skeptical, however, about the contract Portland gave him: a deal with only one guaranteed season and club options for two more. Carlson called the structure 'weird,' arguing a single season is not enough time for a first-time head coach to install a system and properly evaluate roster fit. The unusual terms have already drawn public criticism elsewhere in the league - Cleveland's J.B. Bickerstaff called it a 'slap in the face' to the value of NBA coaches.

Ja Morant's arrival adds another variable Nori will have to manage from day one. Memphis traded the 26-year-old point guard to Portland this off-season in exchange for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray, pairing him in the backcourt with a Trail Blazers team still built around Avdija's playmaking.

Avdija's own trajectory is exactly why the comparison matters. He earned his first NBA All-Star selection in 2025-26, averaging roughly 24.5 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.8 assists a game, and emerged as Portland's most consistent performer through a season disrupted by injuries and the upheaval around Billups' departure.

None of that guarantees anything for the coming season. But ONE's framing, echoing Carlson's assessment, is that Nori inherits a team whose ceiling is largely already defined by an Israeli forward who spent last season proving he could carry it - and whose next step, more than any tactical wrinkle Nori installs, may decide how his tenure in Portland is judged.

title: At 85, Avraham Bachar hears from the coaches he shaped
dek: The former Maccabi Tel Aviv winger turned youth-football lifer marks his 85th birthday as colleagues from across three decades of Israeli coaching pay tribute, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE - 85 לאברהם בכר: שותפים לדרך מצדיעים
Hebrew Wikipedia - אברהם בכר (מאמן כדורגל)

body: Avraham Bachar turned 85 on Thursday - the exact anniversary of his birth in 1941 - and rather than let it pass quietly, ONE gathered four people who worked alongside him across Israeli youth football to say what he meant to them.
Bachar is one of the sport's quieter institutions: a left winger who never became a household name as a player but who spent the following half-century shaping the coaches and teenagers who did.
He came up through Maccabi Tel Aviv's youth ranks and played for the first team between 1960 and 1964, before finishing his playing days at Hapoel/Samson Tel Aviv and retiring in 1968 at 27.

The coaching career that followed dwarfed the playing one. Bachar took charge of Maccabi Jaffo in 1975 and Hapoel Tel Aviv the following season, then moved through youth departments at Hapoel Tel Aviv, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Kfar Saba, Hapoel Herzliya, Maccabi Ramat Chen and Hapoel Bat Yam over the decades that followed.

His most enduring imprint, though, came in a national team tracksuit: from 1994 to 2006 he worked with Israel's boys' and youth national sides, a twelve-year stretch that took in more than 150 official matches.

That body of work was formally recognised in August 2019, when President Reuven Rivlin presented Bachar with the President's Award in honour of his decades of contribution to youth football education in Israel.

More recently he served eight seasons as professional director of Hapoel Herzliya's youth department, from 2017, before stepping back this year into an advisory role with the club - the perch from which, at 85, he is still watching the game he helped build.

For the birthday piece, ONE turned to four figures whose careers intersected with his. Zeev "Zavik" Zalzer, the former player, coach and now football commentator, worked beside Bachar on the youth national teams for a dozen years and recalled him as a player first - "technical, quick, a winger who executed passes with precision and always set others up."

Yossi Shvachon, who trained under Bachar before becoming a coach himself, put it more bluntly: working with him, he said, was the moment he realised how much about football he still didn't understand - crediting Bachar with instilling tactical awareness alongside the values that came with it.

Meyan Negev, who now runs Hapoel Herzliya's youth department where Bachar still advises, called his continued presence there "a great privilege for us all." Amit Artzi, the professional manager at Hapoel Kfar Saba who coached under Bachar earlier in his career, said what stayed with him most was less tactical than personal - "a human approach" to coaching young players.

Little of what Bachar built is visible on a highlights reel. It sits instead in the coaching staffs and federation programmes now run by people he trained thirty and forty years ago - which is precisely why, on his 85th birthday, it was they who did the talking.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv were putting together one of their most emphatic nights in Europe in years on Thursday, leading Sheriff Tiraspol 5-0 deep into the second half of their Europa League second qualifying round opener in Moldova, according to a live-updated report from ONE.

ONE's rolling coverage had the scoring wrapped around a brace from forward Sayed Abu Farhi, who opened the account in the 5th minute and added a second in the 74th. Dor Peretz made it 2-0 in the 29th minute, Sagiv Yehezkel struck in the 53rd and Issouf Sissokho completed the rout in the 78th, with the match still being played as ONE's report was last updated at the 84-minute mark — meaning the final score had not yet been confirmed at the time of writing.

The one sour note for Kenny Miller's side was an injury to defender Christian Blitz during the match, per ONE. Blitz's fitness had already been a live question in the build-up: Sport1 reported earlier in the week that his availability for the trip to Moldova was uncertain.

Maccabi arrived in Tiraspol high on confidence. The club opened its season with a 3-1 win over Hapoel Beer Sheva in the Israeli Super Cup, and Israeli outlets covering the build-up noted the Yellow-and-Blue had looked sharp in every department of that game.

Sheriff Tiraspol, the reigning Moldovan champions, reached this round by eliminating Slovenia's Olimpija Ljubljana — a scoreless draw at home followed by a 1-0 win away, according to Ynet's preview of the tie. On paper it made them a credible European qualifying test, but they were second-best for long stretches of Thursday's first leg.

The rout, if it holds, would represent a near-decisive result before the return fixture. Maccabi are not permitted to host European matches on home soil this season and will stage the second leg on July 30 in Batumi, Georgia — a logistical wrinkle that has shaped much of their continental planning but did nothing to blunt their attacking edge in Moldova.

A five-goal cushion with the game still being played would leave Sheriff Tiraspol needing an extraordinary turnaround in Georgia next Thursday just to force extra time on aggregate. Maccabi's progression to the third qualifying round already looks close to a formality, pending official confirmation of Thursday's final score.

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv are bracing for another summer of suitors circling their back line. According to ONE, centre-back Tyrese Asante has emerged as a target for three clubs, with Serie A side Lecce leading the interest.

The 24-year-old Dutchman has been one of the most consistent defenders in the Israeli Premier League over the past two seasons, and ONE reports Lecce see him as a genuine option to reinforce their defence for next season.

There is a neat subplot to the Lecce interest: the Puglia club is already home to Omri Gandelman, the Israel international midfielder who joined from Belgium's KAA Gent in January. Should Asante follow him south, the two would become teammates in Serie A.

Gandelman signed with Lecce on a contract running until June 2029, with an option for a further year, after two prolific seasons in Belgium. A move for Asante would give the club a second player with deep ties to Israeli football.
ONE's report adds that Monza continue to monitor Asante's situation, while Kasımpaşa of Turkey have gone furthest of all, submitting a formal offer for the defender.

That Monza interest is not solely an Israeli-media story. The Dutch outlet VoetbalPrimeur reported separately this summer that Monza were among several clubs monitoring Asante, describing him there as a six-time Netherlands under-21 international drawing attention from multiple directions.

Asante arrived at Maccabi Tel Aviv in July 2024 on a three-year deal after three seasons with ADO Den Haag, where he made 89 league appearances. Born in The Hague and of Ghanaian descent, he came through the Feyenoord and Sparta Rotterdam academies before his senior breakthrough.

Nothing is close to being finalised. ONE frames the coming weeks as pivotal for the player's next move, but no fee, contract length or timeline has been reported for any of the three suitors, and Maccabi Tel Aviv have made no public comment on the interest.

title: Khalaili breaks silence after failed Inter move: 'I've played 99 games, finished almost all of them'
dek: Weeks after his record-breaking transfer to Inter Milan collapsed on a failed medical, the Israeli winger tells ONE he is back at full training with Union Saint-Gilloise and points to two years of near ever-present fitness as proof he is ready for whatever comes next.

verificationSources.label: ONE - Khalaili interview
Ynetnews - Inter cancel record Khalaili transfer after failed medical

body: Anan Khalaili has broken his silence over the collapse of what would have been the biggest transfer in Israeli football history, telling ONE this week that he is back training at full intensity and feels ready for "what awaits" him.
"I'm returning to full training to prepare for what awaits me, I feel fit and happy to be back on the pitch," the winger said, in his first extended comments since his move to Inter Milan fell apart.

The 21-year-old's transfer to the Italian champions, reported at around €23 million and set to eclipse anything paid for an Israeli player before him, unravelled in mid-July when he failed to clear the medical fitness screening required for registration in Italy. Ynetnews, Haaretz and the Jerusalem Post all confirmed Inter called off the deal after the examinations, carried out under the Italian Olympic Committee's (CONI) sports-medicine protocol, flagged a cardiac finding that blocks clearance to compete professionally in Italy.

Crucially, that ruling is specific to Italy's unusually strict registration rules and does not affect Khalaili's ability to play elsewhere. He remains free to turn out for Union Saint-Gilloise in Belgium without restriction, and the Belgian champions are expected to run their own medical assessment on his return.
In the ONE interview, Khalaili was adamant the setback has not shaken his confidence. "I'm always focused on my career and always believed in myself, I'll continue to give my best," he said.

He then pointed to his own workload as evidence of his physical condition: "I feel good, healthy, in excellent condition and ready to play and train hard to give 100 percent. I played 99 games in the last two years, completed 90 minutes in almost all of them. I feel excellent."

The two-year window covers almost exactly his time in Belgium. Khalaili joined Union Saint-Gilloise from Maccabi Haifa in July 2024, having come through the Haifa academy and made his senior breakthrough there. He has since become a regular starter for Union and a full Israel international.
His father, Majdi Khalaili, is a former Arab-Israeli goalkeeper and manager, and Anan has often spoken of growing up around the game through him.

For now, Khalaili's immediate future stays in Brussels. With the Italian market effectively closed to him under CONI's current standards, his representatives are expected to weigh interest from clubs outside Italy in the weeks ahead, but no fresh move has been confirmed.

title: De Jong pushes back on doubts over his Barcelona commitment after World Cup knee blow
dek: The Dutch midfielder says it is "difficult" to see his loyalty questioned on the back of "false reports," as Barcelona confirm a knee ligament tear that could keep him out for months.

body: Frenkie de Jong has hit back at suggestions that his commitment to Barcelona has wavered, days after the club confirmed the Dutch midfielder is carrying a knee ligament injury picked up at the World Cup.

"It's difficult for me to see people questioning my dedication to the club because of false reports," de Jong said, addressing chatter that had grown around his fitness and his future during the tournament, ONE reported.

Barcelona have confirmed a tear to the medial collateral ligament in de Jong's right knee. Scans taken after he reported back for pre-season medical checks showed the damage was more serious than first thought, with surgery not required at this stage in favour of a conservative recovery programme.

The 29-year-old had played through the injury for the Netherlands at the World Cup, wearing a protective brace after doctors initially assessed it as minor. It was only once he returned to Barcelona and underwent further testing that the full extent of the ligament damage emerged.

"My commitment to Barcelona and to my national team will never change," de Jong said, stressing that football "is everything" to him and that he has "always given everything" for both club and country.

Barcelona have not put an official number of weeks on his absence, though speculation reported by outlets including Goal.com and Barca Blaugranes has put the layoff at around four months - enough to rule him out of the start of the new La Liga season.

The club are not expected to move for a replacement midfielder in the meantime. Barcelona's hierarchy believes the squad already has cover in Pedri, Gavi, Fermín López, Dani Olmo and academy graduate Marc Bernal.

De Jong has been one of Barcelona's most important midfielders since arriving from Ajax in 2019, and the injury is a blow to a Dutch side that also leaned heavily on him through the 2026 World Cup. His absence leaves both club and country needing to adapt without a player they had built much of their midfield around.

body: Beitar Jerusalem opened their 2026/27 European campaign the hard way on Thursday evening, held scoreless through a first half in which AEK Larnaca were plainly the sharper side, according to ONE's live report from the AEK Arena - Georgios Karapatakis.

The Cypriot runners-up controlled possession for long stretches and manufactured the more threatening openings, while Beitar - set up deep and cautious - found it difficult to spring forward with any conviction. Neither side had broken the deadlock as the half wore on.

It is not the ideal backdrop for a club that arrived in Cyprus still nursing the sting of a Toto Cup exit, having lost a penalty shootout to Hapoel Tel Aviv only days earlier. ONE noted that Beitar had nonetheless shown encouraging football in that defeat, and that several of the club's players were also observing the Tisha B'Av fast around the fixture - a detail the report flagged as a possible factor on a demanding matchday in the Cypriot heat.

This is the second qualifying round of the Conference League, played as a two-legged tie: Thursday's contest in Larnaca is the first leg, with the return fixture set for July 30 at Teddy Stadium in Jerusalem. Both clubs are carrying strong domestic pedigree into the tie - Beitar finished as runners-up in Ligat Ha'al last season, while AEK Larnaca finished second in the Cypriot First Division.

AEK Larnaca are no strangers to this stage of the European calendar. The Cyprus club, whose squad and staff have carried a pronounced Spanish accent in recent seasons, have repeatedly pushed into league-phase and group-stage football in continental competition and will fancy their chances of doing so again this term.

Beitar, for their part, are looking to go one better than last season, when their Conference League run ended at the third qualifying round. The two sides have met only once before, in a 2021 friendly that finished goalless, and Beitar's only previous competitive test against Cypriot opposition came against Omonia Nicosia back in the 2016/17 European campaign.

With the first leg still goalless as it approached the interval, ONE's report offered no indication that either side had found a breakthrough by the time of writing - leaving the tie finely poised ahead of the return fixture at Teddy Stadium next Thursday.

title: Carapaz strikes late to win Tour de France stage 18 in the Alps
dek: The Ecuadorian climber soloed clear on the final slopes to Orcières-Merlette for his second career Tour stage win, while Tadej Pogačar kept the yellow jersey intact.

verificationSources.label: EF Pro Cycling (official team report)

body: Richard Carapaz timed his move to perfection on Thursday, attacking on the steepest ramps of the final climb to solo clear and win stage 18 of the Tour de France at the Orcières-Merlette ski resort, as the race left the Isère valley behind and turned into the high Alps for the first of three consecutive summit finishes.

The EF Education-EasyPost rider had spent much of the stage fighting to get into the break, bridging across after a frantic split over the Côte d'Engins and the Côte de Monteynard. Once the group reached the final 15-kilometre haul up to Orcières-Merlette, Carapaz sat tight until the gradient bit hardest before launching the decisive attack that none of his fellow escapees could answer.
He held his advantage all the way to the line, crossing roughly 45 seconds clear of Mauro Schmid of Jayco-AlUla, with Matteo Jorgenson of Visma-Lease a Bike completing the podium.
"It's been a very special moment to win here at the Tour. It's something that you have to put absolutely everything into," Carapaz said afterwards, according to his team.
"It was tricky. It was a very, very tough day... I waited for the right moment, and in the end, it just happened to be at the right time," he added.

It is Carapaz's second stage win at the Tour de France, following his triumph on stage 17 in 2024, when he also claimed the polka-dot mountains jersey. The 33-year-old Ecuadorian remains one of the sport's most decorated climbers, having won the 2019 Giro d'Italia and the road race gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics.

Further back, there was no change at the top of the general classification. Tadej Pogačar kept the yellow jersey with a commanding buffer, with Remco Evenepoel still second at 4:32 and Isaac del Toro holding third, 6:51 off the pace.
In the points competition, Mads Pedersen extended his advantage in the green jersey to 32 points as the sprinters' contest heads into its final act.

Stage 18 covered 185.2 kilometres from Voiron to Orcières-Merlette with close to 3,900 metres of climbing, the gentlest introduction of a brutal closing block that now sends the peloton deeper into the Alps over the coming two days.

body: Michael Olise has enjoyed a plush start to life in Munich, but by the end of August he will have to find somewhere else to enjoy it. ONE reports the Bayern winger must vacate the rented Grünwald villa he has called home since arriving from Crystal Palace, after landlord Jérôme Boateng decided to sell the property.

The story originated with Bild in Germany and has since been picked up widely: Boateng, the former Bayern and Germany defender, has terminated Olise's lease so he can put the house on the market, giving the France international until the end of August to move out.

The property is a serious slice of Munich real estate. Bild describes ten rooms, a private gym, a home cinema, a wine cellar and a spa area with sauna, jacuzzi and outdoor pool, all in Grünwald, an upscale district roughly ten minutes' drive from Bayern's training complex.

Boateng bought the villa in 2016 for €7.4 million; German media now value it at around €11.5 million, with several offers said to have already landed on his desk. Olise moved in as a tenant in September 2024, shortly after his transfer from Crystal Palace.

The timing has invited speculation given the noise around Olise's future, with his name repeatedly linked to Real Madrid in recent Spanish and German reporting. But outlets covering the villa story, including Sports Illustrated Germany and Goal.com, are explicit that the two threads are unconnected - Boateng, they report, had been trying to sell the house even before Olise moved in, and simply found a buyer now.
For Olise himself, the practical upshot is a very 2026-footballer problem: finding a new home in Munich within a matter of weeks, right as preseason preparations with Bayern get under way.

Since joining from Crystal Palace in 2024, Olise has established himself as one of Bayern's most important attacking players, and the club has shown no public sign of wavering on him despite the transfer chatter - this is, for now, a story about a rental agreement, not a farewell.

title: Carapaz solos to Orcières-Merlette as breakaway storms the Alps
dek: The Ecuadorian's late attack delivers the first breakaway win of this Tour's high mountains, while Pogačar and Evenepoel mark each other into the decisive Alpe d'Huez double.

verificationSources.label: CyclingUpToDate — Stage 18 result report
CyclingUpToDate — Classifications update after stage 18
CyclingStage.com — Points classification, stage 18
Vavel — Stage 18 live result
The National — Carapaz wins as McNulty abandons

body: The Tour de France finally let the road break loose in the Alps. On stage 18, a brutal 185.2km haul from Voiron to the ski station of Orcières-Merlette, Richard Carapaz rode away from five breakaway companions in the final kilometres to win alone, the first rider all race to beat the yellow jersey group to the line in the high mountains.

The move that decided the stage went clear roughly 70km from the finish, a six-man raid containing Carapaz, Valentin Paret-Peintre, Matteo Jorgenson, Tobias Halland Johannessen, Mauro Schmid and Raúl García Pierna. Tadej Pogačar and UAE Team Emirates-XRG chose not to chase, content to let the break build a cushion of several minutes while the peloton dealt with its own business on a day stacked with five categorised climbs, including the long drags of the Côte d'Engins and the Côte de Monteynard before the finishing 7.1km ascent to Orcières-Merlette, which averages 6.7 percent.

It was on that final slope that Carapaz made his move, launching with three kilometres to go in a decisive second surge that nobody in the lead group could match. Paret-Peintre was the first to be shed; Jorgenson and Schmid held on longer but could not close the gap, and Carapaz crossed the line 45 seconds clear of Schmid and Jorgenson, who finished together for second and third. It was the Ecuadorian's first stage win of this year's race and his second at the Tour de France, following his polka-dot campaign and stage victory in 2024.

Behind, the general classification contenders rode to a ceasefire. Pogačar controlled the pace through the early climbs to prevent any dangerous names slipping into the early break, and the main favourites came home together roughly four and a half minutes down, without a single attack among them. The result: no change at the top of the overall standings, a rare day of peace before the race turns properly violent.

Pogačar leads the general classification at 64hr 35min 13sec, with Remco Evenepoel of Red Bull-Bora-hansgrohe still his closest challenger at 4:32. Isaac del Toro of UAE Team Emirates-XRG holds third at 6:51, with Decathlon CMA CGM's teenage revelation Paul Seixas fourth at 7:11 and Juan Ayuso of Lidl-Trek fifth at 9:22. Mattias Skjelmose, Lenny Martínez, Tom Pidcock and Jordan Jegat round out the top nine, and Carapaz's ride vaulted him into tenth overall at 21:00 down.

The points battle for green stayed with Mads Pedersen. The Lidl-Trek rider won the day's only intermediate sprint, at Corps, to push his tally to 477 points and extend his advantage over Jasper Philipsen of Alpecin-Premier Tech, who sits second on 445 after his breakaway sprint win in Voiron a day earlier. Biniam Girmay of NSN Cycling Team is a distant third on 361.

In the mountains competition, Pogačar's grip on the polka-dot jersey looks shakier than at any point this July. He leads with 70 points, but Paret-Peintre's aggression in the day's breakaway pulled him to within a single point on 69, and Carapaz's own points haul from the stage carried him to third on 63 — with two summit finishes at Alpe d'Huez still to come, the jersey is squarely in play.

Del Toro's white jersey as best young rider looks more secure for now: the Mexican's overall placing keeps him well clear of Seixas, who trails him by 20 seconds, with Ayuso a more distant third in the classification at 2:31 back.

UAE Team Emirates-XRG had a difficult day beyond the racing itself. Brandon McNulty, one of Pogačar's key lieutenants for the Alps, abandoned the race during the stage after struggling with what team sources described as a sore throat, becoming the first UAE rider to leave this Tour. His exit thins the ranks around Pogačar just as the race turns to its most decisive terrain, though the Slovenian's buffer over Evenepoel means the loss is unlikely to be fatal.

Attention now swings to back-to-back summit finishes on Alpe d'Huez, the first of the race's two visits to the fabled 21 hairpins arriving on stage 19 and a second the following day. With Pogačar and Evenepoel still level in form and Seixas and del Toro both threatening to disturb the podium places, the Alps have only just begun to bite.

title: Sorting Out the Tiberias Affair: The Three Fronts of Israeli Football's Injections Scandal
dek: ONE reports the saga over banned intravenous infusions at Ironi Tiberias has split into three separate battles: one against the coaching staff and ownership, one against five suspended players, and one that could still produce a formal indictment against the club itself.

verificationSources.label: ONE - source article
Walla Sport - indictment expected against Ironi Tiberias
Ynet - explainer on the Tiberias injections case
Mako/N12 - coach and five players suspended

body: Nearly two months after a rival club's complaint first put Ironi Tiberias under investigation, ONE reports the case has hardened into three distinct, overlapping legal fronts - each with its own defendants, its own timeline, and its own potential punishment for a club playing only its second-ever season in Ligat Ha'al.

It began on the pitch. On May 3, in round 30 of the second-tier "lower playoff," Tiberias beat F.C. Ashdod 3-0 at home, with goals from Sambinia, Batcho and Hadida - a result that lifted the hosts to 10th place on 27 points and dropped Ashdod below the relegation line.

Ashdod did not let the result stand unchallenged. On June 21, the club's legal representatives filed a formal complaint with the Israeli Football Association alleging Tiberias players had received intravenous saline infusions before kickoff in volumes well beyond what anti-doping rules allow - more than 100 millilitres within 12 hours of competition. That threshold exists not because saline itself is a banned substance, but because large infusions can mask traces of substances that are.

Israel's national anti-doping agency moved quickly, provisionally suspending coach Eliran Hudda, technical director Chen Sol and fitness coach Shlomi Vadrero along with five players - David Kaltin, Guy Hadida, Niv Gutlieb, Sambinia and Yonatan Tafer - pending hearings under the WADA-aligned disciplinary code.

The first front now runs against the coaching staff and ownership. ONE reports six individuals face formal charges from the anti-doping agency over organizing and administering the infusions, plus separate allegations tied to evidence-handling and obstruction during the investigation: Hudda, Sol, Vadrero, club owner Miki Bitan, team manager Gabriel Cohen and staff member Aviv Jibli.

The second front concerns the five suspended players. ONE reports settlement negotiations are under way in their cases, though any deal cannot be finalized without sign-off from the World Anti-Doping Agency, whose approval Israeli authorities need before closing out a case of this kind.

The third front runs through the Football Association itself. Its prosecutor has, according to ONE, already prepared a formal indictment against the club - but is holding it back for now, pending the outcome of the players' settlement talks, with the federation reportedly ready to file immediately if those negotiations collapse.

Other Israeli outlets covering the case in recent weeks, including Walla and Sport1, have reported that a serious indictment against the club is expected regardless of how the players' track resolves, though the expectation is that any punishment will stop short of relegation or a points deduction - with Hudda, as head coach, seen as facing the heaviest individual sanction.

Tiberias and its ownership - the club is run by the Doroth Group, headed by businessman Aryeh Kalmanzon - have consistently denied wrongdoing. Kalmanzon has said the substance given to players was simple saline, administered "within legal frameworks" and in permitted volumes to guard against dehydration, and the club has signaled it will not accept a rushed plea agreement, preferring to fight the case through the sport's legal channels if it comes to that.

For a club that reached the top flight for the first time only in 2024, the stakes are considerable. A serious verdict against the organization, layered on top of individual sanctions for its coach and players, would land just as Tiberias tries to establish itself in Ligat Ha'al - with the rest of Israeli football already stirring toward the new 2026/27 season.

The May 3 match, round 30 of the lower playoff, ended 3-0 to Tiberias over F.C. Ashdod (Sambinia, Batcho, Hadida), lifting Tiberias to 10th on 27 points and dropping Ashdod below the relegation line.

Israel's national anti-doping agency provisionally suspended coach Eliran Hudda, technical director Chen Sol, fitness coach Shlomi Vadrero and players David Kaltin, Guy Hadida, Niv Gutlieb, Sambinia and Yonatan Tafer.

title: Kibedy Gordon's Warning to His Rival: "You're Going Down"
dek: Ahead of a historic card that will see all three Gordon brothers fight on the same night in Tel Aviv, Kibedy Gordon predicts he'll stop Mexican veteran Jose Alberto Quiñonez inside two rounds.

verificationSources.label: ONE - original report

body: Kibedy Gordon isn't interested in his opponent's resume. Days before the biggest night of his career, the Jerusalem-born Muay Thai fighter had one message for Jose Alberto Quiñonez, the Mexican veteran with previous UFC experience standing across from him: "It doesn't matter how you prepared, Monday I'm going to knock you down."

Gordon's bout with Quiñonez is part of GFN 1: "Israel vs. the World," a card that will make history before a single punch is thrown. For the first time, all three fighting Gordon brothers — Ahavat Hashem, Ruach Hashem and Kibedy — will compete on the same show, in the same building, on the same evening.

title: Leagues Administration orders clubs to ready stadium shelters ahead of new season
dek: With Ligat Ha'al set to kick off next month, Israel's Football Leagues Administration has told every top-flight club to inspect and prepare protected spaces at their home grounds without delay.

verificationSources.label: ONE - דרישה מהקבוצות להיערכות מיידית באצטדיונים
Ynet - לקראת חזרת הכדורגל: במינהלת הכריזו על מבצע מיגון האצטדיונים

body: Israel's Football Leagues Administration has written to every club in the top professional division, demanding immediate action to make sure protected spaces at their home stadiums are ready for use, ONE reported.

The letter, sent as the 2026/27 season approaches, asks clubs to reconfirm that all safe rooms are empty, clean, organized and fit for instant use "should we need them," reflecting the still-complex security backdrop Israeli sport continues to operate under.

According to ONE, clubs are required to carry out a full inspection of every protected facility at their ground, distinguishing between standard safe rooms and any additional emergency shelters installed at the venue.
Beyond a paperwork check, the Administration wants each club to send a representative to physically walk the stadium with venue management and verify conditions in person before the campaign begins.
The wording, as quoted by ONE, is direct: clubs must confirm the spaces are "empty, clean, organized and ready for use should we need them" - language that leaves little room for delay.

The instruction is not new territory for Israeli football. A similar protocol was put in place after Operation Swords of Iron, when the league built a framework around using protected spaces and limiting personnel present at stadiums during alerts.

That earlier push saw the Leagues Administration, under chairman Erez Kalfon, launch an operation to procure and install mobile reinforced shelters at grounds where standing safe rooms could not hold everyone required to be present, with the Ministry of Culture and Sport helping fund the work, according to prior Ynet reporting.

At the time, authorities were warned that stadiums failing to install adequate protection risked disqualification, forcing their tenant clubs to relocate matches to alternative venues - a consequence the league has made clear it does not want to repeat as fixtures resume.

With the new Ligat Ha'al season on the horizon, the renewed letter functions as a check-in: a reminder that the safety infrastructure built during the war has to stay maintained and match-ready, not something clubs can let lapse once the immediate crisis eases.

title: MLS opens tampering investigation into Inter Miami over Casemiro signing
dek: Days after unveiling the Brazilian midfielder as Lionel Messi's new teammate, David Beckham's club is facing league scrutiny over how it obtained his rights from LA Galaxy.

verificationSources.label: ONE
ESPN
CBS Miami
Sportbible

body: The ink was barely dry on Casemiro's Inter Miami contract before Major League Soccer announced it was investigating the club that signed him.

MLS confirmed this week that it is reviewing a tampering allegation against Inter Miami, the club co-owned and fronted by David Beckham, over the process by which it secured the 34-year-old Brazilian midfielder following his exit from Manchester United.

At issue is MLS's "Discovery" system, a league mechanism designed to stop clubs bidding each other up for unsigned international players by granting one franchise exclusive negotiating rights to a target. According to ESPN and CBS Miami, LA Galaxy — not Inter Miami — originally held those discovery rights to Casemiro.

Inter Miami and Galaxy have since reached a settlement transferring the rights, reportedly worth around £750,000, but MLS has not disclosed whether the tampering concern relates to contact Miami may have had with Casemiro before acquiring those rights, or to the rights transfer itself.

"Major League Soccer is reviewing a tampering allegation against Inter Miami CF," the league said in a statement carried by multiple outlets, adding that it was "gathering all relevant information" and would not comment further until the review concludes.
Both clubs have confirmed an agreement was reached but say the full terms will only be released once the investigation is complete.

Casemiro has signed through the 2027 MLS season with an option to extend to 2029, joining Lionel Messi, Luis Suárez and Sergio Busquets in Miami's high-profile squad. The five-time Champions League winner left Old Trafford as a free agent after five seasons in the Premier League.

It is not the first time Beckham's club has drawn league sanction. In 2021, Inter Miami was fined $2 million by MLS after an investigation found the club had violated salary cap and roster rules connected to the signing of former France international Blaise Matuidi.

No penalty has been imposed over the Casemiro deal at this stage, and MLS has stressed the process is ongoing, but the precedent of the Matuidi case means fines or roster consequences cannot be ruled out if wrongdoing is confirmed.

For now, Casemiro's arrival stands as one of the most eye-catching MLS transfers of the year — even if the circumstances of how Miami cleared him for signing are still being picked apart by the league that will decide whether the deal was done by the book.

title: Arsenal land Tzolis in Belgian-record deal as Garnacho quits Chelsea for Aston Villa after a year
dek: The Gunners have completed a £34m swoop for Club Brugge winger Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard, while Alejandro Garnacho's turbulent 12 months at Chelsea end with a loan move to Aston Villa.

body: Arsenal have wasted little time replacing Leandro Trossard, confirming the signing of Greek international winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in a deal reported at around £34m (roughly €40m) on a contract running to 2031.

The 24-year-old leaves Belgium off the back of an outstanding campaign: 17 goals and 23 assists in 36 Pro League appearances for Brugge last season, numbers that made him one of the division's most sought-after attacking talents and turned his sale into a record for a Belgian top-flight club, according to reporting cited by ONE and confirmed independently by Sky Sports and ESPN.

He arrives at the Emirates as the direct replacement for Trossard, who has gone the other way out of English football entirely. The Belgian winger completed a move to Besiktas in a deal worth £17m (£15.3m plus £1.7m in potential add-ons), ending a three-and-a-half-year Arsenal spell in which he made 174 appearances and contributed 36 goals and 34 assists.

Mikel Arteta's rebuild of his wide options isn't finished there, either — Arsenal are said to still be tracking further attacking reinforcements this summer, underlining how central pace and directness out wide have become to the club's planning.

The same day's other big winger story involves a player who, by contrast, is already moving on from a club he only joined a year ago. Alejandro Garnacho has left Chelsea for Aston Villa on a season-long loan that comes with a conditional obligation to buy, reported by Sky Sports and other British outlets at close to £42.5m if certain appearance-based conditions are met over the 2026/27 campaign.

Those conditions are understood to be relatively modest and considered likely to be triggered, meaning Villa's move is, in practice, expected to become permanent rather than a straightforward year-long loan.

It caps an unusually short and rocky stay in west London for the Argentine international. Garnacho joined Chelsea from Manchester United only last summer for a reported £40m, but managed just eight goals in 43 appearances across all competitions before the club moved to offload him.

Aston Villa now becomes Garnacho's third Premier League club in as many seasons, a striking trajectory for a 21-year-old still seen as one of the most talented wide players to come through Manchester United's academy in the last decade.
For Villa, meanwhile, the swoop brings in direct competition and creative depth out wide as Unai Emery's side continue building for another push toward Europe.

Taken together, the two deals capture the churn of this transfer window at its top end: Arsenal paying a Belgian-league record to bring in a proven goal contributor while moving on a reliable servant, and Chelsea cutting their losses on a marquee signing barely twelve months after making it.

title: Beitar Jerusalem Players Pause for Tisha B'Av Prayer Hours Before Larnaca Test
dek: With kickoff in Cyprus arriving before the Tisha B'Av fast even ends, Beitar's squad gathered for Mincha and a Torah reading abroad - a moment that doubled as a birthday blessing for forward Omer Atzili.

body: Hours before one of the biggest nights of their summer, Beitar Jerusalem's players set football aside for a Torah scroll and an afternoon prayer. According to ONE, the squad gathered for Mincha in Cyprus on Thursday - the fast day of Tisha B'Av - with kickoff against AEK Larnaca only hours away.

The timing was no small thing. Beitar are opening their 2026/27 European campaign with the away leg of a Conference League second qualifying round tie at AEK Larnaca, kicking off at 19:30 local time on Thursday evening. Tisha B'Av, the fast marking the destruction of the two ancient Temples in Jerusalem, ran this year from sunset on Wednesday, July 22, until nightfall around 20:11pm on Thursday - meaning the whistle would go before the fast itself had ended.
That left several Beitar players effectively taking the field for a European qualifier while still fasting, a detail the travel schedule was built around rather than ignored.

Per ONE, Rabbi Raskin, who traveled with the squad, arranged for a Torah scroll to be brought along so the players could hold a proper communal reading and prayer even on the road - a small logistical effort that underlined the group's intent to keep its religious routine intact regardless of the fixture list.
Assistant coach Moshe Ohayon appeared among those pictured at the gathering, based on photographs published alongside the report.

The session carried a second, lighter thread too. Forward Omer Atzili's Hebrew birthday fell on the same day, and Rabbi Ami Faikovsky used the moment to bless him in front of teammates: "I wish you abundant blessings ... may everything you do succeed, and may you continue being a special person with a great heart," he said, according to ONE.
Atzili, who rejoined Beitar last year, is no stranger to Cypriot football himself, having previously played for Omonia Nicosia before returning to Jerusalem.

The wider travel plan reflected the calendar squeeze the club was navigating. The squad flew out to Cyprus on Tuesday evening, then held its final training session and pre-match press conference on Wednesday - both wrapped up before the fast began at sundown - leaving Thursday itself as a day split between religious observance and match preparation.
On the pitch, the assignment is straightforward enough: see off AEK Larnaca over two legs for a place in the next qualifying round, with the second leg set for July 30 at Teddy Stadium in Jerusalem.

For a club whose fan base and self-image lean heavily on tradition, the image of players huddled around a Torah scroll in a Cypriot hotel, fasting on the day of their biggest match so far, was always going to resonate back home - regardless of what happens on the scoreboard on Thursday night.
