title: Israeli football's 'Iron Lady' won't blink in the Kangwa transfer stand-off
dek: Greek media have taken to calling Hapoel Be'er Sheva owner Alona Barkat football's toughest negotiator — and ONE reports she isn't giving up a single euro on Kings Kangwa's price, even with AEK Athens and Panathinaikos both circling.

verificationSources.label: ONE - אשת הברזל בכדורגל הישראלי, לא מוותרת על אירו
Ynet - קאנגווה רוצה לעזוב, ברקת לא תתפשר
Sport5 - אלונה ברקת מחכה להצעה הנכונה
Times of Israel - Israel's first female soccer boss blazes a desert trail

body: Greek football writers have found a nickname for Alona Barkat this month, and it isn't a flattering one for whoever sits across the table from her: the Iron Lady. ONE reports that the owner of Hapoel Be'er Sheva has made herself the central character in the transfer saga around Kings Kangwa, refusing to shift her asking price by what the outlet's headline calls, pointedly, not even a single euro.

The pun works in Hebrew as it does in English: Barkat, according to the report, won't give up a euro — the currency her Greek suitors are negotiating in, and the continental competition her club is chasing a place in at the same time. Kangwa, Beer Sheva's Zambian midfielder, has been the subject of interest from both AEK Athens and, more recently, Panathinaikos, and ONE's framing is that Barkat holds the leverage in both conversations because she is simply refusing to blink.

The player himself is coming off the best season of his career. Kangwa was voted the Israeli Premier League's Player of the Season for 2025/26, contributing 12 goals and nine assists as Beer Sheva won the title — the club's first championship in eight years. He is under contract until June 2028, which hands Barkat a strong hand regardless of who is asking.

That leverage has been tested repeatedly this month. Reports in Israel and Greece have described AEK's offers climbing over successive rounds, from an opening bid in the region of €2.5 million toward figures closer to €4 million, with Beer Sheva said to be holding firm near €3.5–4 million before those talks stalled — clearing the way, per ONE, for Panathinaikos to make their own move.

Greek outlets covering the negotiations have not minced words about what it is like to deal with her. "You wouldn't want her sitting across from you in negotiations," ONE quotes the Greek press as writing, describing a businesswoman who will not back down until her position is accepted. It isn't the first time European media has reached for a political comparison — German outlets have previously dubbed her the "Angela Merkel of football" for the same stubborn, unsentimental style.

Barkat's reputation was not built overnight. She bought Hapoel Be'er Sheva in 2007, reportedly for around $1.8 million, becoming the first woman to own a top-flight football club in Israel — a milestone Israeli and international outlets, including the Times of Israel, have documented in profiles of her since. Before football, she and her husband Eli Barkat spent years in Silicon Valley, where the Barkat family was among the early investors behind Check Point and built venture funds of their own.

The turnaround at Beer Sheva has been real, even if the road there wasn't smooth: ONE credits her ownership with four league championships and four domestic cups, achieved across roughly 15 different head coaches — a managerial churn rate that says as much about her demanding standards as any negotiating table ever could.

Her hard line over Kangwa's price also has a specific precedent behind it. Israeli reporting on the saga has pointed back to the sale of winger Tony Wakama for around €800,000 in a previous window — a deal the club came to regret after an early European exit that, in hindsight, a fully strengthened squad might have avoided. That memory is said to be shaping her refusal to sell Kangwa cheaply now, with Beer Sheva also mindful of needing him fit and eligible through their own Champions League qualifying campaign.

As of Thursday, no transfer has been completed on either side of the Athens rivalry. AEK's interest appears to have cooled amid the price gap, and Panathinaikos's move is still, by ONE's own account, at an early stage. For now, the story Greek football is telling itself is a simple one: Alona Barkat has a price, and nobody has met it yet.

title: "If we need to stop the league, we'll stop it": IPFL chief on war footing ahead of new season
dek: Acting league boss Nir Yankelevich says Israeli football is once again preparing contingency plans for a wartime suspension, months after the season was already halted for five weeks during the Iran conflict.

verificationSources.label: ONE - source article
Israel Pro Football Leagues - official English site
Haaretz - league suspension coverage during Iran war

body: As Israeli football edges toward the start of a new season, the man running the country's professional leagues is again talking contingency plans rather than fixtures.

Nir Yankelevich, acting CEO of the Israel Pro Football Leagues management (known in Hebrew as Minhelet HaLigot), told ONE in an interview published this week that the league is bracing for the possibility of another wartime halt. "We've again reached a situation of war - that's beyond football," he said, before adding the line that gives the moment its edge: "We're ready for everything. If we need to stop the league, we'll stop it."

It is not an abstract threat. Ligat Ha'al was already suspended for roughly five weeks this year, from February 28 until April 4, after Israel and Iran traded fire in what officials called Operation Lion's Roar, forcing matches off across the top flight and the National League alike.

Yankelevich indicated the league's approach hasn't changed since then: if the security picture shifts again, organizers will first pause and reassess before deciding whether games can go ahead. "Whenever an attack begins, the first thing that happens is the situation gets put on hold," he said, adding that the Home Front Command's guidance to clubs so far tracks with what the public already knows.

The comments come as the league management works through the routine logistics of preparing grounds for the 2026/27 campaign - including checking that shelter and safe-room facilities are in order at venues such as Sakhnin and Ramat Hasharon.

Yankelevich used the same conversation to address a more mundane but pointed complaint: substandard water and refreshments sold at some stadium kiosks. "That's not acceptable - it doesn't matter which ground you go to," he said, signaling the league intends to push clubs on the issue.

With the new season opening in the height of summer, he also touched on hydration protocols for players during matches. Referees, he said, will apply criteria set by the league's medical department on when to call mandatory drinks breaks in extreme heat, framing it plainly: "Player health comes above everything."

The remarks also touched on an ongoing legal dispute tied to Tiberias's stadium situation, part of the broader list of administrative issues the league management is untangling before the campaign gets under way.

Israel's 2026/27 football calendar is already in motion. The Toto Champions Cup opener between the reigning league champion and cup holder kicked off the season on July 12, with the wider Toto Cup group stage beginning the weekend of July 25 - five days ahead of the National League's equivalent. The Ligat Ha'al regular season itself is slated to start on August 22, with the National League beginning its midweek rounds a few days earlier, on August 18-19.

For now, Yankelevich's message is less about fixtures than about posture: the league wants clubs, players and fans to know that if the security situation deteriorates again, the same playbook used earlier this year - pause first, reassess, then decide - is ready to be used once more.

Ligat Ha'al was already suspended for about five weeks this year, from February 28 to April 4, amid the Israel-Iran conflict (Operation Lion's Roar).

body: Panathinaikos have turned their attention to Kings Kangwa, Hapoel Beer Sheva's Zambian midfielder and the reigning Israeli Premier League Player of the Season, according to a report from ONE.

The Greek club's interest surfaces just after Hapoel Beer Sheva's negotiations with AEK Athens over Kangwa broke down. The Israeli champions had been in talks with AEK for weeks, but ONE reports those discussions have now collapsed, opening the door for a rival Athens club to step in.

Greek outlets have independently picked up the same story. Gazzetta.gr described Panathinaikos as showing "warm interest" in Kangwa, while Onsports.gr and SKAI reported the club is weighing him as an alternative in central midfield after a more high-profile pursuit fell short.

That pursuit was of Brentford's Mathias Jensen. The Danish international had been Panathinaikos's primary target for the deep-lying midfield role, but the move has stalled — reports in England describe hesitation on Jensen's side and Brentford raising their asking price toward €10 million after triggering a one-year extension on his contract.

With Jensen increasingly out of reach, Panathinaikos have shifted their focus to cheaper alternatives, and Kangwa's profile fits. His market value is estimated around €3.8 million, and, according to the Greek reports, his salary demands are modest — a financially comfortable fit for a club not looking to break the bank this window.

Kangwa, 27, arrives into this speculation on the back of a landmark season. He was named the Israeli Premier League's Player of the Season for 2025/26, taking 54 percent of the vote, after contributing 12 goals and nine assists as Hapoel Beer Sheva won the title — the club's sixth championship and first in eight years. He scored and set up a goal in the decisive 4-2 win over Maccabi Tel Aviv that sealed it.
He remains under contract at Hapoel Beer Sheva until 2028, giving the Israeli club leverage in any negotiation even without AEK's involvement.

The interest emerges at a pointed moment for both clubs' European campaigns. Hapoel Beer Sheva lost the first leg of their Champions League second qualifying round tie 2-1 away to Vikingur Reykjavik on Tuesday, with Kangwa scoring the visitors' goal.

Panathinaikos, meanwhile, are focused on their own qualifying assignment, hosting — or travelling to — Hungarian side Paksi in the Conference League's second qualifying round, with the first leg played this week after the Greek club dropped into that competition following Champions League qualifying elimination earlier in the season.

According to ONE, sources close to both the player and Hapoel Beer Sheva have confirmed Panathinaikos's interest is genuine, with further developments expected within days. No formal offer has been reported yet, and the story remains at the reconnaissance stage rather than an active negotiation.

title: Red convoy: thousands of Hapoel Tel Aviv fans escorted to Hungary for Europe return
dek: Around 30 buses of supporters, backed by a police escort, made the journey to Miskolc for Hapoel's first European match in 12 years, against Bulgaria's Ludogorets.

body: Thousands of Hapoel Tel Aviv supporters set off in an organised convoy on Thursday, heading not to Bloomfield but to a Hungarian provincial city, for a fixture the club has waited 12 years to play again: a European away — or rather, a European "home" — match.

ONE reports the fans travelled in roughly 30 buses, escorted by seven police vehicles on the approximately two-and-a-half-hour drive out from Budapest, in what the outlet described as a major logistical operation to get the red faithful to the stadium in time for kickoff.

The occasion is Hapoel Tel Aviv's first leg against Bulgaria's Ludogorets Razgrad in the second qualifying round of the Conference League, kicking off Thursday evening at 21:30 local time at the DVTK Stadion in Miskolc.

Hapoel are staging their home European fixtures this season at the Diósgyőri Stadion in Miskolc rather than in Israel, part of the arrangement clubs have adopted for continental competition amid the ongoing security situation. It means home advantage now comes with a road trip for the club's own fans.

Israeli outlets including Sport1-Maariv and Israel Hayom reported in the buildup that demand for tickets was intense, with more than 5,000 supporters having committed to making the trip — a striking number for a match played roughly 2,500 kilometres from Tel Aviv.
The return leg is set for July 30 at Ludogorets' own Huvepharma Arena in Razgrad, where Hapoel will look to complete the tie and advance further into Europe for the first time in over a decade.

For a club whose last European campaign dates back 12 years, the sight of a police-escorted fan convoy rolling into a Hungarian stadium car park was itself part of the story — a reminder of how much the return to continental football means to Hapoel's supporters, wherever the club is forced to call home.

title: Rodri set for back surgery as Man City face season without their Golden Ball winner
dek: Weeks after captaining Spain to World Cup glory and collecting the tournament's top individual prize, Rodri is heading for surgery on a back problem with no return date in sight, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Yahoo Sports
Goal.com

body: It is barely a month since Rodri stood on a podium in North America clutching the Golden Ball as the best player of the 2026 World Cup. Now, ONE reports, Manchester City's Spanish anchor is heading into surgery on a back problem with no target date to return.

The Israeli outlet cites English media reporting that City have opted for an operation rather than conservative treatment, with the club yet to issue any official medical bulletin of its own. The lack of a public timeline, ONE notes, points to a recovery being planned around the player's long-term health rather than a rush back for the start of the season.

It is a cruelly familiar pattern for the 30-year-old. Rodri ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in September 2024, a injury that wiped out almost his entire 2024-25 campaign and denied him the chance to defend his Ballon d'Or. When he did return, hamstring and groin problems kept interrupting his rhythm, limiting him to 33 appearances in all competitions last season.

None of that was visible in Spain's colours this summer. Rodri started all eight of his country's matches at the World Cup as La Roja lifted the trophy for the first time since 2010, and he left the tournament, by all accounts, in excellent physical shape. The timing of a new setback so soon afterwards will sting all the more for that.

The blow lands at an already delicate moment for Manchester City. Pep Guardiola stepped down as manager in the summer, with former assistant Enzo Maresca returning to the Etihad Stadium to take charge of the club's first season in the post-Guardiola era. Losing his defensive midfield lynchpin for an unknown stretch is not the start Maresca would have chosen.

City are due to open their Premier League campaign at home to Bournemouth on August 23, and question marks now hang over whether Rodri will be fit to feature in the opening weeks, or well beyond them.

Then there is the contract question that refuses to go away. Rodri's current deal at City runs only to the summer of 2027, and talks over an extension — expected to resume once the World Cup was out of the way — have shown no sign of progress.

Real Madrid speculation has trailed him for months, with some Spanish reports suggesting he would welcome a return home, even as outlets in England have played down any concrete interest from the Bernabéu this window. A move did not materialise this summer, but with his contract now entering its final two years, the uncertainty over Rodri's long-term future at City is unlikely to fade — surgery or no surgery.

For now, the more immediate concern for Maresca is simpler: finding a way to cover the loss of the player who, more than perhaps anyone else at the club, has defined City's midfield control since Guardiola made him the pivot of his system.

Manchester City are entering a new era under Enzo Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager after Guardiola stepped down in summer 2026.

Rodri's Manchester City contract runs to June 2027 and no extension has been agreed; he has been repeatedly linked with a return to Spain via Real Madrid, though no move materialised in the 2026 summer window.

title: Beitar spokesman: police told UEFA nothing unusual happened in Larnaca
dek: Asaf Nahum pushes back on a Larnaca hotel's claims of graffiti and disorder by Beitar fans, saying police briefed a UEFA delegate that no incidents occurred, hours before Thursday's Conference League qualifier against AEK Larnaca.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Mako
Sport1 (Maariv)
UEFA.com match page

body: Hours before Beitar Jerusalem's Conference League qualifier in Cyprus, the club found itself fending off accusations that had nothing to do with tactics or team news.

A Larnaca hotel housing Beitar supporters sent a letter to its Israeli guests complaining of graffiti on the property, noise disturbances and a "sharp smell of grass smoking," according to Mako. The letter, sent to fans upon or shortly after arrival, demanded better conduct for the remainder of their stay.
Beitar spokesman Asaf Nahum rejected the substance of the complaints. "We checked and nothing happened," he said, adding that whatever the hotel described did not recur once the letter went out.

Nahum went further, saying the matter had also come up in the routine security meeting between local police and UEFA ahead of the match: the police representative told the UEFA delegate there had been "no unusual events."

At least one supporter pushed back on the hotel's account directly. Fan Shlomi Dehry told Mako it "looks like the letter was prepared in advance," saying he had heard of no such incidents since arriving.

Cypriot media reports had also alleged disturbances by Beitar fans in Larnaca's streets. The club denied any rioting, telling reporters that tear gas seen in footage from the area was used against local AEK Larnaca supporters who tried to confront the visiting fans, not against Beitar's own support.

With the club unable to secure any additional match tickets, Nahum was blunt about fans who traveled without one: "Without a ticket, they will not enter." Supporters have been told they must present both a passport and a valid ticket to get into the stadium, and those without tickets have been discouraged from making the trip to the gates at all.

The friction comes as Beitar Jerusalem prepare for the second qualifying round first leg away to AEK Larnaca at the AEK Arena – Georgios Karapatakis, kicking off Thursday at 19:30 Israel time — which this year falls during the Tisha B'Av fast, adding an extra logistical wrinkle for travelling fans and staff.

Beitar's hardline support base, including the La Familia group, has drawn UEFA and disciplinary scrutiny on previous European trips, which is part of why any hint of trouble abroad tends to escalate quickly into a story of its own — even when, as the club insists here, the underlying claims don't hold up.

title: Karim Adeyemi completes move to Barcelona from Borussia Dortmund
dek: The German winger has signed a five-year deal at Camp Nou in a transfer reported at around €22 million plus €7 million in variables, becoming Hansi Flick's second forward addition of the summer.

verificationSources.label: ONE

body: Karim Adeyemi is officially a Barcelona player. The German winger has completed his move from Borussia Dortmund, ONE reports, ending three years at the Westfalenstadion to join Hansi Flick's rebuilt attacking line at Camp Nou.

The fee, as reported by ONE and matched by outlets across Europe, sits at roughly €22 million with a further €7 million in performance-based add-ons — a deal Barcelona and Dortmund are understood to have quietly agreed more than a week before the announcement.

Adeyemi has put pen to a five-year contract that runs until the summer of 2031. Dortmund, for their part, negotiated a 35 percent sell-on clause on any future sale, a standard piece of business protection given how much they still believe in the 24-year-old's ceiling.
He is expected to earn in the region of €6 million a season net in Catalonia, and he arrives as the second forward Flick has brought in this summer, following the signing of Anthony Gordon.

At 24, Adeyemi is best known for his raw speed — regularly cited as among the very fastest players in world football — and his aggressive, high-intensity pressing, qualities that made him a fixture in Dortmund's attack across three Bundesliga and Champions League campaigns. Last season he produced 10 goals and 6 assists in all competitions.

His path to the top ran through Bayern Munich and Unterhaching's academies before Red Bull Salzburg gave him his platform in Austria. There he won league titles and, in the 2021-22 season, finished as the Austrian Bundesliga's top scorer with 19 goals in 29 appearances, adding four more in the Champions League.
Dortmund moved for him in the summer of 2022, and he grew into one of the club's key attacking outlets, valued for his ability to play across the front line and on either wing.

The connection to his new coach goes back further than this transfer. It was Flick, then Germany's manager, who handed Adeyemi his senior international debut in September 2021 — while he was still a teenager at Salzburg — in a 6-0 win over Armenia in which the youngster scored. Flick had already tracked him closely, having faced him in Champions League ties as Bayern's coach.

Barcelona believe that history, and Adeyemi's tactical range, will translate smoothly into Flick's system, which leans heavily on high pressing, rapid transitions and constant positional rotation in the final third.

The winger also has recent international pedigree of his own, having scored for Germany in their 5-1 opening win over Scotland at Euro 2024 — evidence, Barcelona's recruitment staff will hope, that he can deliver on the biggest stages as he begins his new chapter in Spain.

title: Driks warns Maccabi Tel Aviv: win tonight isn't enough, Sheriff are no pushover
dek: Club legend Eli Driks tells ONE that Maccabi Tel Aviv must both beat Sheriff Tiraspol and go on to reach the league phase proper, cautioning against writing off a Moldovan side with real Champions League pedigree.

verificationSources.label: ONE (one.co.il) original report

body: As Maccabi Tel Aviv prepared to kick off their European season on Thursday evening in Tiraspol, one of the club's own former heroes was on hand to sound a note of caution rather than triumphalism. Eli Driks, the record-scoring forward who became a Maccabi institution both on the pitch and later as the club's long-serving chief executive, told ONE's "Today's Conversation" programme that beating Sheriff Tiraspol tonight would only be half the job.

"I wouldn't underestimate Sheriff, a team that has played in the Champions League," Driks said, according to ONE, framing the Moldovan champions as a side whose European pedigree makes them a genuine threat despite Maccabi's status as strong favorites on paper.

The message from Driks was pointed: Maccabi need to win the tie itself, but the bigger prize is qualifying deep enough to reach the league phase of a European competition again — continuing a run the club has come to expect and depend on financially and competitively.

Kickoff for the first leg was set for 20:00 at Sheriff's own stadium complex in Tiraspol, the club's regular home for continental nights for two decades. It is the second qualifying round of the Europa League, and it will be the first-ever competitive meeting between the two clubs.

Driks singled out captain Dor Peretz as the player who can decide the tie. "Dor Peretz is the leader, and when he brings his abilities, he drags the team along with him," he told ONE, underlining how central Peretz — who recently returned to the squad after exploring a possible move to Croatia — remains to Kenny Miller's plans.

Asked about the stakes, Driks did not equivocate: reaching the group phase again is "very important" for the club, both in prestige and in the finances that flow from another season in Europe. He said he hopes Maccabi can come away from Moldova with some cushion — "even just 1 or 2" goals — to make the return leg in Georgia more manageable.

That return leg is scheduled for Thursday, July 30, in Batumi, Georgia, rather than at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv, continuing the pattern of Maccabi staging its home European fixtures away from Israel this season.

Sheriff arrive in the tie as Moldova's dominant force of the modern era, with 21 league titles, every one of them won since the turn of the century. They advanced from the first qualifying round by eliminating Slovenia's Aluminij, drawing goalless away before winning 1-0 at home.

Miller's Maccabi, for their part, go into the tie on the back of a productive close season domestically. Unable to retain the league title — finishing third in both the regular season and the championship playoff group — they still ended 2025/26 with silverware, lifting the Israeli State Cup for the first time in five years, before beating Hapoel Be'er Sheva 3-1 in the Super Cup, with 20-year-old forward Sayed Abu Farchi scoring twice.

Driks, drawing on his own decades in and around the club, also touched on the practical realities of playing continental football away from home this season — including the financial cost of repeated away trips and the club's use of charter flights, a contrast, he noted, with the commercial travel of his own playing days.

For Maccabi, the framing Driks offered captures the tension of the tie precisely: favorites against a limited but battle-tested opponent, with a result tonight that will only be judged in full once the return leg in Batumi is played out a week later.

title: Kornfein: Beitar face a tough Larnaca test — and a fast to survive first
dek: Former Beitar Jerusalem goalkeeper and ex-chairman Itzik Kornfein tells ONE that Thursday's Conference League opener in Cyprus is complicated by Tisha B'Av, and predicts a 1-1 draw in the first leg.

verificationSources.label: ONE (one.co.il) original report

body: Itzik Kornfein has seen enough European away trips from inside a Beitar Jerusalem dressing room to know when the fixture list has been unkind. Thursday's Conference League opener in Cyprus, he told ONE, is one of those nights — a dangerous opponent arriving on the same day Beitar's players are due to break a 25-hour fast.
"Larnaca is a very good opponent," the former Beitar goalkeeper and ex-club chairman said. "Beitar arrives after training, but the fasting issue will make it difficult."

Beitar travel to AEK Arena in Larnaca for a 19:30 Israel-time kickoff in the first leg of the UEFA Conference League's second qualifying round — the club's opening assignment of Almog Cohen's first season as head coach.

The date is no coincidence for Kornfein's concern. Tisha B'Av, the fast marking the destruction of the First and Second Temples, runs from sundown on July 22 to nightfall on July 23 this year — meaning several Beitar players could, in theory, still be fasting as the match kicks off.

"I don't think it's easy to overcome a 24-hour fast with dates or bananas," Kornfein said, doubting that a quick post-fast snack does much to restore players to full physical readiness against a side he rates highly.

He was more sanguine about how Cohen would actually handle the situation on the touchline, suggesting the coach would only turn to fasting players if truly forced to. Kornfein pointed to squad regulars such as Omer Atzili, Boris Enow and Luka Gadrani as the kind of contributors Beitar will lean on regardless of who observes the fast.

Looking past Thursday's logistics, Kornfein set a measured bar for the tie itself: "I think if Beitar restores last season's ability, we'll be satisfied." His forecast for the first leg was a 1-1 draw.

Cohen took the Beitar bench this summer after stepping down from his previous post as the club's sporting director, inheriting a squad that reached the third qualifying round of last season's Conference League before being eliminated.

AEK Larnaca finished as Cypriot runners-up last season and enter their own new era under Mauro Camoranesi, the former Juventus and Italy World Cup winner appointed to lead them into this year's European qualifiers.

The return leg is set for July 30 — nominally Beitar's home fixture, but staged at Stadionul Ilie Oană in Ploiești, Romania, the venue the club has been assigned for European home matches this season because of the security situation in Israel.

body: Beitar Jerusalem's European trip to Cyprus took an awkward turn hours before kickoff on Thursday, after the hotel housing the club's traveling delegation and fans issued a written complaint over supporters' behavior, according to ONE.

The Radisson Blu in Larnaca circulated a letter to guests citing three specific grievances tied to the visiting Beitar contingent: graffiti and physical damage near the hotel entrance, noise disturbances in the corridors overnight, and a strong smell of cannabis smoke in parts of the building.
"Like we respect them, we expect them to behave respectfully," a hotel staff member told ONE, confirming that graffiti had been sprayed and damage caused at the entrance to the property.

The friction comes as Beitar prepare for the first leg of their UEFA Conference League second qualifying round tie against AEK Larnaca, kicking off at 19:30 local time. Roughly 500 tickets were allocated to Beitar's traveling support, with dozens more supporters said to have made the trip without pre-purchased tickets.

Head coach Almog Cohen, in his first campaign in charge after moving up from the club's sporting director role, was finalizing his starting lineup on matchday, with the club also having to factor in Tisha B'Av, the Jewish fast day falling on the same date, when assessing players' physical readiness.

The tie is a significant early test for Cohen, who succeeded Barak Itzhaki after Beitar finished as runners-up in the Israeli Premier League last season. The club's Conference League run a year ago ended at the third qualifying round stage, and this season's campaign begins a round earlier against Cypriot opposition.

AEK Larnaca themselves finished second in Cyprus last season and enter the tie under new head coach Mauro Camoranesi, the former Juventus and Italy World Cup winner who was appointed to lead the club into this year's European qualifiers.
The return leg is scheduled for July 30, with AEK Larnaca set to host the second leg away from Larnaca, in Ploiesti, Romania, under the competition's stadium arrangements.

Beitar's traveling fans have a documented recent history of run-ins abroad, including scenes at last season's Conference League trip to Riga, and the club will be keen for Thursday's hotel dispute not to overshadow its return to a two-legged European qualifier it has targeted as an opportunity to advance further than in past campaigns.

title: Hapoel Hadera Wins Court Injunction in Liga Alef Placement Fight
dek: A Tel Aviv District Court judge has frozen Hapoel Hadera's disputed assignment to Liga Alef's southern district, ONE reports, pushing a placement fight the club already lost inside football's own courts into the civil system just before the season starts.

verificationSources.label: ONE — placement drama escalates to civil court
ONE — supreme sports court rejects Hadera's appeal

body: Hapoel Hadera's fight over where it will play its home games next season has stopped being purely a football matter. According to ONE, a Tel Aviv District Court judge has granted the newly relegated club a temporary injunction freezing any "irreversible" step on its Liga Alef district assignment — dragging a dispute that had already run its course inside the game's own courts into the civil system, with the new season fast approaching.

The root of it is simple and, for Hadera, maddening. Relegated from Ligat Ha'Al this summer, the club was placed by the Israel Football Association's league committee into Liga Alef's southern district — despite being based in the north of the country, with all the travel that mismatch implies for a full season of league football.

Hadera's target is M.S. Tira (Moadon Sport Tira), the club it argues should be the one to make way. Tira sits in the northern group and, in air-distance terms, is barely down the road from Hadera itself. The club's case, in essence, is that geography and common sense point one way while the league's paperwork points the other.

The comparison that stings most is Hapoel Nof HaGalil, relegated from the top flight in the very same cycle as Hadera but assigned to the northern district without controversy — leaving Hadera to argue it has been treated inconsistently against a club in an identical position.

Hadera took that argument through the association's internal channels first, and lost. Per ONE's earlier reporting, the supreme sports court unanimously rejected the club's appeal, ruling that the air distance between Hadera and Tira — just 22.67 kilometres — was not significant enough to justify a swap, and that Tira's decade of standing tenure in the northern group gave it seniority Hadera, as a newly relegated side, does not have.

The panel also warned of what it called a "problematic domino effect": moving Tira south to accommodate Hadera, the judges found, would likely force other southern-group clubs to be reshuffled in turn, unpicking a placement structure the association was not willing to reopen.

Hadera did not accept that as the final word. ONE reports the club, represented by attorney Roei Rozen, has now taken the case to Tel Aviv District Court, alleging the arbitration process itself was flawed — that it was denied the right to respond to additional geographic data submitted during the hearing, that documents from Tira and its municipality were withheld, and that the criteria for placement were applied inconsistently between clubs.

Judge Gilad Hess has granted a temporary restraining order barring any irreversible action on the league placement, match schedule or district assignment, according to ONE, effectively putting the entire Liga Alef structure for that region on hold until the matter is properly heard.

A hearing on the substance of Hadera's petition is set for July 30, 2026, at Tel Aviv District Court — meaning a civil judge, rather than football's own arbitrators, may now have the final say on where the club spends its season.

Nothing has actually changed yet: the injunction freezes the status quo rather than overturning it, and Tira's camp had been openly relieved the football association's ruling came down before the season's start. But with a civil court now willing to intervene days before fixtures are meant to be finalised, Liga Alef's southern and northern groups both remain, for now, unsettled business.

Hapoel Nof HaGalil, relegated from the top flight alongside Hadera in the same cycle, was assigned to the northern district without dispute.

A hearing on the merits of Hadera's petition, filed via attorney Roei Rozen, is scheduled for July 30, 2026, at Tel Aviv District Court.

title: Manor Solomon named in Tottenham's touring squad for Australia and New Zealand
dek: The Israeli winger, largely frozen out since 2023, joins Spurs' 35-man party for matches against Auckland FC, Sydney FC and Chelsea — a rare chance to make his case, ONE reports.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Spurs Web — pre-season tour squad
Spurs Web — Solomon's future under De Zerbi
Tottenham Hotspur — Pre-Season Tour 2026

body: Manor Solomon has been named in Tottenham Hotspur's 35-man squad for their pre-season tour of Australia and New Zealand, ONE reports — a small but notable vote of inclusion for an Israeli winger who has barely featured for the club in more than two years.

Roberto De Zerbi's group flies south for three matches: away to Auckland FC in New Zealand on July 26, against A-League side Sydney FC on July 29, and against Chelsea on August 1 in the Sydney Super Cup — the first time Spurs have played their London rivals outside Britain.

ONE frames Solomon's presence as more than a formality. With several key players missing the trip, the outlet reports, the winger stands to get real minutes across the three games — an opportunity to remind the coaching staff what he offers before the Premier League season resumes.

Four players who reached the World Cup semi-finals with their countries — Pedro Porro, Cristian Romero, Marcos Senesi and Djed Spence — were left out of the touring party, while Pape Sarr and Rodrigo Bentancur were given extended leave after their own World Cup commitments. Mohamed Kudus, Xavi Simons, Dejan Kulusevski, Wilson Odobert and goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario all stayed in England for injury treatment.

That still leaves a squad heavy with senior names — James Maddison, Richarlison, Dominic Solanke and Sandro Tonali are all part of the touring party, alongside new arrivals Andy Robertson and Jan Paul van Hecke — but the gaps in wide areas are exactly the kind of opening Solomon needs.

The 26-year-old has not played a competitive minute for Tottenham since 2023, spending the interim on loan at Fiorentina. His route back into contention is complicated by his relationship with the current head coach.

De Zerbi managed Solomon at Shakhtar Donetsk before either arrived in England, and Spurs Web has reported this month that he has effectively told the winger he is free to find a new club. Fiorentina, who held an unused purchase option on Solomon from his loan spell, are said to be interested again but want Tottenham to lower their asking price.
Solomon has spoken carefully about where things stand with his old coach. "I also know he really appreciates me, but the situation at Tottenham is different," he said, according to the same report.

None of that changes the immediate picture. For now Solomon remains a Tottenham player, and the trip Down Under — three matches, a rebuilt attack missing several regulars, and a historic first fixture against Chelsea outside the UK — gives him a genuine window to make his case, on the pitch, whichever direction his Spurs career ultimately takes.

title: Maccabi Tel Aviv face Sheriff Tiraspol in a tie that could shape their whole European season
dek: Kenny Miller's side travel to Tiraspol for a Europa League second qualifying round first leg that either keeps the group-stage dream alive or drops them into a tough Conference League fallback.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Walla Sport
Sport1 Maariv - likely lineup
Sport5 - Belić fitness
Maccabi Tel Aviv FC official site

body: Maccabi Tel Aviv open their European campaign proper on Thursday night, away to Sheriff Tiraspol in the second qualifying round of the Europa League, and Kenny Miller's players already understand the scale of what is at stake: get past the Moldovan champions and a route toward the group stage stays open, lose and the fallback is a far harder road through the Conference League.

Kickoff for the first leg is 20:00 Israel time at Sheriff's own stadium complex in Tiraspol, in Moldova's breakaway Transnistria region, where the club have played their European nights for two decades. The return leg follows a week later, on Thursday, July 30, in Batumi, Georgia — the venue Maccabi have been using for home continental fixtures.

It will be a first-ever competitive meeting between the two clubs, according to reporting around the draw. Maccabi were relieved to avoid tougher potential opponents such as Dynamo Kyiv or Hajduk Split when the pairing was confirmed, but ONE's assessment of Sheriff is unambiguous: this is a side that will be very hard to break down.

Sheriff have won Moldova's league 21 times, every one of those titles since the turn of the century, though they slipped to runners-up last season as their long grip on the domestic game loosened. They reached this round by eliminating Slovenia's Aluminij, drawing away in Moldova before winning 1-0 in Slovenia — clean sheets in both legs, largely playing out of defensively compact 5-4-1 and 5-3-2 shapes, per ONE's scouting of the Moldovan side.

Maccabi arrive on the back of silverware of their own. On July 16 they beat Hapoel Be'er Sheva 3-1 to lift the Israeli Super Cup, a follow-up to a 2025/26 league campaign in which they finished third in both the regular season and the championship playoffs but still ended the year with a trophy — their first State Cup in five years. A 3-1 preseason friendly win only added to the sense of early-season momentum, though Miller's staff are wary of reading too much into results before competitive football starts.

ONE reports the manager is expected to stick with largely the same personnel and shape that started that Super Cup win, set up in a 4-2-3-1. Serbian midfielder Kristijan Belić — known in Hebrew coverage as "Blitz," who joined on loan from AZ Alkmaar last year before Maccabi exercised their option to sign him permanently through 2029 — has completed a full training session and is available for selection.

Defender Tyrese Asante, who missed time with illness, has been back in light training and is expected to be fit enough for Thursday. His inclusion matters beyond just squad depth: Italian side Monza have opened contact over a possible transfer, with Israeli outlets reporting Maccabi would be looking for a fee in the region of €3-4 million for a player they signed from ADO Den Haag two years ago for around €600,000.

Further forward, the group Miller has been building around includes Issouf Sissoko and Itamar Noy screening in midfield, with Sagiv Yehezkel and Ido Shahar providing width, Dor Peretz operating in the number 10 role and Sayed Abu Farha leading the line — the same core that has featured through preseason, according to Sport1's reporting on the club's likely XI for Tiraspol.

The consequences of Thursday's result stretch well beyond the tie itself. ONE reports that a Maccabi exit would mean dropping into a Conference League qualifying draw against Switzerland's St. Gallen — described as a notably difficult assignment. Progress, on the other hand, guarantees Maccabi at least a place in the Conference League play-off round, while a Europa League third qualifying round berth would bring a possible meeting with Qarabağ or CSKA Sofia.
For a club still adjusting to life without a title at home, a strong week in Moldova and Georgia would go a long way toward defining what kind of European season this becomes.

title: Beitar Jerusalem denies fans caused damage in Larnaca ahead of AEK clash
dek: Hours before their Conference League qualifier, the club rejected reports of overnight hooliganism in Cyprus, insisting tear gas near their hotel was fired only at AEK Larnaca supporters who started the trouble.

verificationSources.label: ONE — original report

body: Beitar Jerusalem spent Thursday morning fighting a battle that had nothing to do with football — pushing back hard against reports that its travelling fans had left a trail of trouble through the streets of Larnaca overnight, just hours before the club's Conference League qualifier against AEK Larnaca.

Cypriot and Israeli media had reported violent clashes involving Beitar supporters in the city overnight, with some outlets alleging damage caused by fans staying at the Radisson Blu hotel, according to ONE. Those reports said hotel management had documented graffiti on walls, late-night disturbances and marijuana use in and around rooms used by the travelling group.

Beitar's response, relayed by ONE, was blunt: "Our fans caused no damage to the city's streets." The club said any tear gas deployed near the team's hotel had been used exclusively against AEK Larnaca supporters who instigated the confrontation — not against its own fans, as some of the reporting had implied.

The club said it had launched its own inquiry into the night's events in coordination with the Larnaca police commander, though it did not disclose a timeline for that investigation or detail specific findings beyond its denial of property damage.

Beitar also turned its fire on the Israeli press, accusing outlets of publishing accounts of the night's events before verifying the facts. The club urged more caution in future coverage and appealed to Israeli media to back the country's clubs during what it called a sensitive period for the team's travelling support in Europe.

It would not be the first time Beitar's away following has drawn scrutiny on the continent. The club's fans set off pyrotechnics during a Conference League qualifier away to Latvia's RFS in Riga last August, an episode that made international headlines at the time.

The controversy landed on the same day Beitar were due to kick off their 2026-27 European campaign at AEK Larnaca in the Conference League's second qualifying round, a tie the club has been building toward for weeks amid separate frustration among supporters over the cost and scarcity of away tickets for the trip to Cyprus.

For now, the dispute over what actually happened in Larnaca overnight rests on dueling accounts — the club's flat denial against a hotel's documented complaints — with no independent Cypriot or Israeli outlet yet confirming either version in full.

title: Camoranesi brings his anti-Spain football creed to Beitar Jerusalem test
dek: The World Cup winner turned AEK Larnaca coach has never hidden his disdain for Spain's passing game — now his Cypriot side face Beitar Jerusalem in the Conference League with a very different approach.

verificationSources.label: ONE
Sport1/Maariv - Beitar injury news
Jerusalem Post - Almog Cohen appointment
Il Messaggero - Camoranesi to Larnaca
ESPN - 2026 World Cup final result

body: Beitar Jerusalem's push into Europe this evening runs into a Cypriot club being remade in the image of a coach who has built a chunk of his footballing identity around loathing the Spanish passing game.

AEK Larnaca host Beitar in the second qualifying round of the Conference League on Thursday, kicking off at 19:30 in Larnaca. The return leg is set for July 30 in Ploiești, Romania — Beitar's designated neutral venue for European home fixtures.

The Larnaca dugout is now occupied by Mauro Camoranesi, 49, born in Tandil, Argentina, but capped 55 times by Italy — with whom he won the 2006 World Cup — after a decade in Serie A spent mostly at Juventus following his move from Hellas Verona in 2000.

Camoranesi was named AEK Larnaca's head coach on July 1 on a contract running through May 2027, taking charge of a club that finished runner-up in the Cypriot league last season and reached the Conference League round of 16 before losing to eventual champions Crystal Palace.

His coaching résumé since retiring has been a winding one: spells in Mexico and Argentina, Slovenia's Tabor Sežana and then Maribor, where he was sacked after six months, a week as Igor Tudor's assistant at Marseille before being replaced, and two seasons at Malta's Floriana, where he lost a cup final on penalties before leaving in 2024.

What runs through all of it, according to ONE, is an open contempt for possession football of the kind Spain has made its trademark. Camoranesi has been quoted as saying Italians "get bored watching Spain — thousands of passes back and forth," adding that he doesn't like "patient football" and wants his teams to reach goal "as fast as possible, with the fewest touches possible."

The timing gives the line extra bite. Spain won the 2026 World Cup on July 19, beating Camoranesi's native Argentina 1-0 in the final on a Ferran Torres extra-time strike — a result that stung plenty of Argentines just days before their compatriot-turned-Italian faces an Israeli club with a Spanish-style pedigree of its own.

Beitar arrive in Cyprus under their own new management. Almog Cohen, previously the club's sporting director, was elevated to head coach on May 31 after Barak Yitzhaki's exit, and tonight's qualifier is the first serious European test of his early tenure.

Cohen will be without several key names. Defender Luka Gadrani remains sidelined by a shin injury picked up on international duty with Georgia and has not trained with the squad, while Adi Yona and Tomer Yosephi are also out. Gil Cohen or Liel Darei is expected to partner Brian Rabello in central defense, with Omer Atzili more likely to start from the bench than in the XI.

It sets up a stylistic mismatch as much as a sporting one — an Argentine World Cup winner preaching directness against an Israeli club trying to find its footing under a rookie coach, with a Conference League place on the line over two legs.

title: Maccabi Haifa close in on well-travelled Wolves defender Nigel Lonwijk
dek: The 23-year-old Dutchman, a PSV academy product who never played a first-team match at Molineux, is set to fill the gap left by Abdoulaye Seck's departure to Saudi Arabia.

verificationSources.label: ONE - original report
Wikipedia - Nigel Lonwijk career record
Wolves official site - Lonwijk loan profile
Israel Hayom - Abdoulaye Seck's Maccabi Haifa career ends, joins Al-Faisaly

body: Maccabi Haifa are working to add a new centre-back before the new Israeli season begins, and according to ONE the club has turned to a defender with an unusually well-travelled résumé for someone still only 23: Nigel Lonwijk, currently on Wolverhampton Wanderers' books.

The move, ONE reports, is designed to fill the void left by Abdoulaye Seck. The Senegalese centre-back was a fixture at the back for Haifa for four seasons, making 147 appearances and scoring 14 goals, before his contract talks broke down over the length of a new deal and he signed instead for Saudi Arabia's newly promoted Al-Faisaly this summer.

Lonwijk is a product of PSV Eindhoven's academy, where he spent roughly a decade before leaving for England and signing with Wolves in January 2020 as a highly regarded teenage prospect. Despite that pedigree, and a contract extension at Molineux along the way, he has never made a competitive first-team appearance for the Premier League club.

Instead, his development has come entirely out on loan. Since 2021 he has worn the shirts of Fortuna Sittard in the Eredivisie, Plymouth Argyle, Grasshopper Club Zürich, Wycombe Wanderers, Huddersfield Town and, most recently, Luton Town — six different loan spells in five years without ever cementing a place back at Wolves.

The high point came at Plymouth Argyle in 2022-23, where he made 35 appearances as the Devon club won the League One title. He has mostly featured in England's third and second tiers since, with brief stops at Wycombe Wanderers and Huddersfield Town before a longer loan at Luton Town in the Championship this past season, where he made 37 appearances and scored twice — often deployed at right-back rather than his more natural centre-back position, underlining a versatility that will appeal to Haifa's coaching staff.

Explaining his original decision to leave PSV for England, Lonwijk said at the time: "I love challenges. I've always loved English football, so the decision wasn't difficult for me. After ten years at Eindhoven I needed a change of atmosphere. Wolves staff explained their plans for me, and I loved what I heard. I think it can advance my career."

That career advance never quite materialised at Molineux itself, and at international level his recognition has been similarly modest — a single cap for the Netherlands under-16s back in 2018, with no involvement at senior youth or full international level since.

For Maccabi Haifa, the logic is straightforward: a tall, athletic, left-sided defender still just 23, available after Wolves opted not to keep pushing him through their own pathway, arrives as a replacement for a proven starter without the transfer-market premium a fully established centre-back would command. ONE did not report financial terms of the move, and the precise structure of the deal — permanent transfer or loan — was not specified in the original report.

Whether Lonwijk can finally deliver on the promise that took him from PSV to Wolves as a teenager will now be tested in the Israeli Premier League, in a defence Haifa need rebuilt before their title defence gets under way.

title: Mbappé reportedly lobbying Olise to join him at Real Madrid
dek: The France captain has told Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez he has convinced Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise to make the move to the Bernabéu, ONE reports — though Bayern insist their man isn't going anywhere.

verificationSources.label: ONE — original report

body: Kylian Mbappé has apparently decided that landing Real Madrid's next Galáctico is partly his job too. According to Germany's Bild, relayed by ONE, the France captain has personally worked on France teammate Michael Olise to push the Bayern Munich winger toward the Bernabéu — and has already told club president Florentino Pérez that he believes he has succeeded.

The report describes a sustained charm offensive built around the two players' close bond in the France squad. Mbappé is said to have talked up life in Madrid to Olise directly — the football project, but also the lifestyle, from the restaurants to the climate — while assuring him that Real Madrid genuinely want him.

The timing lines up with France's summer at the World Cup. Les Bleus were eliminated in the semi-finals on July 14, beaten 2-0 by Spain, and Bild's report ties Olise's hardened resolve to leave Bayern directly to that exit — with the 24-year-old reportedly concluding his odds of winning the Champions League are considerably better in Madrid than in Munich.

Pérez has made no secret of wanting a marquee addition since his re-election as Real Madrid president, and Olise has emerged as a prime target, with Spanish reports over recent weeks floating a bid in the region of €220 million for the winger. Whether Real actually go that high remains to be seen, but the interest from the Bernabéu is not in doubt.

Bayern's position is the opposite of accommodating. The club has explicitly rejected the idea of selling Olise, regarding him as a core piece of their squad rather than a player to be cashed in on, and — according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano — are working on a new and improved contract to tie him down rather than field offers.

Olise signed for Bayern from Crystal Palace in the summer of 2024 for a fee of around €53 million and has since become one of the Bundesliga's most productive wide players. He remains under contract in Munich until 2029, with no release clause, which gives Bayern real leverage even against a club of Real Madrid's stature.

Bild's report does add a caveat: Olise, while telling French teammates of his wish to leave, is not expected to force the issue or turn himself into a problem for Bayern this summer. Sport Bild's reporting suggests any deal would only move if Olise himself goes to both clubs' hierarchies and makes his desire to leave explicit.

For now, there has been no direct contact between Real Madrid and Bayern Munich over a transfer, leaving this squarely in rumor territory — fuelled by Mbappé's lobbying and Pérez's ambition, but not yet backed by anything close to a formal approach.

It is a familiar dynamic for Real Madrid, whose recent transfer business under Pérez has repeatedly leaned on star players talking up the club to potential signings from within their own national-team dressing rooms — precisely the tactic Mbappé appears to be running now on his French compatriot.

title: Fulham chase Real Madrid pair García and Mastantuono as Arbeloa raids old club
dek: New Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa wants to reunite with two players from his brief spell in Madrid — a permanent deal for striker Gonzalo García and a season-long loan for teenage sensation Franco Mastantuono, according to a report from ONE.

body: Fulham have opened talks with Real Madrid over two players from Álvaro Arbeloa's old dressing room, the Israeli outlet ONE reports — a permanent move for young striker Gonzalo García and a season-long loan for Argentine playmaker Franco Mastantuono.

Arbeloa, unveiled as Fulham head coach on July 8 after Marco Silva departed for Benfica, knows both players well. He took charge of Real Madrid Castilla in May 2025, then found himself running the senior side on an interim basis after Xabi Alonso's exit in January, before José Mourinho arrived to take permanent control. García broke through under him at Castilla, while Mastantuono made his early Real Madrid appearances during that same stretch.

García, 22, is a product of Real Madrid's academy who forced his way into the first-team picture last season, contributing to the club's Champions League and LaLiga triumphs along the way. Fulham are preparing a formal offer and see him as an attacking reinforcement for the new Premier League campaign.

Real Madrid are open to selling him — reports in Spain suggest the club had planned for García to leave even before Mourinho's arrival — but want to protect their long-term interest, either through a buy-back clause or a sell-on percentage, rather than a clean-break sale.
Mourinho, for his part, wants to run the rule over García during preseason training before Real Madrid sign off on any exit, meaning a final answer on his future is unlikely to arrive immediately.

Mastantuono is a different proposition: at 18, he is one of the most closely guarded prospects in Madrid. He joined from River Plate in 2025 after becoming Argentina's youngest ever full international, and Real Madrid regard him as part of their long-term core rather than a player to be sold.

That is why any move for the winger would be a loan rather than a permanent departure, with the fee structure still to be worked out and Real Madrid, according to some reports, still reluctant to let him leave at all this window. Fulham are pushing for the arrangement to include no option to buy attached, in line with what Madrid have indicated they will accept.

Fulham are not alone in the chase — Tottenham have also made contact with Real Madrid to sound out the conditions of a possible Mastantuono loan, adding urgency to Arbeloa's efforts to get a deal wrapped up quickly.

Nothing is close to signed on either front. Both moves hinge on Mourinho's preseason evaluations in Madrid and on face-to-face talks between the manager and the two players before Real Madrid's board engages formally with Fulham's proposals.

title: Hapoel Haifa reopens old file, chases return of William Agada
dek: Coach Haim Silves has put the Nigerian forward, who once starred on loan in the Carmel, back at the top of Hapoel Haifa's wanted list, ONE reports.

body: Hapoel Haifa is going back to a forward it already knows well. ONE reports that coach Haim Silves has identified William Agada, the Nigerian striker who once wore the club's shirt on loan, as one of his top targets to reinforce the attack this summer, and that the club is now in negotiations to bring him back to the Carmel.

The pursuit is a reunion of sorts. Agada spent the 2020/21 season on loan at Hapoel Haifa from Hapoel Katamon Jerusalem, and it was there, still only 21, that he first showed the finishing that would define his career, scoring regularly for a Silves side that leaned on him up front.

From Haifa he returned to Jerusalem, where he was the club's top scorer in 2021/22 with eight league goals as Hapoel Jerusalem fought to stay in the Israeli Premier League. Across four seasons in Israeli football, split between Jerusalem and the Haifa loan spell, he scored 37 league goals - a return that eventually carried him out of the country altogether.

Sporting Kansas City signed Agada from Hapoel Jerusalem in July 2022, and he quickly became a fixture in MLS, twice finishing as the club's top scorer. He moved on to Real Salt Lake in 2025 before a further switch this past January to Real Zaragoza in Spain's second division, where he is currently under contract through the end of the season.

That contract situation is why ONE frames Agada as "relatively expensive" for Hapoel Haifa to land - any deal now would likely mean negotiating a fee, or a loan, with a European club rather than a free pickup. According to the report, agent Yoav Katz is handling the talks on Agada's behalf.

If completed, the move would give Silves a genuine second scoring threat alongside Alon Torgeman, pairing a proven Israeli Premier League finisher with a forward who already knows the dressing room, the coach and, by his own account from his first Haifa spell, the feeling of being trusted as a starter.

Agada has barely featured for Zaragoza since his January arrival, and a summer switch back to a league where he has a track record of goals would not be unprecedented for a player looking to rebuild his minutes. Nothing has been made official by either club, and no fee or contract length has been reported.

For Hapoel Haifa, the interest fits a wider pattern of a squad being rebuilt for the new season, with Silves keen to add proven firepower before the Israeli Premier League campaign gets underway. ONE's report leaves the negotiation open rather than concluded, and further movement is expected to be reported as talks progress.

title: Winner's odds make Maccabi Tel Aviv the only Israeli favourite tonight
dek: Israeli bookmaker Winner prices Maccabi Tel Aviv to beat Sheriff Tiraspol, but has both Beitar Jerusalem and Hapoel Tel Aviv as underdogs as three Israeli clubs open their European campaigns on the same night.

body: Three Israeli clubs kick off their European campaigns on the same evening, and according to the odds Winner has put up for the night, only one of them is expected to win.

ONE reports that the bookmaker prices Maccabi Tel Aviv as clear favourites for their trip to Sheriff Tiraspol in the Europa League second qualifying round, at odds of 2.05 against 2.90 for the Moldovan champions. It is a different story for the other two: Beitar Jerusalem, away to AEK Larnaca in the Conference League, are underdogs at 3.05 with the Cypriots priced at 1.95, and Hapoel Tel Aviv are underdogs even at home, at 2.85 against 2.00 for Bulgarian side Ludogorets Razgrad.
All three are first legs of second qualifying round ties, played on Thursday July 23, with the second legs following a week later on July 30.

Maccabi arrive in Tiraspol with genuine momentum. They lifted the Israeli Super Cup on July 16 with a 3-1 win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva, and this is their fourth straight season in continental competition, a run of European experience Sheriff — who needed a 1-0 win at Aluminij just to survive the first qualifying round — cannot match. Win or lose over the two legs, the tie's outcome already has a route mapped out: the winner meets whoever comes through Qarabağ against CSKA Sofia in the Europa League third qualifying round, while the loser drops into the Conference League to face the loser of St Gallen against Benfica.

Beitar Jerusalem head to the AEK Arena in Larnaca off the back of a penalty-shootout defeat to Hapoel Tel Aviv in the Toto Cup, and Winner's odds reflect a club still finding its footing against a Cypriot side with recent continental pedigree.

Hapoel Tel Aviv, by contrast, arrive at Bloomfield Stadium unbeaten in six matches, but that hasn't been enough to make them favourites against Ludogorets, who are chasing a European group-stage berth for an eleventh consecutive season. The fixture is a landmark one regardless of the result: it is Hapoel's first appearance in European competition since a 2014-15 Europa League qualifying exit to Astana, and their first-ever entry into the Conference League.

None of this amounts to a prediction — Winner's odds are a market snapshot, not a result, and two-legged qualifying ties have a habit of flipping on a single away goal or a red card. But the numbers do capture where Israeli football's three European entrants stand on paper tonight: one clear favourite, and two clubs being asked to prove the bookmakers wrong.

title: LeBron James stalls free agency, banking on a trade for Irving or Davis
dek: Three weeks after leaving the Lakers, the 41-year-old still hasn't picked his next team — reportedly because he's waiting to see if a suitor can first engineer a reunion with Kyrie Irving or Anthony Davis.

verificationSources.label: ONE — original report
Yahoo Sports — Kevin O'Connor
Cleveland19 — Kyrie/Davis angle

body: More than three weeks into free agency, LeBron James still hasn't said where he's playing next season — and according to a report picked up by ONE, that's by design. The 41-year-old is deliberately slow-playing his decision, several outlets now report, in the hope that one of his suitors can first pull off a trade for either Kyrie Irving or Anthony Davis.

James left the Lakers after eight seasons once the NBA's free-agency negotiating window opened on June 30, ending an era in which he restored the franchise to relevance but never recaptured the 2020 championship high with Davis at his side. Since then, the league's most closely watched free agent has offered almost nothing about his thinking beyond hints that a decision is coming.

Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor reported this week that James is holding off specifically to see whether a team courting him can also engineer a reunion with Irving or Davis — the two co-stars who delivered two of his four championships. Irving helped end Cleveland's 52-year title drought in 2016; Davis partnered him for the bubble title with the Lakers in 2020.

Neither reunion looks straightforward. Irving, now with the Dallas Mavericks, is still working back from the torn ACL that ended his 2024-25 season early, and Dallas has given no indication it intends to move him. Davis, dealt to Washington in the blockbuster that sent Luka Dončić to the Lakers, still has two years and roughly $120 million left on his contract — an expensive, complicated piece for any team to pry loose from the rebuilding Wizards.

That hasn't stopped teams from trying to make the numbers work anyway. Reports have floated Cleveland exploring a package built around James Harden to bring Irving back and effectively recreate the Cavaliers' 2016 title nucleus — LeBron, Irving and Kevin Love reborn as a 2026 vintage.

Golden State's interest runs in a similar direction. The Warriors have long coveted pairing James with Stephen Curry, and Walla Sport reports the club has also been working to land Davis from Washington as part of the same push — an attempt to build a roster deep enough to persuade James that the fit, not just the name recognition, is real.

Miami and Philadelphia round out the group most consistently named as finalists, with Jimmy Butler's Heat and a 76ers team still built around Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey both making their pitches. Neither has been linked to an Irving or Davis trade, but both are seen as offering a clearer, ready-made path to contention.

Then there's the long shot with the loudest pitch. Minnesota's Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball have personally phoned James to recruit him to the Timberwolves, according to reporting picked up widely in the American press — even though Edwards has separately admitted Minnesota isn't among the three teams James is said to be seriously considering. The calls say less about Minnesota's chances than about how badly rival locker rooms want to be the ones to land him.

Through it all, James's camp is projecting patience rather than urgency. His longtime agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, has said simply: "We're not going to be rushed." It's a notably different posture from the made-for-television 'Decision' era of James's career — no cameras, no fixed date, just a 41-year-old waiting to see what his former teammates' teams do first.

The stakes for whichever franchise wins him are not symbolic. James averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists for the Lakers last season, still an every-night contributor entering what would be his 24th NBA campaign. For four teams, and perhaps a fifth making noise from the outside, that production is worth the wait — even if the trade James is reportedly hoping for never actually happens.

title: Al-Hilal make surprise move for Dembélé as PSG contract talks stall
dek: Saudi champions Al-Hilal have quietly reached out to Ousmane Dembélé's camp as the Ballon d'Or winner's stalled renewal talks with PSG threaten to collapse, according to reports.

verificationSources.label: Sport1 (Maariv)

body: Ousmane Dembélé's contract standoff with Paris Saint-Germain has picked up an unexpected suitor. Sport1 reports that Al-Hilal have made preliminary contact with the French forward's representatives, opening the door to a move that would blow up months of stop-start renewal talks in Paris.

The report, citing French journalist Sacha Tavolieri, says Al-Hilal have not yet approached PSG directly. The Saudi club is first sounding out whether Dembélé himself would even consider a move to the Saudi Pro League before deciding whether to make a formal offer to the French champions.

The timing is pointed. Dembélé, who won the 2025 Ballon d'Or after inspiring PSG's continental treble under Luis Enrique, has been locked in slow-moving contract talks with the club for months. His current deal runs to June 2028, but PSG have been pushing to extend it and remove any uncertainty over their biggest star.

The gap between the two sides has been the sticking point. PSG have offered around €30 million a year over a new three-year deal, while Dembélé's camp has been seeking closer to €60 million annually — roughly double his current salary, which already makes him the club's highest earner.

Al-Hilal, bankrolled by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, have made no secret of their ambition to keep landing marquee attacking talent. They have already signed winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham United this summer and see a player of Dembélé's stature as the kind of statement addition that would elevate the club's profile further.

For now, according to the report, Al-Hilal are holding off on any approach to PSG until they get a clearer signal from Dembélé's side that he would be open to the move. Only then would talks with the French club begin in earnest.

PSG, for their part, are not expected to entertain a sale easily. Having built their recent success around Dembélé and repeatedly stated their intention to tie him down long-term, the club has shown no appetite to let its Ballon d'Or winner leave while a new contract is still, at least in theory, on the table.

Still, the fact that a rival club felt it worth testing the waters underlines how far apart PSG and Dembélé's camp remain on salary. If the renewal talks in Paris do collapse, Sport1's report suggests Al-Hilal would be ready to move quickly — and they may not be the only ones watching from the outside.

title: Maccabi Netanya close to loan deal for Sheffield United winger Nwachukwu
dek: The Israeli top-flight club is finalizing terms with Sheffield United for a loan-with-option move for Christian Nwachukwu, a 20-year-old Nigerian winger currently out on loan in Turkey, according to Sport5.

body: Maccabi Netanya are closing in on a deal to bring Nigerian winger Christian Nwachukwu to Israel on loan, with an option to make the move permanent further down the line, Sport5 reports.

Nwachukwu, 20, is Sheffield United property, having been signed by the Championship club from Bulgaria's Botev Plovdiv in February 2025 for a reported fee in the region of €1.2 million on a contract running to the summer of 2027. This past season he was farmed out on loan to Serikspor in Turkey to accumulate first-team minutes.

According to the report, Netanya's American owner Ross Kastin is pushing for exactly this kind of profile — a young, developing talent his club can coach up and potentially sell on for a profit, rather than an established, expensive veteran. Kastin's Aliya Capital Partners took control of the club from longtime owner Eyal Sagal, and his stated strategy since taking over has centered on player trading alongside on-field ambition.

A fleet-footed left-sided winger capable of playing on the right or through the middle, Nwachukwu made his name at Botev Plovdiv, where he was part of the squad that won the Bulgarian Cup and also picked up Europa League experience, before scoring four goals in his breakthrough campaign that persuaded Sheffield United to move for him.

Sport5 reports the deal is being brokered through agent Satio Chachmon, and describes it as close to completion rather than finished — the structure being discussed is a loan with a purchase option, which would let Netanya evaluate Nwachukwu in Ligat Ha'al before committing to a permanent transfer fee.

The move would fit the pattern of Netanya's summer rebuild under Kastin's ownership, with the club also said to be working on bringing in a defender and monitoring the futures of players already on the books, including forward Aziz Aouatrah, with a replacement plan in place should he depart.

Separately, Sport5 notes that goalkeeper Omer Niron has returned unexpectedly to full training after completing rehabilitation from the ankle injury that ended his season early, a development the outlet frames as a signal to clubs who had been circling him as Netanya's number one is otherwise occupied.

Nothing is signed yet, and the loan-with-option structure still needs to be finalized between the two clubs, but if it goes through, Nwachukwu would become the latest young overseas prospect to test himself in Israeli football before, potentially, moving back up the ladder in Europe.

title: Tiberias warns it will field an all-youth side if hit with any further points deduction
dek: Owner Arie Kalmanzon calls a withdrawn tribunal petition "a meaningful and positive step," but a senior club official says Ironi Tiberias will turn to its academy and let unhappy players go if the Israel Football Association docks even one more point over the double-contracts affair.

verificationSources.label: Sport5
Haaretz
Sport1/Maariv
Walla Sport
Ynet

body: Ironi Tiberias have issued a blunt warning to Israeli football's disciplinary establishment: take even one more point off the club over the so-called double-contracts affair, and Ligat Ha'al will be watching an entirely youth-led side for the rest of the season. "If they deduct even one point from us, we'll go up with youth players," a senior club official said this week, according to Sport5. "We'll turn it into an economic year, and any player who wants to leave will be released."

The threat followed a hearing on Wednesday before the Israel Football Association's supreme disciplinary tribunal, where Tiberias had petitioned over the ongoing proceedings tied to its handling of player contracts. The judges declined to grant the dismissal the club's petition sought, siding instead with the federation's prosecutor.

Tiberias then withdrew the petition altogether — but owner Arie Kalmanzon insisted the club still came away encouraged, describing assurances he said were given by the prosecution's lawyer during the session. "The judges discussed the petition but refused to dismiss it outright, as the prosecutor had asked," Kalmanzon said, according to Sport5. "We withdrew it. We felt a meaningful and positive step had been taken."

The case dates back to a plea agreement approved by the disciplinary tribunal in April, after Tiberias was found to have signed undisclosed supplementary agreements with players — arrangements that bypassed the league's budget-oversight process, a practice known in Israeli football as "double contracts." That settlement cost the club eight points in the 2025/26 season, a further six points for the current 2026/27 campaign, a fine of 500,000 shekels and a ban on registering new players in the January 2027 transfer window. Former club figure Miki Bitan received a seven-year suspension from football activity over the affair.

Those six points are already gone from Tiberias's ledger before a ball has been kicked in the new Ligat Ha'al season, and this week's hearing raised the prospect of the federation coming back for more. Sport5 did not specify how many additional points are under consideration, only that the club now regards any further deduction as a red line.

The contracts case is not the only disciplinary front the club is fighting. Head coach Eliran Hudeda remains sidelined in a separate matter, after the Israel Anti-Doping Agency and the federation opened an investigation into allegedly excessive saline infusions given to Tiberias players before a match against Ashdod last season — a complaint Ashdod itself filed. Tiberias has maintained the fluids were legal and administered within permitted limits.
With Hudeda unable to work the touchline, the club has turned to Maurice Ozen, the veteran head of its youth department, who has been approved to serve as interim first-team coach for one month.

The squad Ozen inherits for now is already stretched thin. Several players are suspended, the club's foreign-player quota is close to full following the summer arrival of Ivorian midfielder Chris Quacko, and new signing Gal Metuak has yet to be registered to play while his contract paperwork is finalised.

None of it has dented the club's spending ambitions. Tiberias have set a budget of 21 million shekels for the season, three million more than last year, with 13.5 million earmarked for player salaries — a sign the ownership still intends to compete near the top of the table even as it fights the federation on two fronts.

For a club that has spent the close season lurching between tribunal hearings and doping inquiries, the youth-team threat reads as much as a statement of frustration as a genuine tactical plan. But with the disciplinary process still unresolved, Tiberias's hierarchy has made clear it sees a further points penalty as the point at which cooperation ends.

title: Abada nets a brace, Baribo strikes late as Blorian tastes first MLS win
dek: Three Israelis were involved across MLS on the same night — Liel Abada scored twice for Charlotte, Tai Baribo salvaged a point for DC United, and new Sporting Kansas City signing Or Blorian started at left-back in a 2-1 win over Minnesota.

source.originalTitle: עבדה ובריבו כבשו, ניצחון לבלוריאן וקנזס סיטי
