body: Gaya Datiashvili closed the ILCA 6 Youth European Championships in Thessaloniki on Saturday as the seventh-ranked European in an 89-boat girls' fleet, extending a run of top-ten continental finishes that has made the Hapoel Zvulun Acre sailor the most consistent presence in Israel's youth dinghy programme.

The official results place her eighth across the line overall. New Zealand's Chloe Turner, third, raced for the accompanying Open European Trophy rather than the championship itself, which left Datiashvili seventh in the European championship classification.

Her twelve-race series at the Nautical Club of Kalamaria was a study in recovery. She won the opening race outright, then slumped to 35th in the second and was disqualified under the U flag for a premature start in race four — a score she was able to discard.
From there she steadied through qualifying to make the gold fleet, then produced her best sailing of the week at the start of the final series with a third and a race win.

Two heavy scores of 35 and 21 followed before she closed with a tenth and a sixth, ending on 131 net points. In a format with no medal race, that consistency over a dozen starts is what the class rewards.

The championship, sailed from 10 to 18 July in light and moderate winds on the Thermaic Gulf, drew 314 sailors — 89 girls and 225 boys. The girls' title went to the home fleet through Greece's Hermionie Ghicas on 58 net points.

Datiashvili arrived as a genuine contender, having finished fourth at last year's European championship and fourth at the 2025 ILCA 6 Youth Worlds in Los Angeles. Her coaches' assessment after racing was candid: she competed at the front for most of the week, but the mid-series inconsistency and the start disqualification cost her a shot at a first international medal.

The boys' team delivered Israel's other headline result. Yahav Geva, also of Hapoel Zvulun Acre, finished 14th overall in the 225-boat male fleet — the best Israeli placing among the boys — winning two qualifying races and signing off with a second place in the final race of the regatta.

Gal Einav of Hapoel Tel Aviv followed in 18th. Both marks represent a clear step up from Israel's leading boys' finishes of 35th and 40th at the previous edition, in a fleet won by Lithuania's Erik Scheidt.

Rebecca Mantel, the second Israeli girl, took fourth place in the silver fleet, closing her week with a race win in the last start. The delegation of twelve — ten boys and two girls — returns directly to training, with the class youth world championship scheduled for mid-August.

For the Israel Sailing Association, Thessaloniki reinforces the ILCA 6 as the productive middle of its youth pathway. A sailor who has now gone fourth, fourth and seventh at major youth championships in successive seasons is knocking persistently on the door of a podium.

Her series included a race-one win, a U-flag disqualification in race four (her discard) and a gold-fleet race win; the format had no medal race.

title: Eli Ohana bids official farewell: "I have finished my path in football"
dek: The 62-year-old Beitar Jerusalem great and 1988 Cup Winners' Cup winner has ruled out ever returning as a coach or executive, dismissing talk of leading Israel alongside Eyal Berkovic and confirming that broadcasting is now his only place in the game.

source.name: Sport1 / Maariv
source.originalTitle: אלי אוחנה נפרד באופן רשמי: "סיימתי את דרכי"
source.author: Sport1 editorial team

verificationSources.label: English Wikipedia record of Eli Ohana's playing, managerial and executive career
Hebrew Wikipedia record confirming honours, 51 caps and 17 goals, the 1988 Cup Winners' Cup role and the 2017-2022 Beitar chairmanship

body: Eli Ohana, one of the greatest footballers Israel has produced, has formally declared his working life in the game over. Asked on the radio programme he presents on Sunday morning whether he would agree to lead the national team alongside Eyal Berkovic, the 62-year-old closed the door without hesitation. "Me and Berkovic to the Israel national team together? There is no chance — it is of no interest," he said. "In sport and in football I am staying only at the sports channel. I have finished my path in football."

The declaration formalises a retreat that has been under way for some time. Ohana has held no formal post since stepping down as Beitar Jerusalem chairman in May 2022, yet his name has rarely left conversations about vacancies at his old club or on the national-team staff. Sunday's remarks were his most explicit farewell yet: no return as coach, executive or federation figure — only the pundit's chair.

It ends one of the richest careers in Israeli football. Nicknamed "King Ohana", the forward came through Beitar Jerusalem's youth ranks and starred for the club across two spells, from 1980 to 1987 and again from 1991 to 1999. He won four Israeli championships in that time — in 1986-87, 1992-93, 1996-97 and 1997-98 — along with State Cups in 1984-85 and 1985-86.

In between came the achievement that made him a landmark figure for the Israeli game. At KV Mechelen between 1987 and 1990 he won the 1987-88 European Cup Winners' Cup, scoring in the semi-final and setting up the winning goal in the 1-0 final victory over Ajax, to become the first Israeli footballer to win a European club trophy.
He added the 1988 European Super Cup with the Belgian side and received the Bravo Award that same year. Between 1984 and 1997 he scored 17 goals in 51 appearances for Israel.

His second career kept him close to the touchline for two more decades. He managed Beitar Jerusalem and other Israeli clubs, led Israel's under-19 side from 2008 to 2016, took caretaker charge of the senior national team in 2010, sat on the Israel Football Association's executive and served as Beitar chairman from May 2017 to May 2022.

Reflecting on Israel's repeated failure to reach major tournaments, Ohana rejected the idea that coaching was to blame. "I do not think Israel's problem over the years has been the coaches. There have been excellent coaches, both foreign and Israeli," he said. "At the end of the day the players do the work on the pitch — their influence is even greater than the coaches'."

Nor does he expect Berkovic, once a mooted candidate, to take the national job. "If you had said Berko to me three or four years ago, I would have been with you. Today? I am not sure he would go. From what I understand — and I have heard him say it himself — that matter is already behind him."

The farewell came, fittingly, with Ohana still at work: his remarks aired hours before Sunday evening's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain, which he was previewing as a broadcaster, sticking with the Spain tip he has carried since the start of the tournament. The man who took Israeli football to a European final will watch this one from the studio — which, by his own words, is now where his story in the game continues.

With KV Mechelen he won the 1987-88 European Cup Winners' Cup — scoring in the semi-final and assisting the winner in the final against Ajax — becoming the first Israeli footballer to win a European club trophy.
He scored 17 goals in 51 appearances for Israel between 1984 and 1997.
After playing he managed Beitar Jerusalem among other clubs, coached Israel's under-19s from 2008 to 2016, and served as Beitar Jerusalem chairman from May 2017 to May 2022.

body: Twenty-one years of waiting ended in a near-empty hall in Cluj-Napoca on Sunday lunchtime. Israel's under-20 handball team beat Croatia 36:31 in the 15th-place match of the M20 EHF EURO in Romania, claiming the final ranking position that carries qualification for the age group's World Championship. According to Hebrew-language coverage, it is the first time the side known domestically as the reserve national team has reached the tournament since 2005, with the finals now awaiting in North Macedonia in the summer of 2027.

It was done the hard way. Israel trailed 14:17 at the interval, a scoreline confirmed by the official match record, against opponents from one of Europe's genuine handball powers. What followed was the best half of Israel's tournament: a 22:14 surge after the break turned a three-goal deficit into a five-goal victory, completed barely 48 hours after the same squad had been dismantled 35:23 by Iceland.

The comeback was driven by two players in relentless scoring form. Guy Ran Arman, listed on the official match sheet under the surname Resch Erman, struck 11 goals, and Loïc Bakasu Bibange added ten, the pair accounting for 21 of Israel's 36. Yonatan Pelach contributed five, Adi Cohen four, Asaf Sharon and Ben Gross two apiece, and Uri Cohen and Itamar Goldstein one each.

Behind them, the goalkeeping load was shared. Hebrew-language reports credit Alon Rossabi with six saves at a 33 per cent stop rate, Yehonatan Benshitrit with four, and Eitan Elbaz with three. The win owed nothing to the seven-metre line: the official sheet shows Croatia converted seven of eight penalties while Israel scored just one from two, meaning the 36 goals were built almost entirely from open play. Croatia's Moslavac finished with ten at the other end but found too little support once the second half turned.

The route to this decider was unforgiving. Israel arrived off the back of Friday's heavy defeat to Iceland, fielding a squad the Hebrew coverage had described as shorn of four players, while Croatia dropped into the tie after losing their placement meeting with the host nation. On paper it was a mismatch of pedigrees; on the court, Israel's response after the interval settled it emphatically.

The setting gave little hint of the occasion. The official record logs a 12:00 throw-off at the Horia Demian hall in Cluj-Napoca in front of just 60 spectators, a modest stage for the most consequential result an Israeli age-grade handball team has produced in more than two decades.

The wider arc makes the achievement sweeter still. This tournament brought heavy defeats to Sweden, Romania, Czechia and Iceland around wins over Bosnia and Herzegovina and Poland, and after the Iceland loss the campaign had come down to a single winner-takes-all fixture. The players delivered when only victory would do, and a generation that has spent a fortnight absorbing hard lessons in Romania will now test itself against the world's best junior sides next summer.
facts: Israel beat Croatia 36:31 (half-time 14:17 to Croatia) on 19 July 2026 in the 15th-place match of the M20 EHF EURO, per the official EHF match record (match 089; 12:00 throw-off, Horia Demian hall, Cluj-Napoca, 60 spectators).

Fifteenth place secured qualification for the age group's World Championship; Israeli reports state it is the reserve team's first qualification since 2005 and that the 2027 junior World Championship will be staged in North Macedonia.

Guy Ran Arman (match sheet: Resch Erman, No. 3) scored 11 goals and Loïc Bakasu Bibange (No. 34) 10; Yonatan Pelach added 5, Adi Cohen 4, Asaf Sharon 2, Ben Gross 2, Uri Cohen 1 and Itamar Goldstein 1.
Israeli goalkeeper figures per the Hebrew reports: Alon Rossabi 6 saves (33%), Yehonatan Benshitrit 4 (23%), Eitan Elbaz 3 (30%).
The official sheet shows Croatia converted 7 of 8 seven-metre throws to Israel's 1 of 2; Croatia's top scorer Moslavac finished with 10 goals.
Israel won the second half 22:14 after trailing by three at the interval, two days after losing 35:23 to Iceland.

title: Israeli teenagers clock 2:15.00 to erase 35-year-old 1,000m relay record in Rieti
dek: Nivi Seligmann, Roni Rabinovitz, Koral Tsimbalist and Hila Varsano took nearly five seconds off a national mark that had stood since 1991, closing Israel's European under-18 championships on a record even without a place in the final.

body: Israel's under-18 women closed their European championships in Rieti with a national record. Nivi Seligmann, Roni Rabinovitz, Koral Tsimbalist and Hila Varsano ran 2:15.00 in Sunday's opening round of the 1,000m medley relay at the Stadio Raul Guidobaldi — a time confirmed on the official results — to set a new Israeli best over the rarely contested distance.

The mark they beat had stood for 35 years: 2:19.7, set back in 1991. Sunday's quartet stripped almost five seconds off it in a single run of the sprint-medley format, whose legs of 100, 200, 300 and 400 metres were shared out with Seligmann of Leader Netanya leading off, Maccabi Tel Aviv's Rabinovitz and Maccabi Ramat Hasharon's Tsimbalist carrying the middle two legs, and Varsano closing on the 400m.

The record did not come with progression attached. Israel finished seventh in the third heat, 20th of the 24 nations entered, and missed the final in a round where Czechia's 2:07.62 led all qualifiers and every finalist broke 2:10.
For a team assembled from three clubs in an event Israel almost never races, the gap to the leaders reads less as a verdict than as a starting point.

For Varsano, the relay capped a heavy weekend. A day earlier the 17-year-old had run her 400m hurdles semi-final, finishing eighth in the third semi in 1:02.11 to fall short of the final — an entirely forgivable exit two days after a 1:00.02 in the heats had lowered her own Israeli under-18 record.

There was a sharper ending on the infield during the same session. Ido Noam took sixth place in the 2,000m steeplechase final in 5:53.96, delivering exactly the top-eight finish the national federation's professional director had predicted for him.
Aviv Ochman fared tougher in the same race, caught out in a punishing pace and coming home 14th in 6:19.99.
Israel left Rieti with two new national marks to show for the trip — one individual, one shared by four teenagers who had never run faster.
facts: Israel's under-18 women's team of Nivi Seligmann, Roni Rabinovitz, Koral Tsimbalist and Hila Varsano ran 2:15.00 in round 1 of the 1,000m medley relay at the 2026 European Athletics U18 Championships in Rieti on 19 July 2026, confirmed on the official World Athletics results page.
The time is reported as a new Israeli record for the 1,000m relay, beating a 2:19.7 mark that had stood since 1991.
Israel finished seventh in heat 3 and 20th of the 24 nations entered; Czechia led round 1 with 2:07.62.
Hila Varsano finished eighth in her 400m hurdles semi-final on Saturday in 1:02.11 and did not reach the final, after her Israeli U18 record of 1:00.02 in the heats.
Ido Noam finished sixth in the men's 2,000m steeplechase final in 5:53.96; Aviv Ochman was 14th in 6:19.99.
The championships took place at the Stadio Raul Guidobaldi in Rieti, Italy, from 16 to 19 July 2026.
